spec_units.heading: PROP-000: Codkit foundations
Codkit is a standalone product for maintaining a structured patch set over any fork of an upstream its project type describes (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-TERM`). @status:spec/done
Independent locations
The Codkit installation contains only tool code, specifications, documentation, and tests. @status:spec/done
The managed fork tree is an external upstream checkout selected by the operator. @status:spec/done
The patch-set directory is external and owns the pin, intervention artifacts, inventory, history, and runtime state. @status:spec/done
No location is inferred from the current directory or from a neighbouring path. @status:spec/done

`toolRoot`, `patchesDir`, and `forkDir` must be pairwise disjoint: no two may be equal and none may contain another. Resolution canonicalizes existing path prefixes before enforcing this invariant. @status:spec/done
Path configuration
For both external directories the precedence is command-line flag, environment variable, then `~/.codkit/settings.json`. @status:spec/done
The fork path sources are `--fork-dir`, `CODKIT_FORK_DIR`, and `forkDir`. @status:spec/done
The patch-set path sources are `--patches-dir`, `CODKIT_PATCHES_DIR`, and `patchesDir`. @status:spec/done

The user settings file is `~/.codkit/settings.json` with strict schema `{"codkitSettings":1,"patchesDir":"/absolute/path","forkDir":"/absolute/path"}`; either path may be omitted, but unknown fields, relative paths, and unsupported schema versions are errors. @status:spec/done
Engineering posture
The AI-native TypeScript discipline applies to Codkit production code and tests. @status:spec/done
Dependencies are permissive-only unless the owner explicitly approves an exception. @status:spec/done

Tombstone (campaign STANDARDS, 2026-09-06): the proprietary posture of 2026-08-31 was cancelled by an owner decision; the anchor in force is `LICENSE-UPL` below. The address is not deleted (NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR). @status:spec/done

Codkit is released under The Universal Permissive License (UPL), Version 1.0 (SPDX `UPL-1.0`); the root `LICENSE.md` is the governing notice, the `license` field of `package.json` states the same, and the standards packages under `vibevm/vibepacks/` carry the same licence. Changing this posture is an owner decision made in one commit that updates every licence statement together. @status:spec/done
PROP-001: Codkit vision

Codkit turns a fork upgrade into a repeatable operation, for any family of upstreams a project type describes (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-TERM`): move the upstream pin, reapply a machine-readable patch set, resolve the explicit red list, verify, and regenerate. @status:spec/done
Goals
The same Codkit installation can operate on unrelated forks and unrelated patch sets, of one project type or of several. @status:spec/done
Every downstream difference has an owner, reason, intervention layer, and verification evidence. @status:spec/done
Upgrade cost is proportional to the maintained intervention inventory, not to upstream repository history. @status:spec/done

Linux, macOS, and Windows are supported targets, and offline CI is a first-class target. A target is not accepted merely because platform-neutral code exists: native execution evidence is required. @status:spec/done

Linux automation proves the currently executed host. Native macOS and Windows wrapper, filesystem, Git, and regeneration runs remain open acceptance evidence until those runners execute successfully. @status:spec/plan
Principles
The patch set is source of truth; the managed fork tree is reproducible working state. @status:spec/done
Developers edit and test in the managed tree, then use `codkit save` to extract validated changes into the patch set. @status:spec/done
Codkit prefers owned modules and declarative layers; textual patches are the last intervention layer. @status:spec/done
Upstream lines are preserved; intentional changes remain attributable and reversible. @status:spec/done
PROP-002: Standalone architecture
Three independent boundaries
The Codkit repository is the distributable tool and does not contain a consumer fork's patch artifacts or product history. @status:spec/done
The patch-set directory is a Git work tree that owns `codkit.json`, delta layers, cycle records, inventory, and review history. @status:spec/done
The managed fork tree contains the upstream history of the patch set's project type plus generated Codkit refs; direct human commits there are forbidden. @status:spec/done
Workflow

Tombstone (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE Phase 1, 2026-09-06): superseded by `FLOW-LOAD`; this anchor's address is immutable (NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR), the name `sync` is reserved for the future two-way command. @status:spec/done
`load` materializes one patch-set revision over its configured upstream pin. @status:spec/done
Implementation work and upstream-run tests happen in the managed fork tree. @status:spec/done
`save` validates and serializes tree changes back into the patch set. @status:spec/done
An upgrade cycle advances the pin and records every resolution as patch-set history. @status:spec/done
`publish <patch-set-ref>` generates downstream refs from immutable patch-set and upstream coordinates. @status:spec/done
Invariants
Each patch-set commit is self-consistent: its pin, artifacts, inventory, and checks describe one reproducible result. @status:spec/done
There is no default sibling fork or patch-set directory. @status:spec/done
The installed tool, patch-set directory, and fork directory are pairwise disjoint, including containment: a managed cleanup may never reach another root. @status:spec/done
Generated commits identify `Codkit-Patchset-Commit` and `Codkit-Upstream-Pin`. @status:spec/done
PROP-003: Codkit conventions
Identifiers
The tool is Codkit; a consumer product and its fork-specific namespace are external inputs. @status:spec/done
Intervention ids use `CK-<area>-<number>` and are unique within a patch set. @status:spec/done
The downstream-owned source directory is configured per patch set as `typeConfig.ownRoot`, inside the bounds the project type sets, and has no product-specific default. @status:spec/done
Terms
Upstream is the history consumed by a managed fork, of the family the patch set's project type describes; a pin is an exact tag and commit. @status:spec/done
A patch set is the complete machine-readable downstream delta plus its configuration, state, and inventory. @status:spec/done
A managed fork tree is the reproducible checkout to which Codkit applies a patch set. @status:spec/done
An intervention is one attributable downstream change represented by a Codkit layer. @status:spec/done
Language

The specifications of this repository - `vibevm/vibespecs/common/*` and `vibevm/vibespecs/modules/codkit/*` - are written in English: prose, decision records, acceptance scenarios, status comments and section titles alike. Identifiers, anchors, file names, command names, flags, settings, keys, error codes and code stay as they are, and a quotation from upstream, from a log or from a user-facing string keeps the language of its source. Commit messages are English as well (the attribution policy and Conventional Commits). A consumer product keeps its own rule for its own specifications and is not bound by this one. Owner ruling of 2026-09-08; the earlier Russian text of the module specifications was translated under it. @status:spec/done
Versions

**1.0.0 is the development version.** Every package this repository ships - the standards package, the agent-skills package and the runtime library - and the tool's own npm package (`package.json`, owner's word of 2026-09-09) carry version 1.0.0 and is changed in place under that number: a product takes the changed copy with `codkit standards load --upgrade` and `codkit runtime load --upgrade`, and no change bumps the number. This is how the internal packages of the package manager live during development (30 of the 31 installed here are at 1.0.0), and the owner applied the same rule to this tool and to the product on 2026-09-08. Honest re-releases - a new number for every change - return only when the owner says so explicitly; `EDITION-IS-MUTABLE-FOR-NOW` in the standards protocol and `DECISION-STD-MUTABLE-EDITION` in PROP-014 say the same for the standards edition. A version directory named after an older number is a tombstone: its content moves to `v1.0.0`, and the anchors that carried the old number stay as tombstones pointing at the new ones. @status:spec/done
History
Published patch-set history is not rewritten; generated fork refs are derived and replaceable under their guarded workflow. @status:spec/done

The current checked-out Codkit tree has zero occurrences of the retired consumer-product identifier in tracked paths or tracked content. Preserved Git object history is intentionally outside this current-tree gate. @status:spec/done
PROP-004: Clean-room development
Codkit implementation is derived from its specifications, tests, and public VS Code behavior; it does not copy implementations from unrelated fork-management tools. @status:spec/done
Rules
Do not copy source text, tests, comments, or distinctive internal structure from reference products. @status:spec/done
The selected VS Code upstream is implementation input, not a prohibited reference repository. @status:spec/done
Comparative research produces prose facts; implementation sessions consume ratified specifications. @status:spec/done
The clean-room checker and focused review verify the boundary before release. @status:spec/done

The tool repository names no consumer product built with the tool and holds none of its implementation - not in code, tests, specifications, research or design documents; a consumer product holds no implementation of the tool, only the managed copies the tool delivers (standards, runtime, skills, the licence notice). The isolation grep over the tool repository for the names of the consumer products prints zero before every commit. Owner rule of 2026-09-08/09, stated for every product alike. @status:spec/done
codkit FEAT-001: Standalone integration polygon
1. Boundary and purpose

The polygon is an external patch-set repository plus an external managed VS Code checkout operated by the installed Codkit tool. It is test data, not a consumer product and not content owned by toolRoot. @status:spec/done
toolRoot, polygon patchesDir, and polygon forkDir use unrelated, pairwise-disjoint paths; the run starts from a cwd outside all three. @status:spec/done

At least one full run selects both external roots only through a temporary HOME containing strict `~/.codkit/settings.json`; separate runs prove each CLI and environment override independently. @status:spec/done
The patch-set describes only its selected fork/pin. No path, identifier, service, feature, or branding from another consumer is required. @status:spec/done
2. Minimal layer samples

Each sample is authored in forkDir, extracted or declared in patchesDir, verified, synchronized again from the pin, and inspected through schema-2 inventory/effective diff. Sample ids use a reserved test range in that patch-set. @status:spec/done

Inventory has at least one entry for every intervention layer, all ids and owners are unique/known, every required guard is declared, and completeness explains every generated fork path exactly once. @status:spec/plan
3. Upgrade-cycle proof
Prepare a branch on an older reachable VS Code pin with a clean, a renamed, and a deliberately conflicting intervention. @status:spec/plan

Run forecast, cycle start/continue/status, rename handling, classified full red list, required resolution stop, journal completeness, regeneration and final verify on the target pin. @status:spec/plan
Inject interruption at each durable phase boundary and prove a fresh process continues without lost work or duplicate canonical commits. @status:spec/plan
Record the final inventory metrics snapshot in the committed cycle journal; no tool-repository metrics file is required. @status:spec/plan
4. Environment matrix
Run verify and, with supplied dependencies, build in a container with physical `--network none`; any attempted network operation is a failure. @status:spec/plan
Exercise foreign UID/safe.directory and read-only mounts: read-only commands work, writes fail before partial mutation, and writable runtime mounts are explicit. @status:spec/plan
Run the selected full upstream/Electron runner baseline, not only focused own tests, and preserve its complete red list as evidence. @status:spec/plan
Build/package a distributable bundle and inspect that own, overlay, resource and generated metadata are present in final artifacts, not merely in the development checkout. @status:spec/plan
Execute the same fixture natively on macOS and Windows, including launchers, Git/path semantics, double regeneration and daemon lifecycle. Linux evidence does not close these rows. @status:spec/plan
5. Acceptance

The polygon is accepted only when every sample, upgrade/resume proof, air-gap/UID/read-only proof, upstream baseline, packaging proof and native OS row has recorded executable evidence. A missing runner is an explicit open risk, never an implied pass. @status:spec/plan
6. The second polygon - synthetic and typeless

FEAT-001 becomes **two** polygons (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-ENGINE-TESTS`). The first is the one described in §§1-5: a real fork tree of a `vscode` patch set. The second is the polygon of the `generic` type and is a **synthetic repository in the fixtures** (owner ruling of 2026-09-09) - a small git upstream generated by code, with two pins, no product manifest, no extensions, no service registry and no entry module; its install, lint, compile and test commands are stub scripts declared in `typeConfig`. It costs no external checkout, it runs in the tool's own CI, and it is the standing proof that the engine works without a product model. @status:spec/plan

What the synthetic polygon must carry: the layers a typeless upstream can have - `own` in a configured directory, `patch` with markers, `resource-file`, `rewrite-rule` and a `config-overlay` over a declared JSON target with no dev channel; the verbs `load`, `save`, `verify`, `cycle`, `publish` against a local bare remote and `ci --profile verify`; and the capability refusals of the verbs the type does not answer (`imageset`, `gen brand`, `build`, `runtime load`), each `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`. What it deliberately does not carry: brand images, a runtime library, built-in extensions and any upstream-specific build - those are proved on the first polygon alone. @status:spec/plan
codkit FEAT-002: End-to-end acceptance scenarios S01–S28 (Given/When/Then)
0. Notation

`$TOOL`, `$PATCHES`, `$FORK` are three unrelated disjoint roots; the cwd is in a fourth place. A clean fork is a checkout of the upstream pin without local edits. A Then over the output is checked through the schema-2 `roots.tool|patches|fork`; the exceptions are explicit human-message checks. The codes are 0/1/2/3 from PROP-007. @status:spec/done

The scenarios are a permanent acceptance contract and do not depend on a removed campaign or on a consumer product. A particular execution plan may group them however it likes, but it cancels no Then. @status:spec/done
S01 — load with a provided tree

**Given**: `$TOOL`, a clean fork at the configured pin in `$FORK`, the FEAT-001 patch set in `$PATCHES`; both external roots are selected by env. **When**: `$TOOL/bin/codkit --json load`. **Then**: exit 0; `roots.tool.source=install`, `roots.patches={path:$PATCHES,source:env}`, `roots.fork={path:$FORK,source:env}`; generated branch is current and clean; ownDir is materialized/excluded; fork mark and `$PATCHES/.codkit/trees/<id>.json` agree. @status:spec/plan
S02 — cloning into an empty directory (locally) and the ban in CI

**Given**: `$FORK` does not exist; `--from <local-bare-mirror-repository>` is given. **When**: `codkit clone --from …`; then again; then `codkit clone --ci`. **Then**: the first run — exit 0, the tree is at the pin, `check-tree` passes; the repeat — exit 0, the output contains `already present`, no changes; with `--ci` — exit 2, the error `CK-E-NET-FORBIDDEN`. @status:spec/plan
S03 — an idempotent repeat of load

**Given**: the state after S01. **When**: `codkit load` again; timing and an mtime snapshot of every `src/vs/workbench/**` file before/after. **Then**: exit 0; the output contains `up to date`; not one mtime changed; the time is a fast no-op (< 5 s on the polygon). @status:spec/plan
S04 — an edit → save → a patch with markers

**Given**: S01; a `CK-workbench-905` marker block was added by hand in `$FORK/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/titlebar/titlebarPart.ts` through `marker new`, then one functional line. **When**: `codkit save --commit`. **Then**: exit 0; `.ckpatch` appears only under `$PATCHES/delta/patches/`; all additions marker-scoped; `$FORK` clean; patch-set commit touches only its delta; repeat save is byte/mtime no-op. @status:spec/plan
S05 — the guard catches unextracted work

**Given**: S01; an unmarked edit in any upstream file of the tree (one line). **When**: `codkit load`. **Then**: exit 1; the error `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` with a list of one file; the hint contains `codkit save`; the tree is unchanged (the edit stays in place, the branch is not regenerated). @status:spec/plan
S06 — an edit outside the markers is rejected by save and caught by verify/pre-commit

**Given**: S01; a line was added to an upstream file **outside** the marker blocks. **When**: (a) `codkit save`; (b) a patch with such a line is forged by hand in `delta/patches/…` and `codkit verify` is run; (c) the same forged patch staged, and the patchset `pre-commit` git hook. **Then**: (a) exit 1, `CK-E-HUNK-OUTSIDE-MARKER` with the file and the line, no patch written; (b) exit 1 with the same code; (c) the commit is rejected by the hook with the same code; the hook's run time on one file is fractions of a second. @status:spec/plan
S07 — the inventory and its diff

**Given**: the whole level-A polygon (PG-01…PG-09); the patchset branch `feature/x`, which adds one more marker intervention. **When**: `codkit inventory` on `feature/x`; `codkit inventory --diff main`. **Then**: exit 0; `.codkit/out/inventory.json` is valid against the schema of PROP-006 §3; entries hold ≥1 record of every layer (`own`, `service-override`, `entry-module`, `config-overlay`, `resource-file`, `rewrite-rule`, `patch`); the metrics are filled in; the diff shows exactly one added record with the id of the new intervention; generation takes seconds. @status:spec/plan
Standalone acceptance records a fresh inventory result from the external polygon. Historical results from a removed consumer tree do not satisfy this scenario. @status:spec/plan
S08 — an upgrade without conflicts: canonical commits, a green clean pin

**Given**: the polygon branch `codkit/playground-134` (pin `1.134.0`) with the PG-01 intervention (the title bar; upstream did not change the file within the window) — without PG-C1 and PG-R1. **When**: `codkit cycle start 1.135.0`; then `codkit cycle continue` up to `done`; then `codkit ci --profile verify` on the result. **Then**: `start` — exit 0 or a move to advisory (exit 3 only on a non-empty advisory; for the polygon the toolchain diff is non-empty → one advisory stop is allowed, followed by `continue`); the outcome: `cycle status` — `phase: done`; the history of the cycle branch holds the canonical commits `bump pin` and `regeneration`, each with the trailer `Codkit-Cycle: 1.135.0`; `codkit.json` carries the new pin; `ci --profile verify` — exit 0 ("the delta lands on a clean pin"). @status:spec/plan
S09 — an upgrade with a rename: carrying the artifact over

**Given**: `codkit/playground-134` with PG-R1 — the marker intervention `CK-platform-902` in `remoteAgentHostProtocolClient.ts` (upstream renamed the file to `agentHostProtocolClient.ts` between `1.134.0` and `1.135.0`, R096). **When**: `codkit cycle start 1.135.0` → `continue` up to the apply. **Then**: the rename step reports the pair with similarity ≥ 90; the patch file in patchset is renamed after the encoding of the new path, the `---`/`+++` headers name the new path; the carried-over patch is applied on trial (the outcome `clean|shifted|merged` in the report: the rename is a separate lifecycle fact, while the changes of the other R096 lines honestly give a 3-way `merged` even with our hook stable); the record of the carry-over is in `cycle/state.json.renames` and in the journal; a separate canonical `renames` commit exists. @status:spec/plan
S10 — an upgrade with a conflict: the stop, the classification, the journal, the continuation

**Given**: `codkit/playground-134` with PG-C1 (a hook in the constructor of `activitybarPart.ts` — upstream added a 7th DI parameter in the `1.134→1.135` window). **When**: `codkit cycle start 1.135.0`. **Then**: exit 3; the report classifies PG-C1 as `conflict`, groups by cause (the SHA of the upstream commit; the field `approx` is allowed), names the owner from the inventory; the file in the tree holds the standard conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`/`|||||||`/`>>>>>>>`). **When (continued)**: the conflict is resolved by an edit in the tree; a record is added to `cycle/log/1.135.0.jsonl`; `codkit cycle continue`. **Then**: the phase moves past `resolve`; the fix commit carries the trailer `Cause: <sha>`; an attempt to `continue` into `done` **without** the journal record — exit 1 `CK-E-LOG-INCOMPLETE`. @status:spec/plan
S11 — upstream renamed a CSS class: the contract test is red, the message is clear

**Given**: PG-04 (the contract test `patchset.contract.statusbar-class` over an upstream CSS class); a simulated drift: the class is renamed in the tree (the mechanics of the simulation — PROP-013 §4). **When**: a run of the contract tests (as part of `ci --profile build` or addressed directly by the runner). **Then**: the test is red; the failure text holds the id `patchset.contract.statusbar-class`, the name of the expected class and the hint "upstream contract drifted; find cause and update intervention `CK-workbench-905`" (the id of the linked intervention from the inventory). @status:spec/plan
S12 — the R2b race: pin-guard catches a PR with an old pin

**Given**: the patchset branch `feature/old-pin`, created before the upgrade (its `codkit.json` — pin `1.134.0`); main is already on `1.135.0`. **When**: `codkit ci --profile verify` on the merge result of the PR (the job emulated: base=main). **Then**: exit 1; a pin-guard error with the text "branch pin 1.134.0 != target branch pin 1.135.0"; the hint holds `codkit rebase-onto-pin`. **When (the cure)**: merge main + `codkit rebase-onto-pin` are run on the branch (+ the resolve, `codkit save`). **Then**: a repeated `ci --profile verify` — exit 0. @status:spec/plan
S13 — an agent resolve: a journal without commits

**Given**: S10 stopped at exit 3; an agent following FEAT-004 edits `$FORK` and appends its result under `$PATCHES`, without commits. **When**: inspect both Git histories, then `cycle continue`. **Then**: no agent-created commits exist; Codkit validates/extracts and creates the canonical fix commit; the agent journal attribution is preserved. @status:spec/plan
S14 — air-gapped: a full run without the network

**Given**: the container of PROP-011 §8, started with `--network none`; the tree is provided by a bind mount at a non-standard path; pre-filled `node_modules`/`.build` (for the build profile). **When**: `codkit ci --profile verify`; then `codkit ci --profile build`. **Then**: both — exit 0; the output holds not one attempt at a network call (the measurement method — PROP-013 §6); an unreachable pin (a variant: a tree with a truncated history) — exit 2 `CK-E-PIN-UNREACHABLE` with the exact fetch command in the hint, without an attempt at the network. @status:spec/plan
S15 — the tree is swapped under a live cache

**Given**: S01 cache/mark exist; a different clean checkout replaces `$FORK` at the same path. **When**: `codkit load`. **Then**: exit 0 but not `up to date`; the actual fork cannot validate the stale cache, so the patch-set is reapplied and cache/mark are rewritten. @status:spec/plan
S16 — a double regeneration: an empty diff (three OSes)

**Given**: the same non-empty fixture on native Linux, macOS and Windows runners. **When**: save → snapshot patch bytes/tip → restore → repeat identical edit → save. **Then**: each native run produces identical patch bytes and generated tip for the same patch-set/pin. Current Linux evidence closes only Linux; macOS/Windows remain open until actually executed. @status:spec/plan
S17 — commits in the fork tree: save extracts them into patchset

**Given**: the state of S01; two manual commits were made in `$FORK` on the generated branch (`--no-verify` or `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1`; campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decisions D3/D4/D5/D6). **When**: `codkit save`; then `codkit save` again; then `codkit load`. **Then (a)**: the first — exit 0; the patch artifacts hold the lines of both commits; `refs/codkit/consumed/*` points at the former HEAD of the tree; patchset gains one new commit per tree commit — with the original subject/author/date and the trailer `Codkit-Tree-Commit` on its own sha; the tree is clean, HEAD is on the generated branch; the repeated save — "nothing to save"; `load` — "up to date". An addressed `save <path>` while commits foreign to that path exist: the branch is untouched, the commits stay in place, `info` "N tree commit(s) stay in the tree until a full save". **(b, Phase 4)**: three commits of three authors → three patchset commits with the same subject/author/date, one trailer each; the uncommitted remainder is in the patchset working tree, uncommitted; `--commit --message` adds a fourth commit (the remainder, with the given message, without a trailer); `--squash` — one commit `codkit save: squash of 3 tree commit(s)` with three trailers and the list; `git show <patchset commit>:delta/patches/…`, applied over the pin, reproduces byte for byte the file of the corresponding tree commit — the proof that the history was replayed, not only the number of commits; idempotence — through the test seam `replayCheckpoint` (a hard exit after the first state commit): the repeated save skips the replayed commit (its trailer is already in history), replays the rest, and does not duplicate; an empty state (an empty tree commit) is skipped with a visible message; a malformed `Cause:` in the message of a tree commit — blocked, exit 1, nothing written; `--squash` without tree commits — a no-op with a message. **(c, Phase 4)**: an intermediate commit with an edit outside a marker — the refusal `CK-E-HUNK-OUTSIDE-MARKER` with the sha/subject of that commit, patchset without new commits or artifacts, the tree untouched; the variant "the violation is hidden by a later commit" (the final state is clean) refuses with the same code — the state-by-state validation of pass 1 (P4). @status:spec/plan
S18 — commits in the fork tree: the guard and the status

**Given**: the state of S01; two manual commits were made in `$FORK` on the generated branch (`--no-verify` or `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1` — bypassing the hook is trivial, the guard must see the result; campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decisions D7/D8). **When**: `codkit load`; `codkit ci --profile verify`; `codkit status`; `codkit load --fresh`. **Then**: `load` — exit 1 `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` with the text "2 commit(s) in the fork tree since the last codkit apply are not in patchset yet"; HEAD, the working files and the status of the tree are untouched, both commits are ancestors of HEAD; `ci --profile verify` — the same refusal; `status` — exit 1 with `treeCommits.count = 2` and without the line `reload needed`; `--fresh` does not lift the refusal. The extraction of this work is scenario S17. A separate case `CK-E-TREE-HEAD`: the branch exists, HEAD is off it and carries foreign work — `load` and `save` refuse with the recipe for returning (`git switch <branch>`). @status:spec/plan
S19 — half-committed work: save extracts both halves

**Given**: the state of S01; half the work is committed in the tree (a manual commit with an edit inside a marker block), half is left uncommitted (an edit in the block of another file). **When**: `codkit save`. **Then**: exit 0; both halves reach their artifacts; the file that carried the committed line still carries it (the rebuild replays the state of the commit instead of overwriting it — the counterexample to the F9 loss path); the tree is clean; the consumed commit is reachable through `refs/codkit/consumed/*` and is named by the `Codkit-Tree-Commit` trailer of the single new patchset commit. @status:spec/plan
S20 — the tree hook reminds about save instead of refusing

**Given**: the state of S01 — HEAD on the generated branch, the hook installed by the latest `load` (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decision D9; the norm PROP-012 §5 `##FORK-TREE-PRECOMMIT-HOOK`). **When**: a manual `git commit` on the branch; then on a detached HEAD; then with `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1`. **Then**: all three — exit 0: the hook never rejects a commit. On the branch stderr holds "this commit is work in the fork tree" and "codkit save or codkit sync"; on a detached HEAD — "HEAD is not on codkit/applied/<tag>" and "git switch codkit/applied/<tag>" with the concrete tag of the tree; with `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1` — not one `codkit:` line. A linked worktree has no hook (the S0 level: the warning `CK-W-MARK-RO`), there the norm is held by the refusal of `load`/`save` — S18. @status:spec/plan
S21 — the former name sync: the tombstone of the stub

A tombstone (Phase 8 of the campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, 2026-09-06). Since Phase 1 this scenario asserted (decision D14): `codkit sync` (and `codkit --json sync`) is a stub with exit 2, stderr "codkit sync was renamed to codkit load; the name sync is reserved for the two-way save+load command", without an envelope; an alias was rejected so that scripts carrying the old meaning break loudly. Phase 8 (decision D15) executed the reservation: the name is carried by the real two-way command, and the assertion about the stub stopped being true by construction. The live contract is `CMD-SYNC-TWO-WAY` (PROP-007 §5), the acceptance scenarios are S24 and S25 below; the crash atoms are PROP-013 §5 `##SYNC-CRASH-TESTS`. The anchor itself is neither renamed nor deleted (NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR): the address Phase 1–7 cited is unchanged. @status:spec/plan
S22 — an artifact moved in patchset: save refuses before the first write, the recipe works by hand

codkit FEAT-003: Requirements for the human working protocol

The protocol (`docs/codkit/protocol/human/*`) is written **after the first manual upgrade cycle on the polygon**: the cycle procedures describe the process that was carried out, not an imaginary one. The protocol does not invent the process — it states a procedure a human can execute on top of the decisions already taken: every requirement refers to a spec and/or a codkit command instead of retelling their behavior. @status:spec/done

After the accepted `1.134.0→1.135.0` cycle, `docs/codkit/protocol/human/00-index.md`…`12-maintenance.md`, four shared templates and an executable checker of links, anchors and line caps are implemented. Field tests on new people and the owner-only organizational decisions stay explicitly open and are not marked green. @status:impl/done
1. Quality bar (normative for the whole protocol)

**Procedures** are numbered steps: the exact codkit command → the expected result (what is printed, the exit code) → the next step; branching happens only on an observable sign («exit 1 and the code `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` → step 4»), never an «act as the situation demands» without a criterion. @status:spec/done

**Decision trees** have explicit branches and terminal outcomes; every leaf names a layer, a command or an escalation. **Checklists** consist of checkable items (the «yes/no» answer is established by a command or by a look at a concrete output). @status:spec/done

**The mechanization rule**: everything a text warns about («do not forget to…») is in fact done by a command, a hook or CI — the protocol refers to the mechanism; a text warning without a mechanism is a defect of the protocol, and a task for the mechanism is opened. @status:spec/done

The terms follow `common/PROP-003`; one point of definition, everything else refers to it. The language is Russian; the commands and identifiers are English. The clean room is `common/PROP-004`. @status:spec/done

A self-check of every section before acceptance: «will a person doing this for the first time be able to carry the procedure out without taking a single uncovered decision?» — plus a field test for the key documents (§4). @status:spec/done
2. Layout, audiences, sizes

The audiences: the ordinary developer (hundreds of them; some touch upstream files once a quarter) reads 01 and 02 as a duty and 03/04 as needed; the intervention reviewer — 03, 10 (+11); the upgrade team and the DRI — 05, 06, 07, 09, 10 (+08, 11); the release engineer — 08, 10; the protocol maintainer — 12 and everything else. @status:spec/done

The size guidelines are a hard upper bound of acceptance (lines): 01 ≤ 150; 02 ≤ 250; 03 ≤ 350; 04 ≤ 200; 05 ≤ 500; 06 ≤ 120; 07 ≤ 200; 08 ≤ 300; 09 ≤ 250; 10 ≤ 200; 11 ≤ 150; 12 ≤ 100. The brevity follows from the rule «refer to the mechanism instead of retelling it». @status:spec/done
3. The executable against the text (a mandatory table of 00-index)
The criterion: the protocol contains not a single «do not forget» that is not backed by a row of this table. @status:spec/done
4. Requirements for the sections (goal / content / acceptance)

**10-roles** — the table of roles: the DRI / merge captain of the cycle (appointed per cycle; rights: the cycle branch, running `cycle`, merging), the subsystem owners (the keys of `delta/owners.json` ↔ the inventory; they must react to the addressed notifications of the forecast and to the red list within a working day — a weekly cadence does not tolerate week-long pauses), the intervention reviewers (the right to approve a descent down the hierarchy of layers), the release engineer (`publish`, the supply kit), the upstream watcher, the protocol maintainer. For every role: the duties, the inputs and outputs, the SLA; and the procedure «a rehearsal on draft branches before the first real cycle». Acceptance: for every artifact of the process (a PR, the red list, the journal, a release) the responsible person is defined unambiguously; there is no action without a role. @status:spec/done

**02-daily** — the formula of the day (word for word in meaning): **the history, the branches and the PRs live in the patch set; editing happens in the fork tree**. The loop: `codkit load` (on a `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` refusal — `codkit save` first) → an edit in the tree (own code in `src/vs/patchset/**`; upstream files only through 03) → `codkit status` → `codkit save [--commit]` → a commit/PR in the patch set. Plus: how to obtain the tree locally (the resolver, `clone`, `check-tree`); building and running (`build up` → `build errors` once, the output in full; the run is `scripts/code.sh` from the tree; the prohibitions: a direct tsc, `npm run compile` while the daemons are alive, `npm install` without stopping the daemons); what is forbidden in the tree; a multi-root IDE and which Git panel shows what; the PR checklist. Acceptance: after 01 a newcomer carries out the full loop «an own edit + an edit of an upstream file → a PR» on the polygon without questions (a field test on two people who did not take part in the development). @status:spec/done

**01-quickstart** — within 1 hour: half a page of «how it is built» (the two repositories; the patches as the truth; the picture «patchset → load → tree → save → patchset»); three commands with examples of their output; the «five prohibitions» (a commit into the tree; an edit outside a marker; deletion of upstream lines; a direct compiler; a hand edit of `product.json`); five training assignments on the polygon with a self-check: (a) `load` + running the product; (b) an own edit → `save` → see the diff in the patch set; (c) `marker new` → an edit of an upstream file → `save` → find your own patch and the inventory entry; (d) an edit outside a marker on purpose → read the `save` refusal; (e) a `load` with unextracted work on purpose → read the refusal of the guard. Acceptance: two people «off the street» get through it in ≤ 1 hour. @status:spec/done

**03-interventions** — the layer decision tree (the terminal leaves are a layer + a command): «can it be expressed by own code?» → own; «replace the behavior of a service?» → service-override (check `forbiddenServiceIds`); «remove something upstream?» → hide + a guard test; «JSON without comments?» → config-overlay; «a binary?» → resource-file + a guard; «a uniform mass edit?» → rewrite-rule (agree it with the upgrade team); otherwise → a patch with a marker, and a justification in the PR is mandatory. How to shape a marker (ASCII; the hook goes into `create*`, not into the constructor; DI through an accessor; the logic lives in own; upstream lines are commented out). The intervention review: the questions of the hierarchy; a check of the metadata; the diff of the inventory and the «effective diff» are the subject of the review, the patch files are not; the intervention budget of a subsystem (the thresholds are an open question, §6). De-intrusion iterations: a periodic pass over the patch and rule entries of a subsystem — what to lift into an upper layer, what to upstream as a seam. Acceptance: on five training cases three different people arrive at the same leaf of the tree; the reviewer's checklist covers every check of `verify` without duplicating them in text. @status:spec/done

**04-team** — procedures by race scenarios (symptom → diagnosis → steps): R1 — a Git conflict on a patch file while merging main: take the version of main → `codkit load` → `codkit reresolve <file>` → `codkit save`; R2b — a red pin guard: merge main → `codkit rebase-onto-pin` → resolve → `save` → push; R4 — a `load` refusal with unextracted work; switching branches: `git switch` → `codkit load` (mandatory, under the guard); `CK-E-LOCKED` — wait for or check somebody else's process. Explicitly: files that do not overlap require no coordination at all. Acceptance: scenario S12 and the R1 case can be walked through from the text of the document by a person who has not seen the architecture specs. @status:spec/done

**05-upgrade-cycle** — the DRI runbook: the cadence (weekly; the pin moves only on a green CI; batching is an exception of ≤ 2 tags by a DRI decision); a step-by-step runbook over the phases of `codkit cycle` — for every phase the command, the expected output and code (0/1/3), the control points; the table of outcome classes with the action for each one (shifted/merged — the machine; conflict — a resolution in the tree; target-deleted — an owner decision, and abandoning the intervention = a separate commit that deletes the artifact with an explanation; target-renamed — a check of the automatic port; rule-broken — a repair of the rule; contract-failed — semantic drift, an analysis of the cause; the class «divergence of two upstream branches» is absent from the patch model — this is recorded explicitly); the escalation of design decisions (the signs → a stop, an issue, an owner decision, an entry in the journal); the journal and the retrospective with the metrics; the light procedure of a minor security bump; the templates of the cycle issue and PR. Acceptance: a maintainer who did not take part in the development of codkit walks the polygon cycle `1.134.0→1.135.0` (S08–S10) through from the document alone; every stopping point is recognized; the journal is complete. @status:spec/done

**06-history** — the canonical set of the cycle commits and the «do not squash» rule (the cost metric lives in the history); the hook puts the trailers in and CI checks them (the text only explains what for); the authorship of the generated tree commits is a technical author, and their SHAs go into the file of revisions ignored by blame; the history of the patch set is not rewritten; LF/`core.autocrlf=false`/`core.longpaths=true`. Acceptance: three questions are answered from the document without reading the architecture specs: «why the cycle branch cannot be squash-merged», «where Cause comes from», «what blame is to do in the tree». @status:spec/done

**07-upstream-watch** — the role of the watcher (who reads the iteration plans and the release notes of the VS Code team, and where the digest is written); how to read the `codkit forecast` report (a nightly job; addressed notifications to the owners), when to start the adaptation before a release (a conflict class in the forecast → the adaptation does not wait for the cycle); the policy «upstream the seams, not the features»: the criteria of a candidate (a patch that has survived ≥ 2 adaptations; a seam that removes a patch for good), the process of a PR into `microsoft/vscode` (minimal, without our functionality, motivated by extensibility), and the bookkeeping: the patch stays until acceptance and after it the artifact is deleted by a separate commit. Acceptance: from a forecast report with one red intervention an owner determines their actions for the week without questions. @status:spec/done

**08-release-ci** — the versioning scheme (the patch set has a version of its own, the pin is a machine field; the exact scheme follows the status of the open choice in PROP-012 §5); `codkit publish` — who (the publish bot only), when, idempotency; air gapped is the main mode: four ways to obtain the tree in CI with the recipes from `docs/codkit/ci-examples/`; the zones of responsibility (the image, the caches — a single writer, the supply kit — who refreshes it on an advisory); the verify/build profiles; what to do on a cold build. Acceptance: a customer's engineer brings a `verify` job up on their own CI from the document and the ci-examples alone (a field test on a «foreign» runner). @status:spec/done

**09-incidents** — «symptom → steps» procedures with a completion criterion: (a) upstream broke a critical seam (the contract test of the seam is red / the forecast is on fire): an assessment through the cause → an owner decision (rework the intervention / a temporary rollback onto the old pin) → an issue to upstream if needed; (b) a rollback of the cycle: before the merge — `cycle restart`; after the merge — revert commits of the cycle branch (the history is not rewritten) plus a return of the pin in the same canonical format; (c) a hotfix on top of an old pin: a branch from the last release commit of the patch set → an edit under the usual discipline → `publish` with a release tag (the self-consistency invariant makes this a routine); (d) a fast port of an upstream security fix without a full bump: a marker or add-file patch with a cause; it is removed automatically at the next cycle (a regeneration against the new pin, which already carries the fix — «the patch became empty → delete it»). Acceptance: a tabletop game over every scenario on the polygon, with the time recorded. @status:spec/done

**11-metrics** — which series are written (`inventory-history.csv`): the number of interventions by layer and by subsystem (the target trend falls for the rule and patch layers), the hours per cycle, the time «a VS Code release → our release», the conflicts per cycle, the share of resolutions done by agents, the coverage by contract tests; how to read them (the trend, not the absolute value — the baseline comes from the first cycle); the threshold alerts (the values are an open question, §6); who looks at them and when. A dashboard comes later; until then — a table in the retrospective. Acceptance: from the CSV of two training cycles a person builds the conclusions of the retrospective by the template. @status:spec/done

**12-maintenance** — the shared protocol is versioned with toolRoot; a patch set keeps only its own owners, journal and intervention evidence. The shipped `toolRoot/config/conventions.json` is the base machine source; an explicit additive extension in patchesDir adds to it per PROP-003 and never weakens it. Agent and human documents refer to the effective policy; the docs gate checks the paths, the commands and the schema-2 roots. @status:spec/done

No separate section about product work is created: work on the features of the product follows the same discipline of layers, markers and review — `00-index.md` carries one paragraph with this norm and a reference to 03. @status:spec/done
5. The order of writing and acceptance

It is written after the first manual polygon cycle: 05 first (while the traces of the cycle are fresh), then 02/03/04 (following the traces of filling the polygon), then the rest; 01 comes last (the digest). @status:spec/done
The field tests of acceptance (02, 01, 05, 08) are mandatory and are part of the criterion of milestone M3. @status:spec/done
The `templates/` are created together with the document that uses them. Before the commit of every document — the clean-room check and the self-check of §1. @status:spec/done
6. Open questions (recommendation + status)

**The rotation of the DRI**: the term and the order are not decided. Recommendation: a DRI for one cycle, rotation around the upgrade team, and the new DRI assists the previous one for one cycle. **Requires an owner decision** (organizational). @status:spec/plan

**The numeric intervention budgets and the threshold alerts**: no values are assigned before the baseline exists. Recommendation: after two cycles the budget = the current value for the subsystem, and the alert is any growth of the rule and patch layers two cycles in a row. Decided by the subsystem owners + the DRI; recorded in 11-metrics. @status:spec/plan
**The period of de-intrusion iterations**: the recommendation is every fourth cycle; decided together with the budgets. @status:spec/plan

**The cadence** is decided (weekly) — the protocol does not discuss it, it only executes it; the batching parameter is «no more than two tags, only by a DRI decision» and is recorded in 05. @status:spec/done

**The boundaries of agent rights** are the subject of FEAT-004; the human protocol only refers to the journal of agent decisions and to the role of the reviewer of agent resolutions. @status:spec/done

**The pre-commit hook in the fork tree** — the open choice was closed by an owner decision of 2026-08-31: every `load` tries to restore the owned hook, but the guard counts as active only when Git demonstrably executes its exact current bytes. In an ordinary checkout a manual commit is rejected and the internal path is separated by `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1`; a linked worktree, a custom/global/system `core.hooksPath`, `/dev/null`, a foreign hook or an unresolvable effective path give an explicit warning/false, without a promise of blocking (PROP-012 §5). @status:impl/done
codkit FEAT-004: Requirements for the AI-agent working protocol

The requirements for the agent protocol: instructions, rules, skills, subagent definitions, hooks, journals and evals with which agents (Claude Code and compatible tools that read `AGENTS.md`) work with a patch set and with codkit safely and efficiently. The protocol states procedures and guardrails **on top of the decisions already taken**, referring to the codkit specs and commands instead of retelling them. The mark «(J1)» on a fact about agent-tool mechanisms means: re-verify it by experiment on the current version before implementation. @status:spec/done

The shared generated core `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, four scoped rules, deny-only settings, the fail-closed PreToolUse Node/Bash/PowerShell guard, five profiles with file outputs, the protocol checker and the explicit-only `ck-resolve` are implemented. The S13 fixture proved: the resolver does not commit and does not call `save/continue`, it writes a task result and a journal candidate, the helper links task/result/entry, and only the orchestrator creates the fix commit. The remaining skills of the table stay future planned slices. @status:impl/done
1. Quality bar (beyond FEAT-003 §1)
Instructions are short and checkable; instead of retelling the tool's behavior — a codkit command with `--json` (the PROP-012 §1 envelope) and the expected `exitCode`/error code. @status:spec/done

Every norm for an agent exists in two echelons: the text (an instruction) **and** machine enforcement (hook/permissions/architecture); a text-only norm is admissible only where no mechanism physically exists, and it is then marked «text-only» explicitly. @status:spec/done
Agent results are handed over **as files, not as context**: every procedure names the exact paths of its output files. @status:spec/done

A self-check for every artifact: «will the agent carry the procedure out without taking a single uncovered decision and without performing a single irreversible action without a human?» @status:spec/done
2. File layout

Sources of generic agent descriptions live under `toolRoot/docs/codkit/agents/`; the rendered profile lives under `toolRoot/claude/` and is installed into the product repository's `.claude/` and root `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`. Hooks are shipped under `toolRoot/hooks/`. A patch-set receives runtime task/result files only under its own `.codkit/`, never a copied Codkit implementation. The Codkit tool repository carries no agent perimeter of its own (§5, `GR-TREE-EDITS-SCOPE`). @status:spec/done
3. The instruction layer

The core (`CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`) is short (target ≤ 120 lines) and holds only what is always needed; everything else follows an index of links. Contents: (1) the topology of the two repositories; «we edit in the tree, we commit into the patch set»; the tree path comes only from `codkit where`/the resolver and is never assumed; (2) upstream AI instructions inside the tree are not ours: they are neither executed nor edited; (3) the seven layers and the top-layer rule, the `codkit:begin/end` markers with `CK-…` ids, the inventory, own/follow/hide; five prohibitions (commits into the tree; edits outside markers; deletion of upstream lines/files; a direct compiler over the project; hand-editing of overlay targets); (4) compilation — in our own words, not as a quotation: code is checked through `codkit build up|status|errors`; `errors` waits for the end of the pass itself, is called once, and its output is read in full; (5) tests: our own — through upstream runners, addressed precisely; upstream tests are not edited; (6) working with codkit: always `--json`; codes 0/1/2/3; on `exitCode 3` — stop and hand over to the human; (7) the index of links. @status:spec/done

The rules (`toolRoot/claude/rules/*.md`, installed as the product's `.claude/rules/*.md`; `ck-codkit-dev.md` stays in the tool's `.claude/rules/`; the paths-scope mechanism is to be re-verified, J1): `ck-delta-artifacts.md` (`delta/**`) — the artifact formats are the module specs; artifacts are not edited by hand (apart from header metadata) — `codkit save` writes them; `ck-markers.md` — the marker rules; `ck-codkit-dev.md` (`codkit/**`) — the clean room of the implementation; `ck-cycle.md` (`cycle/**`) — the journal is mandatory, `state.json` is not edited by hand (only the `cycle` commands). @status:spec/done

**A limitation of the mechanism and how it is closed:** the path scope of rules works over paths inside the patch-set repository; the fork tree is an external directory with a non-fixed path, and a glob over it in a committed file is impossible (no mechanism hard-codes the path). Norms about editing tree files therefore live in the core and are enforced by hooks (§5), which obtain the tree path dynamically through `codkit where --json` — the single resolver. This decision is recorded in the protocol explicitly. @status:spec/done
4. Skills and subagents

Common requirements for every SKILL.md: the frontmatter `name`, `description`, `allowed-tools` (an allowlist); the body — the goal, the inputs (codkit `--json` commands), a numbered procedure, the outputs (files), the prohibitions, the completion criteria, the behavior under uncertainty (the default rule: **uncertainty = a stop with the state written into the journal**, not a guess). The ban on invoking an expensive skill on the agent's own initiative has two layers of defence: (a) the `description` is worded «only on an explicit request»; (b) expensive actions inside the skill run into permissions/hooks (J1). @status:spec/done

**`ck-resolve`** — the procedure by outcome classes: clean/shifted — nothing (the machine); conflict — a resolution in the tree file with the standard markers, **preserving our marker blocks and their ids**; target-deleted — a stop (an owner decision); target-renamed — a check of the automatic port; rule-broken — a repair of `ops`/`expectedMatches` with a justification; contract-failed — analysis through `ck-find-cause` and a stop if the intervention has to be reworked. Prohibitions: do not commit; do not widen the edit beyond the conflicting files; a design decision is a stop with a templated entry. The completion criterion: a journal entry for every non-clean artifact; `cycle continue` is started by the human or the orchestrator. @status:spec/done
**`ck-verify-report`** — a fixed order of checks and the «single call rule» for `build errors`; the report must contain the full red list, not «there are errors». @status:spec/done
**`ck-commit-conventions`** — does not write the trailers by hand: it checks that the hook is installed (`hooks check`) and shapes the messages by the canon of the cycle. @status:spec/done

The order of writing: `ck-resolve` and `ck-cycle-run` — **only after the first manual cycle** (otherwise they describe an imaginary process). For every skill — a test scenario on a fixture (§8): the pair «input → expected output files». @status:spec/done

Running in parallel is allowed: the verifier together with the reviewer; several cause-finders over independent refusals; the resolver — one per subsystem, never two on one file (the codkit lock is a single one anyway). Context is not passed between agents — only the task and journal files (their paths are fixed in §6). @status:spec/done
5. Guardrails — the two echelons plus the architectural one

**Decision (2026-09-05):** the agent perimeter binds product and fork sessions only; the tool repository is worked freely. **Why:** the owner ruled that Codkit is not used to develop Codkit, so a «codkit session» in the tool repository has no meaning; with the hook installed there, a tool-repository session could neither edit `codkit/**` nor run its own floor, because every Edit/Write and Bash call was denied before evaluation whenever fork/patches roots were unset (observed 2026-09-05: `Codkit guard failed closed: codkit where --json returned an invalid envelope` on `echo ok`). **Considered and rejected:** a mode-aware hook that allows toolRoot targets — keeps a meaningless perimeter alive in the tool repository and still fails closed on unset roots; a separate task kind for tool development — invents a task perimeter for ordinary development. **When to revisit:** the tool repository becomes its own consumer (a `codkit.json` patch set maintained by Codkit appears at toolRoot) or a CI job requires an agent session over the tool repository (an agent job definition lands in the tool repository's CI). @status:spec/done

PreToolUse blocks forbidden writes. A hook resolves active boundaries by invoking the installed `codkit --json where` and reading schema-2 `roots.patches.path` and `roots.fork.path`; it does not treat toolRoot or cwd as patch-set. Global root-changing flags are denied inside an active agent perimeter. @status:spec/done

The text echelon — targeted wordings against the typical workarounds (the second echelon, not the only one): «do not rewrite the patch file by hand to get around a save refusal», «do not switch a red test off with a filter — that is a human decision backed by proof», «do not delete a marker to make verify go quiet», «do not substitute state.json — the cycle commands only». The list grows out of incidents. @status:spec/done

The architectural echelon (an agent in CI without a human): executable instructions and settings are taken **only from the trusted base branch**; the content of a PR is read as data; the trigger comes only from people with write access, and bots come from an explicit list; fail-closed: no rights or no configuration → no run. @status:spec/done
6. Journals and reports

The resolve journal is the jsonl of the cycle (PROP-009 §3), `by: "agent:<name>"`; the fields of an entry: the file, the artifact id, the outcome class, the resolution, the justification (1–3 sentences), `cause`, and what was verified (the list of commands with their exitCode). Completeness is a machine check of `cycle`. @status:spec/done
The verification report is the file `cycle/reports/<targetTag>-verify-<n>.md`: a table of checks → status → the full red list; and a section «what was not checked and why». @status:spec/done

The review notes are the file `cycle/reports/<targetTag>-review.md`: a note = {the intervention id, the substance, a reference to the rule, the proposed action}; the human reads the reports from the PR of the cycle. @status:spec/done
7. A single source of truth shared with the human protocol

Agent rules consume the effective conventions assembled from immutable shipped policy plus an explicitly configured additive-only patch-set extension. They never load a same-path patch-set file as a replacement or duplicate safety lists in prompts. @status:spec/done

The rubrics and checklists (the intervention review, the PR checklist, the outcome classes) are single files in `docs/codkit/protocol/human/templates/`, read by the human and by the agent alike. @status:spec/done

A change of the human protocol → an edit of the agent rules in the same PR; the documentation linter gains a check of the agent↔human cross-references. `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` are generated from one template, and a divergence is caught by a CI comparison. @status:spec/done
8. Evals and memory

In two steps: (1) practice from the very first cycle — the retrospective includes an «agent lessons» item: every mistake or rollback of an agent resolution → an edit of the corresponding skill in the same PR; (2) a regression harness (after the skills stabilize) — fixtures on a fake tree (PROP-013 §2) plus a substituted hosting client (a local bare repository); a run of the skill in headless mode; **structural checks of behavior**, not of text: the output files exist and are valid against the schemas, the journal is complete, there are no forbidden actions (the Git history of the tree and of the patch set has not changed), the exit codes are right; the threshold «k of N passed» (start: 4 of 5) against model flake. Run on a change of `.claude/skills/**` and on a schedule. @status:spec/done

The metrics (for the retrospective and for the series): the share of conflicts resolved without a human; the share of agent resolutions rejected by the reviewer; the resolution time. @status:spec/done

Agent memory (project scope, committed memory directories) is used as **team memory**: resolution patterns per subsystem, upstream traps. The policy: the agent **proposes** an entry (a file in the branch of the PR) and the human reviews it as code; it is forbidden to store the paths of a particular machine, secrets, the content of references, or conclusions that contradict the specs (memory is not a channel for bypassing the conventions). Stale entries are cleaned at the retrospective; every entry carries a date and a pin. @status:spec/done

The clean room for work on codkit: the implementing agent has no access to the references (the permissions profile of §5 plus a session without `--add-dir` onto the references); the names are our own; the final step of any task over `codkit/**` is the clean-room check (`common/PROP-004`). @status:spec/done
9. Open questions (recommendation + status)

**The boundaries of agent autonomy** — what may be carried through to the end without a human. Recommendation (the default): shifted, or a clean 3-way — autonomously (machine regeneration + verify); a substantive conflict — resolved by the agent, merged after a human review; target-deleted or semantic drift — the human only. **Requires an owner decision** (it moves the human/machine boundary). @status:spec/plan

**What counts as a design decision** (the stop criterion). Recommendation — a formal list: a change of the target layer of an intervention; an edit of own code beyond imports and signatures during a resolution; any new delta artifact; abandoning an intervention; an edit of a contract test. Recorded in `ck-resolve`; approved by the upgrade team. @status:spec/plan

**The memory policy**: the volume and the lifetime of entries, and whether every one of them must be reviewed — the default is «every entry through a PR review»; revisited after three cycles. @status:spec/plan

**LLM access in the air-gapped circuit**: the agent circuit in an air-gapped environment requires an internal API endpoint (a gateway or proxy in the internal network; the endpoint variables are the territory of CI, like credentials). Recommendation: the agent CI jobs are an optional profile, enabled only when an internal endpoint exists; without one the whole agent circuit is the local sessions of developers. **Requires an owner decision** (the delivery infrastructure). Related to J2. @status:spec/plan

**J1 (an experiment before implementation)**: on the current version of the agent tool, verify — the format and the semantics of the paths scope of rules; the way to forbid an automatic invocation of a skill; the behavior of `permissions.deny` inside `--add-dir`; Windows hooks (PowerShell); the mechanism that generates `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` from one source; whether the loading of instructions from added directories still behaves as described. @status:spec/plan
**J2 (an experiment)**: running the agent circuit in CI — authentication, headless mode, and the boundaries of a PR-driven run (the architectural echelon of §5) on our CI system. @status:spec/plan
codkit PROP-001: Purpose, boundaries, MVP scope

The specifications of the codkit module are written for a worker who took no part in the design and has no access to the reference repositories (clean room, `common/PROP-004`). Every design decision is already made; the implementer makes no design decisions and reads no references; when a fact about upstream is missing, the implementer reads the fork tree at the pin (this is allowed) or stops and asks the owner. @status:spec/done

Module contents: PROP-001 purpose (this document); PROP-002 layout and launch; PROP-003 configuration and data conventions; PROP-004 markers and patch format; PROP-005 delta layers; PROP-006 application metadata, locking, inventory; PROP-007 CLI commands; PROP-008 engines (load/save/classification/renames/reason); PROP-009 the cycle orchestrator; PROP-010 integration with the build of the fork tree - code delivery, the watch daemons, the tests; PROP-011 CI and the air-gapped circuit; PROP-012 output, errors, NFRs, documentation, open decision points; PROP-013 testing of codkit itself; PROP-014 the standards package and licence annotation; PROP-015 the delivery of the Codkit runtime - `runtime load|check`, `gen`, the delivered files (the content of the library belongs to the project type); FEAT-001 the polygon; FEAT-002 acceptance scenarios; FEAT-003/004 the requirement specifications for the human and the agent protocol. PROP-016 project types - the contract between the engine and a project type (`vscode`, `generic`, `theia`), types as packages, the split of the specifications into `modules/codkit` and `modules/vscode`. The answers of the `vscode` type live in the module `modules/vscode` (`spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-001#VSCODE-MODULE-MAP`). @status:spec/done
1. What codkit does
Resolves the path to the fork tree and checks its fitness (PROP-008 §1–2). @status:spec/done

Tombstone (Phase 1 of campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, 2026-09-06): the anchor is replaced by `DOES-LOAD` below; this anchor's address is immutable (NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR). The name reservation has been honoured: since Phase 8 of that campaign (2026-09-06) `codkit sync` is a real two-way save+load command, the live contract is PROP-007 `##CMD-SYNC-TWO-WAY` and the algorithm is PROP-008 §5a. @status:spec/done
Brings the fork tree to the pin and applies the delta as commits on a disposable generated branch (`load`), and delivers own code by copying. @status:spec/done
Extracts edits from the tree into patch-set artifacts (`save`/extract) and protects against the silent loss of work (the drift guard). @status:spec/done
Maintains the delta layers (PROP-005), the markers (PROP-004), the inventory (PROP-006). @status:spec/done
Wraps the build watch daemons of the project type into the commands `build up|down|status|errors` (PROP-010). @status:spec/done

Publishes the generated branches to the hosted fork repository (`publish`, `common/PROP-002` §4). @status:spec/done
Gives a containerized CI run «from scratch» with no network (`ci`, PROP-011) and race guards (`common/PROP-002` §7). @status:spec/done
2. What codkit does not do
Does not define or develop the user-facing product that a particular patch set serves; such requirements belong to the external consumer. @status:spec/done
Does not rewrite patch-set history; does not commit into the fork tree «by hand» (the generated commits of the delta branch are not manual). @status:spec/done

Does not rebase the delta, squash cycles, infer state from heuristics, or make the main path interactive (the non-goals of `common/PROP-001` §4). @status:spec/done
Does not edit upstream files with AI instructions in the tree (`AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and the like) and does not execute them. @status:spec/done

`load`/`save` with idempotence and fingerprint metadata - the successor of the tombstone `MVP-SYNC-SAVE` in the table above (Phase 1 of campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE). @status:spec/done

The build order is «foundation first, superstructure second»: independent resolution of the three roots → apply/extract → inventory/layers → orchestrator → rules/agents. The execution plan may change and is not part of the permanent specification. @status:spec/done
