codkit PROP-002: Code layout, launch, toolchain, components
1. Where the code lives
The layout is split into three roots which may live on different disks and may not coincide, nest inside one another, or be derived from one another: @status:spec/done

toolRoot is the CLI package `packages/codkit` of the tool's npm workspace, and only it owns the sources, the launchers, the base safety configs, the tests and the npm dependencies of Codkit; the workspace root above it owns the repository's own machinery (the specs, the generators, the gates, the development lock) and is private - it publishes nothing. Only patchesDir owns `codkit.json`, `delta/**`, `cycle/**`, the runtime `.codkit/**` and the Git history of the patch set. Only forkDir owns the VS Code checkout and the generated refs. The standards package in toolRoot belongs to toolRoot; its installed copy under patchesDir belongs to codkit and is edited only by the standards load command (PROP-014). @status:spec/done
A patch set ignores at least `codkit.local.json` and `.codkit/`. It is not obliged to have a `package.json` or `node_modules` for the sake of Codkit. @status:spec/done

`package.json` and the publishable `npm-shrinkwrap.json` belong to toolRoot - that is, to the CLI package `packages/codkit`, not to the workspace root - and fix the runtime dependency graph identically in the source checkout and in the npm artifact. The workspace root carries its own `npm-shrinkwrap.json` for the development install of every package at once; it is never published. The runtime dependencies are installed next to the tool. Missing dependencies give a diagnosed refusal that demands the installation be restored from the approved supply; for a source checkout `npm ci` is admissible. @status:spec/done

Bounds of the npm tarball in `packages/codkit/test/unit/packageManifest.test.ts`, applied to every published package of the workspace (PROP-016 ##TYPE-SUPPLY-KIT): the test packs each `packages/*` with `npm pack --dry-run` and states, per package, the files it must ship, the executables it must keep executable, and these bounds. **Decision (owner ruling, 2026-09-07, verbatim: «поднять размер в тесте до 50 мегабайт»):** `unpackedSize < 50_000_000`; `entryCount < 640` and the tar bound `2_000_000` stay as the ruling of 2026-09-06 left them. **Why:** the unpacked bound fired on planned work - the STANDARDS campaign added the standards package (81_940 bytes), PROP-014 (112_670) and six modules that ship twice, as sources and as their compiled output, taking the tarball to 5_055_081 unpacked with the tar at 1_383_894 and 429 of 640 entries. Nothing a consumer experiences was near a limit: 5 MB unpacked on a developer machine costs nothing, and this decision's own revisit trigger (the tar above 2 MB, or a consumer complaint) had not fired. A ratchet that blocks planned work without naming a cost measures the wrong thing. The consequence is recorded rather than hidden: at this number the effective ratchet is the tar bound, which text compressing about fivefold reaches near 10 MB unpacked, so 50 MB is never approached - the unpacked bound is now a backstop against a pathological artifact, not the growth signal. **Consequence of the workspace split (2026-09-09):** a package can only ship what lies inside it, so the CLI tarball carries the runnable tool and the operator surfaces that live in `packages/codkit` - the sources, the compiled runtime, the launchers, the configs, the agent profile and its guard, the shipped vibe packages and the runtime library - while the repository's specifications, `docs/codkit` and the repository-level `AUDIT.md`/`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` stay at the workspace root and reach a consumer through the repository rather than through the tarball. **Considered and rejected:** dropping `packages/codkit/src` from the shipped set - measured at 272 entries and 3_063_152 unpacked, and the launcher runs `packages/codkit/dist/main.js` so sources are not needed at runtime, but a consumer would stop receiving the source of the tool they installed, and that is a distribution decision nobody asked for; a smaller step such as 5_500_000 - the owner named 50 MB; dropping `AUDIT.md` or `docs/codkit` - documentation a consumer should have. **When to revisit:** the tar exceeds 2 MB (unchanged, and now the binding signal), or a consumer reports install size or time. @status:spec/done

toolRoot is computed only from the `import.meta.url` of the tool being launched. patchesDir and forkDir are resolved independently through the sources of PROP-003; cwd never becomes a root automatically. @status:spec/done
2. Launch and toolchain

The source of truth is the TypeScript in `packages/codkit/src`. `npm run runtime:build` produces plain ESM JavaScript in `packages/codkit/dist` with rewritten relative extensions; `runtime:check` compares a fresh temp emit with the tracked dist byte for byte. The launcher calls `node toolRoot/dist/main.js <args>` with the same `process.execPath`, so an installed npm package does not try to strip `.ts` under `node_modules`. @status:spec/done

The user entry points are `bin/codkit` for Bash and `bin/codkit.ps1` for PowerShell. They exist twice and identically in purpose: inside the CLI package, where an installation is rooted, and at the workspace root of the source checkout. Both resolve the root relative to their own file (not to cwd), check that Node is available and pass argv and the exit code on to the internal `bin/codkit.mjs` of the CLI package; the wrapper scripts carry no command or format logic. @status:impl/done

A constraint for the codkit code: erasable TS syntax only — no `enum`, no `namespace`, no constructor parameter properties; instead of an enum — union types and `as const` objects. (It coincides with the `erasableSyntaxOnly` flag of the AI-native TypeScript envelope — `common/PROP-000` §5.) @status:spec/done

Codkit itself requires Node ≥ 22.6 as its installed runtime floor. The build version of a particular fork is set by that fork's `.nvmrc`; if the resolved tree requires another major, Codkit warns instead of substituting the environment, and it does not make a consumer-specific version part of the tool policy. @status:spec/done

git ≥ 2.40 (a stable `git apply`, `merge-file`, `commit-tree` and `--force-with-lease` are needed); git-lfs ≥ 3.0 is an environment contract: without it the tree holds pointer files. @status:spec/done

The operating systems: Linux, macOS, Windows. All paths go through `node:path`/`node:fs` (`realpath`), never through concatenation of strings with separators; on Windows codkit checks `core.longpaths=true` in the config of the tree and warns when it is absent. @status:spec/done

`CODKIT_PATCHES_DIR` and `CODKIT_FORK_DIR` are public user sources, not test overrides. Each root has its own independent precedence CLI flag → env → `~/.codkit/settings.json`; relative CLI and env paths are resolved from cwd, and settings accepts absolute paths only. @status:impl/done

**The isolation of the Git environment is the foundation of determinism:** every git run from codkit is executed with the environment `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `LC_ALL=C`, `TZ=UTC` and with explicit `-c core.autocrlf=false -c core.quotepath=false`; the repository settings that are needed are passed as `-c` flags. The exceptions are the operations obliged to see the config of the repository or of the container (reading `safe.directory` in CI, PROP-011 §5; their list is fixed there) and the single read-only query `rev-parse --git-path hooks/<name>` with the machine config visible (the `machineConfig` flag of the wrapper, legal ONLY together with `pathResolution`): the effective location of a configured hook is a property of the user's git, an isolated view does not see it, and to declare the guard active without asking the user's git would be a lie (PROP-008 §3 `##TREE-HOOK-STEP`, REPAIR-006). @status:spec/done

**The administrative files touched by REPAIR-006 (the git mark, the hooks, the exclude) and the configuration reads of `codkit.json` / `codkit.local.json` / the declared build-watch and conventions all go through one implementation, `containedFile.ts`.** Reading: the parent components are checked with lstat (a symbolic link is a refusal), the leaf is opened with a single descriptor with `O_NOFOLLOW` (the platforms without it — Windows — check the leaf before the open and compare the descriptor afterwards; the remaining check-then-open window is documented, not hidden), the descriptor must be a regular file, and after the open it is proved that it names a file inside the root (realpath + a comparison of dev/ino with the canonical path) — a parent component swapped for a symlink after the check is caught by the post-open proof and its bytes are not used. Writing: an atomic replacement (an exclusive temporary file + rename) only inside a parent which, immediately before the write, must be a real canonical directory; a leaf symlink is a refusal (`codkit never writes through a link`), and a symlink swapped in after the check of the leaf is replaced by the rename itself — the target of the link does not change; after the write the identity and realpath of the parent are re-checked. The limitation of the Node `fs` is recorded honestly: the portable API gives no `openat`/`renameat` relative to a held directory descriptor, so a malicious swap of the parent itself in the narrow window between the last check and the creation of the temporary file is detected post-write but is not prevented before the first byte on every platform; a pre-existing parent or leaf symlink and a swap during a read are refused before the data is used. The administrative directories (`hooks/`, `codkit/`, `info/`) are created only as real directories — a symlink component is a refusal. The module does not decide «whose bytes these are»: ownership and refusal stay with the calling layer. @status:impl/done

REPAIR-007: the tree mark, the common/worktree exclude, the tree hook and the patch-set hooks use `readContainedFile(root, relative)` end-to-end, and the writes use `writeContainedFileAtomic`; a checked parent is not then handed to a weaker leaf-only reader. On a real FS `writeConfigPin` reads descriptor-held bytes, performs a repeated contained CAS read and writes a contained atomic replacement; the injectable legacy FS stays a test seam only. Every public consumer has a deterministic after-open parent-swap regression with an unchanged outside sentinel. @status:impl/done

REPAIR-009: mutating the pin in `codkit.json` requires a LIVE capability of this patch set's cycle-global lock, not merely a structurally similar handle: a forged, a copied, an already released and a foreign (another patchesDir) handle all refuse. The bytes are re-read before the replacement, so an external edit that arrived after the comparison is preserved and the call returns a locked/config failure. The residual limitation is recorded honestly: an external editor whose last system call writes after our repeated read can still be overwritten — Node gives no atomic compare-and-swap over an ordinary file. @status:impl/done
3. Components (the modules of packages/codkit/src/lib/)
The file names are a recommendation, the responsibilities are normative: @status:spec/done

`layers/*`, `applyEngine` and `inventory` know nothing about the CLI; the commands receive explicit toolRoot, patchesDir, forkDir and the patch-set config object instead of reopening the roots through cwd. This is the cell rule of AI-native TypeScript as well: one module = one cell with a single public entry. @status:spec/done
4. Cross-platform support — the conditions of acceptance

Acceptance requires a native test «a double regeneration gives an empty diff» separately on Linux, macOS and Windows (S16). The current Linux run is not a proof for the two other operating systems. @status:spec/plan
No mechanism assumes that the three roots are neighbours; the tests use three unrelated random paths (PROP-013 §1). @status:spec/done
Symlinks are not used as a mechanism (code is delivered by copying); on Windows linking is replaced by a copy everywhere. @status:spec/done
codkit PROP-003: Configuration, data conventions, the owners map, common format rules
1. Common rules of every codkit format
Every format carries its schema version - an integer in the field named after the format itself (for example, `"codkitConfig": 1`, `"codkitOverlay": 2`). @status:spec/done

The migration rule after the first user: a reader accepts version `N`; on `N+1` and above it fails with code 2 and the text «the format is newer than the tool, update codkit»; a version below the current one it reads by the rules of that version and writes the current one at the next write. The one-off pre-user exception of the owner, 2026-08-31: the D5 metadata formats `patch/overlay/resource/rule/own/inventory` moved from v1 to v2 through a hard rename of the former field into `cause`; there were no external users and no meaningful values of the former field, so v2 deliberately refuses v1 and no legacy reader is shipped. @status:spec/done
All format files: UTF-8 encoding without a BOM, LF line endings, a trailing LF is mandatory. @status:spec/done

JSON is serialized deterministically: an indent of two spaces; object keys in the order defined by the schema (NOT alphabetically); arrays in the order defined by the schema (usually sorted by `id` or by path). @status:spec/done

The format schemas are described by Zod schemas as the single source of the static type and of runtime validation (`common/PROP-000` `##CODKIT-VALIDATOR-ZOD`); the diagnostic text of a schema error is formed in the terms of the code registry of PROP-012 §2, not as the raw output of the validator. @status:spec/done
2. User settings for the locations

`~/.codkit/settings.json` selects the external roots independently: the strict schema `{"codkitSettings":1,"patchesDir":"/absolute/path","forkDir":"/absolute/path"}`. Both path fields are optional and absolute only; an unknown field, a wrong type or another schema version gives `CK-E-CONFIG`. @status:spec/done
patchesDir: `--patches-dir` → `CODKIT_PATCHES_DIR` → the settings `patchesDir`; the absence of all three is a diagnosed refusal for the commands that need a patch set. @status:spec/done
forkDir: `--fork-dir` → `CODKIT_FORK_DIR` → the settings `forkDir`; the absence of all three is allowed only for the commands that do not need the tree. @status:spec/done

A relative CLI or env path is resolved against the cwd of the process. The settings accept absolute paths only. `codkit.json`, a neighbouring directory and the location of toolRoot are never a fallback source of a root. @status:spec/done

After canonicalization toolRoot, patchesDir and forkDir must be pairwise disjoint, nesting included. A violation stops the command before the patch set is read and before any mutation. @status:spec/done
3. The patch-set configuration - codkit.json (+ codkit.local.json)

`upstreamAnchorCommit` is the SHA by whose reachability the tree is recognized as «the microsoft/vscode history» (the origin is checked by the reachability of a known commit, not by the name of a remote). The value is computed once when the configuration is created: `git rev-list --max-parents=0 <pin.sha>` (the root commit of the history; if there are several roots, the lexicographically smallest SHA is taken). It is committed in `codkit.json` and does not change when the pin is raised. @status:spec/done

**Schema 2 (PROP-016).** `codkit.json` carries `"codkitConfig": 2`, the required `"type": "<identifier>"` and the required `"typeConfig": { ... }`, whose first field is `ownRoot` - a full path from the tree root. The engine validates the universal fields of the table above and hands `typeConfig` to the type, which validates it with its own schema and refuses with `CK-E-CONFIG` naming the field (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-CONFIG-FIELD`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-OWN-ROOT`). One patch set, one type. The row `ownDirName` of the table above is the schema-1 field it replaces. @status:spec/done

**There is no compatibility layer.** A `codkit.json` without `type` is schema 1 and is refused with `CK-E-CONFIG` that names the two fields to add - `type` and `typeConfig.ownRoot` - and nothing else; no command reads schema 1 and no code path infers a type from `ownDirName` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-SCHEMA-2-REQUIRED`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#DECISION-NO-COMPATIBILITY-LAYER`). The single existing consumer is migrated inside the campaign, with its own gates as the proof. @status:spec/done

`codkit.local.json` contains only optional non-pin operational overrides (`typeConfig`, the branch/ref prefixes, `publishRemoteUrl`; in schema 1 the first of them was `ownDirName`). The `type` itself is not overridable locally: one patch set declares one type and it is a shared invariant of the repository. It does not accept `pin`, `upstreamAnchorCommit`, the schema field, the location roots or references to a safety/build policy. The root paths belong to the CLI, the environment and the user settings alone. @status:spec/done
After the initial bootstrap of a patch set the pin changes only by the canonical commit of an upgrade cycle. @status:spec/done
A valid sample (the `upstreamAnchorCommit` value is a placeholder of the example; in a real file it is the computed SHA): @status:spec/done

An invalid sample and the expected diagnostics: a file with `"pin": {"tag": "1.135.0"}` (no `sha`) → exit 2, the message `CK-E-CONFIG: codkit.json: pin.sha is required (full 40-hex commit sha of the pin tag)`. @status:spec/done
4. Data conventions and safe extension

The mandatory base policy lives only in `toolRoot/config/conventions.json`; the CLI, the checks, the CI and the agent protocols read it. A file with the same path under patchesDir never shadows the installed policy. @status:spec/done
Tombstone (PROP-016 split, 2026-09-09): moved to spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-009#FORBIDDEN-SERVICES-SEED; the address stays for citations. @status:spec/done

If `conventionsExtensionFile` is given, the path must stay inside patchesDir after symlinks are resolved. The strict schema `codkitConventionsExtension:1` may add `subsystems` (the effective idPattern is derived from the union), additional `forbiddenPatchTargets`, `forbiddenServiceIds` and `markerComment` for new file extensions only. It cannot delete, replace or weaken the base prohibitions, change the layer order, an existing marker form, the intervention types/categories or the cleanup policy. @status:spec/done

A patch-set file `codkit/config/conventions.json` without an explicit `conventionsExtensionFile` is ignored. Even with an explicit reference the content is treated as an additive extension, not as a replacement of the shipped policy. @status:spec/done

By default the build wrapper reads `toolRoot/config/build-watch.json`. Only an explicit `buildWatchFile` selects the strict versioned profile of a particular fork; the patch set is the project policy chosen by the user, but a hidden copy under the same name is not taken into account. The path must be relative and contained inside patchesDir. Every channel must have at least one `errorLine` or `errorCountLine`; unknown fields are forbidden. The author of a custom profile keeps green/red log fixtures and confirms that an error does not become exit 0. @status:spec/done
5. The owners map - delta/owners.json
The format: `{"codkitOwners":1,"owners":{"workbench-core":{"contact":"<team-or-login>","paths":["src/vs/workbench/**"]}, …}}`. @status:spec/done
The `owner` value of any artifact must be a key of `owners`; otherwise `verify` gives exit 1, `CK-E-OWNER-UNKNOWN`. @status:spec/done

The CODEOWNERS file of the hosting is generated from this map (the command is not in the MVP; the map itself is already in the MVP: the inventory needs the «subsystem → owner» routing). @status:spec/done
6. Artifact metadata - the common dictionary

Every layer gives the inventory the same set of fields: `id`, `layer`, `type`, `category`, `owner`, `reason`, `link`, `cause`, `pin`, `contract-tests`, plus the computed `subsystem` (from the id) and `files` (the targets of the intervention). The carrier for a patch is the `.ckpatch` header (PROP-004 §3); for an overlay/resource/rule it is the fields of their JSON (PROP-005); for own and entry-module it is the records in `delta/own/patchset.delta.json` (PROP-005 §3). @status:spec/done
codkit PROP-004: Markers and the .ckpatch patch format
1. Marker forms by language

A marker carries the identifier and nothing else; the full metadata live in the delta artifact in the patch set (the patch header and the like). This way the marker does not inflate the patch or the context of the diff, and it is carried over renames reliably, together with the metadata, by the identifier. @status:spec/done
2. Marker rules (normative, checked by verify)

A marker line: an optional indent, the comment form, the word `codkit:begin|end`, one space, an id matching `idPattern`. Nothing else on the line (except the comment terminator for CSS/HTML). @status:spec/done
Marker lines and the service comments inside a block use ASCII, so as not to introduce a dependency on a fork-specific Unicode hygiene policy. @status:spec/done

Inside a block: a functional change only; upstream lines that are neutralized are **commented out, not deleted**; formatting edits outside one's own block are forbidden; multi-line logic is not written where a one-line hook is enough - the logic lives in own code. @status:spec/done

A hook is placed at a point of the particular pin that is stable: preferably the beginning of an existing `create*` method, not a constructor signature; DI goes through an accessor or instantiation service that is already available, not through a new constructor parameter. @status:spec/done
Nesting of markers is forbidden; one id may cover blocks in several files only for the `entry-module` layer (PROP-005 §4), otherwise it is one file. @status:spec/done

One id may open **several blocks in one file**: a graft usually consists of an import line and a call site, and that is one intervention, not two. The blocks of one id are not nested inside each other; every block of the file with that id belongs to one artifact (`save` collects them into one patch, `verify` counts the graft budget over all the blocks together - PROP-005 `PATCH-HOOK-BUDGET`). `CK-E-MARKER-DUP-ID` remains the error of two *records* with one id and of a repeated `marker new` with an id already taken. Decision of 2026-09-07: before it the rule «one block per file» forced one either to put the import and the call site under different ids (two records about one intervention) or to stretch the block over the whole span between them; rejected - both variants lie to the inventory. @status:spec/done

JSON without comments and binary files have no marker by construction - their interventions live in the overlay, the resource map or the removed registry, and must have a guard test. @status:spec/done
3. Marker parsing (the algorithm)
Input: the content of the file (bytes), the extension. Output: a list of blocks `{id, beginLine, endLine}` (1-based lines, the marker lines included) plus a list of errors. @status:spec/done
Performance: a linear pass; the pre-commit requirement is a fraction of a second per file (PROP-012 §3). @status:spec/done
4. A patch - the file delta/patches/*.ckpatch

**The file name** encodes the path of the upstream file: the separator `/` is replaced by `__` (a double underscore), and the extension `.ckpatch` is appended to the full name. Example: `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/titlebar/titlebarPart.ts` → `delta/patches/src__vs__workbench__browser__parts__titlebar__titlebarPart.ts.ckpatch`. Decoding back: cut off `.ckpatch`, replace `__` with `/`. Before the replacement the encoder checks that the path contains no `__`, and on a collision it fails with code 2 (there are no such paths at the pin; the check is for the future). @status:spec/done

**The structure of the file**: the metadata header, then the unified diff. The header is the lines that start with `# `, up to the first `--- ` line; `git apply` ignores such lines (garbage before the diff headers), so the file is applicable as an ordinary patch. @status:spec/done
The header fields (the order is fixed, all of them are mandatory): @status:spec/done
**The body** is a normalized unified diff of exactly one file: @status:spec/done

exactly one pair of headers `--- a/<path>` and `+++ b/<path>` with the same `<path>` (LF line endings, no tabs and no quotes; paths with spaces are not escaped - there are none in the upstream tree, and their presence is an encoder error); @status:spec/done

then the hunks `@@ -l,c +l,c @@` with a context of exactly 3 lines (`-U3`); refined by the M0 implementation: git omits the `,1` of single-line ranges and adds a section heading after the second `@@` - both forms are accepted and preserved byte for byte (otherwise double regeneration is unreachable); an empty context line may arrive without the leading space - it is accepted and reproduced verbatim; @status:impl/done
no `diff --git`, `index` or `mode` lines, no dates, authors or series numbers: they are not needed for applying and they carry non-deterministic data; @status:spec/done

the content of the lines is byte for byte as in the files (LF; trailing spaces are preserved); the file ends with an LF; the marker `\ No newline at end of file` is allowed by the rules of unified diff. @status:spec/done

A patch always describes a **state**, «the file at the pin → our state of the file», not an increment. There is no order and no dependency between patches (one file is one patch by construction); the order of applying under `load` is the lexicographic sort of the patch file names by UTF-8 bytes (it is needed only for the determinism of the branch). @status:spec/done

**An add-file patch** (a new file in the upstream zone - allowed only as an exception, PROP-005 §9): `--- /dev/null`, `+++ b/<path>`, one hunk `@@ -0,0 +1,N @@`. **Deleting an upstream file by a patch is forbidden** (`--- a/… +++ /dev/null` is a validation error; hide plus the removed registry are used instead). @status:spec/done
A valid sample in full (ours, written from scratch; the path and the context lines are notional and show the form only; a real patch carries the bytes of a real upstream file): @status:spec/done

An invalid sample: the same file, but the added lines stand **outside** the `codkit:begin`/`codkit:end` pair. The expected diagnostics of `codkit verify` (exit 1): `CK-E-HUNK-OUTSIDE-MARKER: delta/patches/…ckpatch: hunk at target line 113 adds lines outside any codkit marker block. Wrap the change in "// codkit:begin CK-workbench-001" … "// codkit:end CK-workbench-001".` @status:spec/done
5. Deterministic patch generation, «pin → file»

Input: the path F, the pin bytes `pinBytes` (the git object: `git show <pin.sha>:<path>` - with no network and no checkout), the target bytes `curBytes` (the working file of the tree). Output: the bytes of the `.ckpatch` (the header preserved or updated + the new body) or «no changes». @status:spec/done

**The byte predicates** (before the diff): `curBytes` is valid UTF-8; the line endings are LF (a CR found → refusal `CK-E-CRLF`, with a hint about `core.autocrlf=false`); the trailing LF is present if it was present at the pin (lost → refusal `CK-E-EOF-NEWLINE`); the file is not binary (a NUL byte → refusal: binary targets belong to the resource-file layer). Trailing spaces are NOT cleaned up - the bytes are preserved. @status:spec/done

The diff: `git diff --no-index -U3 --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -- <tmpPin> <tmpCur>` in the isolated environment (PROP-002 §2), with the explicit `-c diff.algorithm=myers -c core.autocrlf=false -c diff.renames=false -c diff.mnemonicPrefix=false -c diff.noprefix=false`. The temporary files are created in `.codkit/tmp/` under the fixed names `a`/`b` (which do not depend on absolute paths); the `diff --git`/`index`/`old mode`/`new mode` lines are removed from the output; the `---`/`+++` headers are rewritten to the canonical path F. (The hashes of the `index` lines are thrown away: their abbreviated length depends on the number of objects in the repository - a source of non-determinism.) @status:spec/done
An empty diff → the patch file is not written at all; an existing patch, once the target has returned to the pin, is deleted by the `save` command with a message. @status:spec/done

Assembling the `.ckpatch`: an existing header is preserved (regeneration changes neither the id nor the metadata; the `pin` field is updated only by the regeneration step of an upgrade cycle); for a new file the header comes from the answer of `marker new` or from the flags. @status:spec/done
The comparison with the old `.ckpatch` is **byte-wise**: on a match → do not write (do not touch the mtime). @status:spec/done

The format requires a double regeneration to produce an empty diff. The Linux check is part of the current floor; native macOS/Windows proofs are separate open rows of the S16/PROP-013 matrix, not an implied result. @status:spec/done
codkit PROP-005: Delta layers - formats, materialization, prohibitions
1. The seven layers and the choice rule

For a new divergence from upstream the **topmost applicable layer** of the `layers` list is chosen (PROP-003 §3): own → service-override → entry-module → config-overlay → resource-file → rewrite-rule → patch. Descending to a lower layer requires a justification in review ("why not own? why not a service override?"). @status:spec/done
The metric is the number of rewrite-rule + patch artifacts per subsystem; it must fall, not grow (`common/PROP-001` `##GOAL-SHRINK-COUPLING`). @status:spec/done

Every layer is a distinct kind of artifact in patchset with an owner and a reason; every one is accounted for by the inventory; every convention of a layer is introduced together with a machine check. @status:spec/done

Calibration on product examples confirmed the load-bearing capacity of the upper layers: interface modes → layers 1–2 (0 patches); extension control → own + override + hide + overlay + pinpoint patches; subsystem modules → own + entry-module; rebranding → overlay + resource-file + own. No example required mass patches. @status:spec/done
2. Summary table of the layers

Cross-cutting mechanisms (not layers, but a discipline over them): **hide** is the category `hide` on an entry of any layer (preferably own/overlay, not patch); **removed-registry** is `delta/removed.json` (§10); a **contract/guard test** is a mandatory coverage field for the config-overlay and resource-file layers and for every entry of the `hide` category (checked by `verify`). @status:spec/done
3. own - own code

The source of truth is `delta/own/**` in patchset; on `load` the content is copied into `<tree>/src/vs/<ownDirName>/` (= `src/vs/patchset/`), and on `save` it is mirrored back. The copy has rsync semantics by content: a file is rewritten only when its bytes differ; files absent from the source are removed in the destination; the mtime of untouched files does not change (PROP-008 §3). @status:spec/done
Tombstone (PROP-016 split, 2026-09-09): moved to spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-002#OWN-UNDER-SRC-VS; the address stays for citations. @status:spec/done

Locally the directory is not tracked by the git of the tree, BUT only in a single-worktree repository: there `load` appends to the effective `info/exclude` (the path git reports as `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path info/exclude`; the rule for administrative paths is PROP-008 §3 `##TREE-HOOK-STEP`) a managed block (`# codkit:begin managed` / the path `/src/vs/patchset/` / `# codkit:end managed`), restored on every `load`. In a repository with several worktrees (two or more entries in `git worktree list`) `info/exclude` is ONE file for all the siblings: the block of one tree would hide the own paths in all the others, and a second patch set with its own directory would overwrite the block of the first (REPAIR-006). The exclusion there is therefore worktree-local: codkit owns the file `codkit/exclude` in the per-worktree administrative directory (next to the PROP-006 mark `##TREE-MARK`), enables `extensions.worktreeConfig=true` in the common config of the repository (a foreign value is a refusal, never an overwrite) and points the per-worktree `core.excludesFile` at its own file (a foreign value is a refusal; a file with foreign content is a refusal). Every `load` rewrites the file; on the first worktree-local `load` codkit removes ITS OWN stale block from the common `info/exclude`, and foreign lines are left untouched. The life cycle is explicit: the key and the file are the codkit namespace and are not removed automatically; to remove them by hand, `git config --worktree --unset core.excludesFile`. An accidental commit is impossible, because git does not see the directory. In CI/publish mode the directory is committed to the generated branch instead; the modes are not mixed in one tree: the sign is that the mode is determined by the command (`load` is local; `ci`/`publish` commit own), and the branch is fully recreated before the mode is switched. @status:spec/done

REPAIR-007 failure-atomic activation: the owned per-worktree exclude is first written atomically and byte-verified, and only then may the config point at it. Before the changes the exact bytes of the common config, of config.worktree, of the owned exclude and of the migrated common exclude are saved; a failure after the owned write, the extension enable or the core.excludesFile set restores the snapshots in reverse order. The config is never left pointing at a missing file; index/worktree bytes take no part and stay exact. @status:impl/done

**The graft point** is a minimal side-effect import from an existing entry of the current pin into `./<ownDirName>/<ownDirName>.contribution.js`. The graft is a patch artifact of the entry-module layer; the number of interventions made to wire in own code stays constant. The concrete entry is confirmed against the actual desktop/web chain of the selected fork. `marker new --layer entry-module` carries the layer into the header; `rewrite-rule` is available only to the rule generator. @status:spec/done

Own files pass the actual hygiene/lint policy of the selected fork/pin. The preference is to follow the local format without exceptions; if an exception is unavoidable, it is a separate minimal intervention with contract evidence. @status:spec/done

**The declaration of own units** is `delta/own/patchset.delta.json` (`codkitOwnManifest: 2`): the array `units` holds entries `{id, layer:"own", type, category, owner, reason, link, cause, pin, contractTests, roots}`, where `roots` are paths inside `delta/own/`; the array `serviceOverrides` holds entries `{id, serviceId, module, owner, reason, link, cause, pin, contractTests}`, whose `type`/`category` in the inventory are the derived constants `modify`/`own` (there are no such fields in the schema; M1 refinement). Every own file must fall into exactly one unit, including the modules from `serviceOverrides[].module` (the override entry sets the layer, the module file is covered by an own unit; M1 refinement); `verify` checks coverage and non-overlap; a file outside the units is `CK-E-OWN-UNCOVERED`. The exception of the STANDARDS campaign (2026-09-06): the file `LICENSE-CODKIT.md`, which `codkit standards load` puts into `delta/own/`, requires no unit but is delivered into the tree as an ordinary own file (PROP-014 §4a `STD-NOTICE-IS-A-DELIVERED-OWN-FILE`); the set of "not own code" is `patchset.delta.json`, `.gitkeep`, `LICENSE-CODKIT.md`. @status:spec/done

The manifest is a patchset artifact, NOT part of the delivered code: mirroring own into the tree excludes `patchset.delta.json` just as it excludes `.gitkeep` (otherwise it materializes into `src/vs/<ownDirName>/` and is carried by the transpiler into `out/`; observed by the M1 polygon, fixed). @status:impl/done
4. service-override and entry-module
Tombstone (PROP-016 split, 2026-09-09): moved to spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-003#SO-MECHANISM; the address stays for citations. @status:spec/done

entry-module is a fork of the import list of an upstream entry: the unneeded upstream imports are **commented out** inside marker blocks and our own are added. Which module is an entry is the project type's answer (VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-003#VSCODE-ENTRY-MODULE-LOCATOR`, which also names the upstream precedent of a forked import list). @status:spec/done

The layer has two forms: (a) **a graft**, a minimal marked import from an existing entry; (b) **an own entry** of a new top-level module, own files plus separate pinpoint artifacts for the actual build/i18n/style/test registries of the current fork. No file list is taken to be eternal: it is checked on the pin and recorded by the inventory. @status:spec/done

A candidate for rewrite-rule: generating the entry fork by the operations "comment out import X" / "add import Y" with the `expectedMatches` counter, so that a drift of the upstream import list becomes the loud error `CK-E-RULE-DRIFT` instead of a silent loss of the contribution. @status:spec/done
5. config-overlay - format and materialization

The relation of files to a target is many-to-one (M1 refinement): every overlay file carries one target, but one target may be carried by SEVERAL files; both materialization channels and the check of a materialized target work with the COMPOSITION of all overlays of that target (in the lexicographic order of the file names); the generated branch commit is one per target, with a `Codkit-Artifact:` trailer for every overlay that entered it; the dev channel is NOT written when target materialization is enabled (the channels are alternatives). @status:impl/done

One overlay file, one target: `delta/overlays/<target-name>.overlay.json` (for example `product.json.overlay.json`). The fields: `codkitOverlay: 2`; `id`; `target` (the path of the target file from the root of the tree); the metadata dictionary of PROP-003 §5 (`type`/`category`/`owner`/`reason`/`link`/`cause`/`pin`/`contractTests`, where the guard test is **mandatory**); `operations`, the list of operations, whose order matters. The overlay is applied by parsing and serializing JSON, not as text. @status:spec/done

An operation: `op` is `"set"` (create/replace the value at the path) or `"remove"` (delete the key); `path` is an array of object keys from the root of the JSON, array indices are not supported (an array is replaced whole through a `set` on its parent); `value` is, for `set`, a static value **or** an object `{"$var": "<name>"}`; `expectUpstream` is optional: the expected upstream value at that path on the pin, or `{"$absent": true}` ("the key is absent on the pin"). @status:spec/done

The `$var` variables (computed at the moment of materialization): `pin.tag`, `pin.sha`, `pin.date`, `patchset.commit` (the SHA of the patchset HEAD), `build.date` (the UTC ISO date of the moment of materialization; in deterministic contexts, the date of the pin commit). @status:spec/done

The semantics of `expectUpstream`: on `overlay check` and on every `load` the value at `path` in the **clean** file of the pin (`git show <pin.sha>:<target>`) is compared with `expectUpstream` (deep equality). A mismatch is the error `CK-E-OVERLAY-DRIFT` (exit 1): upstream changed the key, and the intervention needs review. @status:spec/done
A valid sample: @status:spec/done

An invalid sample: the operation `{"op": "insert", …}` → exit 2, `CK-E-OVERLAY-SCHEMA: delta/overlays/product.json.overlay.json: operations[0].op must be "set" or "remove", got "insert"`. @status:spec/done

**Materialization has two channels:** (1) the dev channel for `product.json` builds `product.overrides.json`, but only if the actual bootstrap of the current pin supports that file; `verify` checks the support and that the target is ignored by Git. A nested operation first seeds the top-level key from the clean pin and then changes the required path. (2) packaging/publish/`ci --profile build` materializes the complete target file from the clean blob of the pin, applies the operations in order and commits the result. A missing or changed upstream seam is an explicit `OVERLAY-DRIFT`, not a hidden heuristic. The two channels are universal machinery; which file is the manifest, and whether a dev channel exists for it at all, is the project type's answer (VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-003#VSCODE-OVERLAY-TARGETS`). @status:spec/done

**Known materialization (REPAIR-005):** channel 2 writes strictly deterministic bytes into the tree - the clean blob of the pin plus the operations of all overlays of that target in canonical order, tab indentation and a final LF, in the context of the run (`pin.*`, `patchset.commit`, `build.date`). Such bytes are therefore recognizable: before the drift guard refuses, `load --fresh` compares every tracked overlay target that differs from HEAD with that composition, and an exact byte match is a state that codkit wrote itself (`overlay apply`), not unextracted work; this run replaces it and returns the tree to dev mode (the raw file is the state of the dev/generated branch, the dev channel is written), without a direct `git checkout` of the target. Any deviation - an extra, a missing or a hand-made byte, a foreign file, a missing file - stays dirt, and `--fresh` is not a blanket reset. A plain `load` makes no such comparison and stays red on a materialization: its fast path could answer "up to date" and leave the packaging bytes standing as the dev state. A refusal to classify (an unreadable base, an unsafe target path) is treated as "not recognized" and stays dirt; the guard may only narrow. @status:impl/done

For targets other than `product.json` (for example the `package.json` of the tree) there is no dev channel: materialization always follows variant 2. The permitted change to the upstream `package.json` is **addition only** of keys in `scripts`; for that target `overlay check` verifies that every operation is a `set` on the paths `["scripts", *]`. @status:spec/done
6. resource-file - replacement of binary/resource files

`delta/resources/map.json`: `codkitResourceMap: 2`; `entries` (sorted by `target`; an unsorted file is read with sorting and a warning - M0 refinement) holds entries `{id, target, source, type, category, owner, reason, link, cause, pin, contractTests}`. `target` is the path of an upstream file from the root of the tree; the file **must exist on the pin** (the layer replaces content, it does not add files). A narrow transitional exception inside an active upgrade cycle: after a rename has been confirmed by hand, `target` may already equal the exact `rename.to` while `pin` still points at the source pin, but only if the classifier proved a regular blob `rename.from` on the source pin and a regular blob `rename.to` on the target pin; a merely new file on the target pin does not count as such an exception, and the regeneration in the same transaction moves the metadata pin to the target pin. `source` is the path of our file from the root of patchset, under `delta/resources/files/`. The names of target files do not change - the content is replaced under the same names (the brand resource names are hardcoded in the build). @status:spec/done

The `contractTests` of an entry is **mandatory and non-empty**: the guard test catches the "silent loss of a binary" at an upgrade (on this class a reference fork twice lost a branded file silently). An example entry: `{"id":"CK-product-002","target":"resources/linux/code.png","source":"delta/resources/files/linux/app-icon.png", …}`. @status:spec/done
7. rewrite-rule - the format (the engine comes later)

A rule is a declarative operation over the text of a file on the clean pin; **the output of a rule is an ordinary `.ckpatch`** (the layer creates no new way of applying). The MVP implements the schema, validation, accounting in the inventory and the **expected-match counter** as a `verify` check; patch generation by the engine comes later. @status:spec/done

`delta/rules/*.ckrule.json`: `codkitRule: 2`; the metadata dictionary of PROP-003 §5; `target` is the path of an upstream file; `engine` is `"line-ops"` (the only MVP engine: line-wise operations); `expectedMatches` is the expected number of matches of all match operations (actual ≠ expected → the loud error `CK-E-RULE-DRIFT`, exit 1); `ops` are the operations. @status:spec/done

The `line-ops` operations: `{"match": "<exact line>", "action": "comment-out"|"append-after"|"insert-before", "text": "<line>"?}`. `match` is an exact byte match of the whole line (no regular expressions in the MVP); `text` is mandatory for `append-after`/`insert-before`; every inserted line must lie inside a marker block that the rule adds itself (the first operation inserts `codkit:begin`, the last one `codkit:end`). The first candidate for use is the generation of an entry module (§4). M1 refinements: a rule without a single inserted line is illegal (there is nothing to frame with a marker - a schema error); `comment-out` with a `text` field is a refusal; the `contractTests` of a rule may be empty (guard tests are mandatory only for overlay/resource/hide/removed). M1 relaxation (polygon PG-09): with a single operation the requirements of the envelope ("the first insertion carries `codkit:begin`, the last one `codkit:end`") converge on one insertion, and `text` is then multi-line (the whole marker block as one value, lines separated by `\n`); "one inserted line per operation" is the norm for multi-operation rules, but not an absolute. @status:spec/done
8. hide - switch off without deleting

Implemented by the upper layers: a setting or a `when` context (any setting is the context key `config.<id>`), not including a module in our own entry, `deregisterViews`/`deregisterViewContainer` (the public APIs of the registries), overriding a configuration default (`registerDefaultConfigurations`). Every hide intervention is an entry of the `hide` category in the corresponding layer plus a **mandatory** guard test (an intervention outside the zone of the compiler). A patch for the sake of a hide is a last resort with a justification. @status:spec/done
9. New files in the upstream zone

By the hierarchy, new files live in own. An add-file patch (PROP-004 §4) is admissible only when the file must lie in the upstream zone (for example a resource with a specific path); each one carries a justification in `reason` and an inventory entry. `save` creates an add-file patch only under the explicit flag `--allow-new-file <path>` (otherwise `CK-E-NEW-FILE-IN-UPSTREAM-ZONE` with a hint to move it into own). @status:spec/done
10. removed-registry — delta/removed.json

A registry of deliberate removals (a dependency, a file, a registration, a setting) that cannot be expressed by a deleting patch (deletion is forbidden): `{"codkitRemoved":1,"entries":[{"id","kind":"file|dependency|registration|setting","target":"<path|package name|registration id|setting key>","how":"<which layer implements the switch-off>","owner","reason","link","pin","contractTests":[…]}]}`. @status:spec/done

`verify` requires that every entry has a guard test and that the guard test checks that what was removed has not come back; otherwise upstream silently brings the removal back at an upgrade. @status:spec/done
11. Linter and hygiene for the own directory
Tombstone (PROP-016 split, 2026-09-09): moved to spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-002#OWN-LINT-TARGET; the address stays for citations. @status:spec/done

The set of interventions made to wire in own code is limited to the entry graft and only those build/hygiene registries that the current fork/pin actually requires. Its size does not grow with the volume of own code; empty or stale artifacts are forbidden. The target names and their number are checked at upgrade, not baked in from a consumer tree. @status:spec/done
12. Files delivered by Codkit into own, and the hook-patch budget

The set of own files **delivered by Codkit**: the notice file `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` (in any own directory) and any path whose first segment is `codkit/` (the runtime library, PROP-015). They are not product code: they are not covered by the units of the manifest (`OWN-MANIFEST`), they are not edited in the product (`save` refuses with `CK-E-DELIVERED-EDIT` when the tree differs from the delta under `src/vs/<ownDirName>/codkit/**`), they are updated only by Codkit commands (`standards load`, `runtime load`), and their drift from the shipped version is `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` in `verify` and `runtime check`. In the inventory the library is one synthetic entry `CK-codkit-runtime`. `isDeliveredByCodkit(relative)` is the only function that answers the question of whether a file is delivered; the former list `NOT_OWN_CODE` is a special case of it. @status:spec/done

The root `codkit/` inside own belongs to Codkit (PROP-015 `RT-DIRECTORY-IS-CODKIT`, PROP-014 `STD-NOTICE-SCOPE-BY-PATHS`): an own unit or a `serviceOverrides` entry with a root or a module inside `codkit/` is `CK-E-OWN-UNDER-CODKIT` in `verify`; otherwise product files would fall under a foreign licence by the text of the notice. @status:spec/done

A patch with `type = hook` in the `.ckpatch` header is a graft: between the markers (over all blocks of the patch in the file together, PROP-004 `MR-SEVERAL-BLOCKS-ONE-ID`) there are no more than three lines of code (empty lines and `//` comment lines do not count) and at least one line between the markers - any line, a comment line included - contains a path with the segment `<ownDirName>/` (usually an import or a call of own code; a comment naming an own path counts too: a graft may only say where it delegates); otherwise `verify` gives `CK-E-HOOK-TOO-LARGE` with the name of the patch and the number of lines (the standard `MI-PATCH-IS-A-GRAFT`: the logic lives in own, the patch only creates a seam). The budget is a constant; it can be widened only by editing this rule. @status:spec/done

codkit PROP-006: Apply metadata, locking, inventory
1. Apply metadata: the cache + the mark (the truth is the tree itself)

**The truth about the applied state is the tree itself**: the generated branch, its tip and the commit trailers (`Codkit-Patchset-Commit`, `Codkit-Upstream-Pin`). The metadata is a cache that can always be thrown away; losing it means «apply from scratch» and never an interactive question. @status:spec/done

**The delta fingerprint** (`deltaFingerprint`) is the hex sha256 of a canonical string: for every file under `delta/` recursively (the paths sorted by their UTF-8 bytes) — the line `<path-from-the-patchset-root>
<sha256 of the content in hex>
`; plus the closing lines `pin <pin.sha>
schema 1
`. Own code enters through its own files under `delta/own/`. @status:spec/done

**The identity of the tree** (`treeId`) is the hex sha256 of the realpath of the root of the tree (the normalized absolute path after the symlinks are resolved), its first 16 hex characters. @status:spec/done

**The cache in the patch set** is the file `.codkit/trees/<treeId>.json`: `codkitTreeCache: 1`; `treePath` (the realpath, for diagnostics); `treeRepoAnchor` (the confirmed `upstreamAnchorCommit`); `pinSha`; `deltaFingerprint`; `branchTip` (the SHA of the tip of the generated branch); `updatedAt` (ISO). @status:spec/done

**The mark in the tree** is the file `codkit/applied.json` in the per-worktree git directory (`git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`; in an ordinary tree — `<tree>/.git/codkit/applied.json`, in a linked worktree — the per-worktree directory, not the common dir: every worktree has a mark of its own; it survives `clean -fdx` and is invisible to status): `{"codkitTreeMark":1,"pinSha":…,"deltaFingerprint":…,"branchTip":…,"ownFingerprint":…}`. The fields `ownFingerprint` (the hash of the own subtree at the moment of the `load`) and `ownFiles` (a map `path → sha256` of the own files at the moment of the `load`; added by the M0 implementation) are needed by the guard to tell apart, file by file, «the patch set was edited» / «the tree was edited» / «both sides were edited» (`##PATCHSET-SIDE-EDIT-RULE` PROP-008 §4). The fields of Phase 7 of the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign (decisions D16/D17, S0.9): `artifacts` — a map `path → sha256` of all the `delta/` files outside `delta/own/**` at the moment of the load (one traversal shared with the fingerprint — `deltaFiles()`; excluding own is the single filter `deltaArtifactMap`, and the writer of the mark and the reader of the check both go through it) — and `patchSetCommit`, the patch-set commit the load represented (`sha` | `dirty` | `none`; the value is the same one the `Codkit-Patchset-Commit` trailer of the built commits carries — the mark answers the case of an empty patch set, where there is no trailer). Both are `.optional()` in the schema: a mark written before them is read without them, and the shift check then honestly answers «unknown» (R13, PROP-008 `##PATCHSET-MOVED-RULE`); every write of the mark writes both. On a read-only mounted tree the mark is not written (a write error into `.git` is not fatal, the warning `CK-W-MARK-RO`). @status:impl/done

**The consumed tree commits** — `refs/codkit/consumed/<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<short7>` → the former HEAD of the tree: the write `recordConsumedRef` (the module `lib/treeCommits.ts`, the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign, decision D6) is performed under the lock of the common repository — the refs are shared by all the worktrees of the repository (PROP-008 `##GENERATED-REF-WORKTREE-PREFLIGHT`). They are created when the tree commits are consumed by an extraction (the `save` of the later phases) or discarded explicitly (`load --discard`). The refs are diagnostics, not the truth (`##TREE-IS-TRUTH`): only `gc` cleans them (decision D22), they are never touched by hand; they are reachable from any worktree of the repository. @status:impl/done

**The transaction file of the two-way `sync`** is `.codkit/sync-transaction.json` in the root of the patch set (the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign, Phase 8, decision D20; the module `lib/syncTransaction.ts`, the algorithm is PROP-008 §5a `##SYNC-TRANSACTION`). It is written by `writeContainedFileExclusive` before the first mutation of the run (a second start over a live record is impossible by construction), atomically rewritten after every atom (a patch-set commit — with the trailer `Codkit-Sync-Transaction: <id>` — and the consumed ref are appended to the record) and removed after the last one. It carries: both HEADs, `markSnapshot` (the mark as it was found), `dirtyBefore`, the `hash-object -w` snapshots of everything the run will overwrite, `patchsetCommits`, `consumedRef`, `conflicts` — `[{path, materialized}]` (Phase 8b: the sha256 of the written markers, or `null` — the merge did not reach the file; `status` prints `conflicts: N` from this field and `--continue` checks completeness against it). While the file exists: `load`/`save`/`sync` (step 0 of every call of the engines) refuse with `CK-E-SYNC-IN-PROGRESS` (exit 1) and `status` prints `sync in progress: <id>, conflicts: N`. The ownership protocol is its own (F24): it is touched neither by hand nor by `gc` (D22 lists it and explains why); a refusal without a single write removes the file itself (the proof is a comparison of the snapshots and of HEAD, not a guess), while a refusal or a crash after a write leaves it for the recovery by `--abort`/`--continue` (Phase 8b, D21; the audit of `--abort` and the restoration from the snapshots are PROP-008 §5a). A broken or foreign file is fail closed: a refusal, not a guess. @status:impl/done

**The classes of `codkit gc`** (the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign, Phase 9, decision D22; the module `lib/gc.ts`, the command is PROP-007 `##CMD-GC`). gc takes the lock of the tree, prints the plan — every candidate with its class and its remove/keep action, the kept ones included — and removes **only** a closed list of classes: `refs/codkit/consumed/*` older than N days beyond the last n (`--keep-consumed n`, default 5; `--older-than days`, default 30; the refs are shared by all the worktrees, hence the removal under the lock of the common repository); `.codkit/tmp/*` — the scratch of runs whose `finally` did not execute (a per-tree scratch `<treeId>.index|.blob` whose lock owner is alive stays); a tree lock with a dead owner (the pid in the file is not alive; the release goes through the acquisition protocol with a choice of generation, not a bare unlink; a stale lock of **its own** tree is released by the acquisition itself, as it is today — ##LOCK-MECHANISM §2, and gc names that release in the plan); a `.codkit/trees/<id>.json` whose `treePath` does not exist; `.codkit/out/*`. **It never touches**: `.codkit/locks/daemon-*` and `.codkit/build/*` (their own protocol of a provable owner, REPAIR-011; the cleanup of the daemon logs is DEF-9), the transactions and the receipts — `.codkit/sync-transaction.json` (##SYNC-TRANSACTION-FILE), `.codkit/rename-transaction.json`, `.codkit/rename-completions/`, `.codkit/rebase-onto-pin/` — and `.codkit/pending/*`: gc only lists them with an explanation of why they are kept. It does not touch the Git objects of the tree (a `git gc` on the tree is a human decision). `--dry-run` prints the same plan without removing anything; `--json` gives `data.plan`, `data.removed`, `data.kept`. Directories are not cleaned blindly: every entry is classified by its name and removed one at a time. @status:impl/done

**The comparison rule (a fast no-op `load`)** — it is allowed only when ALL of the conditions are true: the cache exists ∧ the `pinSha`/`deltaFingerprint` of the cache equal the current ones ∧ the branch `codkit/applied/<pin.tag>` exists in the tree ∧ its tip == the `branchTip` of the cache ∧ the HEAD of the tree points at it ∧ (the mark is absent ∨ the mark matches). Any mismatch → a full bring-up from scratch. A stale cache cannot be taken for the truth by construction. @status:spec/done

Multiple trees are supported: the cache records are keyed by `treeId`; concurrent access is protected by the lock (§2); a tree swapped under a live cache must lead to a full re-application (scenario S15 of FEAT-002). @status:spec/done
2. Locking

The file `.codkit/locks/<treeId>.lock` in the patch set is created with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` and holds `{pid, startedAt, command}`. Every writing command takes it; `status`/`where`/`inventory` work without the lock (the read-only path). A stale lock (the process with that pid does not exist) is released automatically with a warning. A second process gets exit 2 `CK-E-LOCKED` with the pid and a hint. `EACCES`/`EPERM`/`EROFS` while creating the lock is an environment refusal 2 `CK-E-TREE-READONLY` that demands a separate writable `.codkit` mount; the source patch set may stay read-only in that case. A shared tree in CI is additionally protected by the fingerprint (a mark mismatch → a full re-application). @status:spec/done
3. The inventory

The inventory is **generated** by the tool from the `delta/**` artifacts and the marker annotation; it is not kept by hand and is not committed as a source of truth. The output is `.codkit/out/inventory.json` (+ `--md` for a human); the generated version and its diff between two states are published into the CI artifacts and for the review (we review the changes of the inventory, not the patch files). @status:spec/done
The schema (`codkitInventory: 2`): @status:spec/done
`entries` are sorted by `id`; the metrics are derived; the serialization is deterministic. @status:spec/done

The main metric is `patchAndRuleCount` per subsystem (rewrite-rule + patch). Every completed cycle writes a snapshot of the metrics into its committed journal; the aggregated time series is a derived report and requires no separate CSV in the tool repository. @status:spec/done

Routing: the subsystem of an intervention → the set of tests and the owner (the owners map) — from the inventory; the review checklist of the cycle is generated from it as well (it is not hard-coded). @status:spec/done
4. Building the inventory
Read and validate against the schemas: all the `.ckpatch` (their headers), the overlays, the resource map, the rules, `patchset.delta.json`, `removed.json`, `owners.json`. @status:spec/done
For every artifact — an inventory entry: `subsystem` = the second component of the id; `files` = the target or targets of the artifact; `artifact` = the path of the artifact file. @status:spec/done
The metrics are aggregates over the entries; the serialization is deterministic (the entries are sorted by id). @status:spec/done
The speed requirement: a build over the full volume takes seconds; the patches are parsed without touching the tree; the tree is needed only by the cross-checks (§5–6). @status:spec/done
5. «Every hunk inside a marker» — the matching

The input: the patch P of the file F; the content of F in the **target state** (the pin + P — computed by applying P to the content of the pin in memory with our own implementation of `applyUnified` with an exact context match: there are no shifts on our own pin — by construction the patch is regenerated against the pin). @status:spec/done

The consistency «marker ↔ artifact»: the id of every block in the target state of the file = the id of the patch of that file (for entry-module — an id from the list of the patches of the layer); the id of the patch must be present among the blocks. A violation is `CK-E-MARKER-ARTIFACT-MISMATCH`. @status:spec/done

An add-file patch (the whole file consists of added lines) is not subject to the «every hunk inside a marker» check — there are no upstream lines to protect; only the validity of the markers of the file and the consistency «block ↔ artifact id» apply to it (a clarification of M0). @status:impl/done

Clarifications of the «neutralization by commenting out» (the M0 implementation): the comment wrapper is an ORDINARY comment of the language (the marker form minus the word `codkit:`: `// `, `/* … */`, `<!-- … -->`, `# `), and the closing half is mandatory for CSS/HTML; the comparison of the text trims the leading spaces and tabs on both sides and the trailing ones on the wrapper; the commented-out copy must lie in the SAME hunk as the removal. A `-`/`+` pair that edits an upstream line in place (rather than commenting it out) is `CK-E-DELETES-UPSTREAM-LINE` by construction (the rule `##MR-FUNCTIONAL-ONLY` of PROP-004: upstream lines are commented out, not edited) — the most frequent expected signal of this check, and not a false one. @status:impl/done

The semantics of `\ No newline at end of file` in `applyUnified`: after a `-` line the marker asserts the state of the pin (a mismatch is the refusal `CK-E-ARTIFACT-BROKEN`), after a `+` line it sets the state of the result, and after a context line it does both. @status:impl/done
6. «No interventions outside the inventory» (completeness)

The input: the tree in the applied state (the tip of the generated branch) and the pin. The algorithm: `git diff --name-status <pin.sha> <branchTip>` → the list of the changed paths. Every path must be explained by exactly one source: the own directory (`src/vs/<ownDirName>/**` — only in the CI/publish mode, locally own is not in the commits), a patch with that target path, an overlay target, a resource-map target. An unexplained path → `CK-E-UNTRACKED-INTERVENTION`. Conversely: an artifact whose target is not changed in the diff → `CK-E-STALE-ARTIFACT` (an empty patch, for instance) — with the M1 reservation for overlays: a local `load` materializes an overlay through the dev channel only, so overlay targets DO explain a changed path but are NOT obliged to be present in the diff. The absence of the generated branch is not a failure of completeness but a skipped check with the warning «run codkit load first» (verify works otherwise). @status:spec/done

The entries of the removed registry are NOT inventory entries (the kind is not a layer): they do not enter `entries`, but they do enter the requirements of the guard coverage (`contractCoverage.requiredTotal` may exceed the number of guard-obliged entries) and are checked by verify (a clarification of M1). @status:impl/done
codkit PROP-007: CLI commands - contracts
1. Rules common to every command

Invocation is the installed `bin/codkit` or `bin/codkit.ps1` from any cwd. `npm run codkit -- …` is allowed only as a developer entry from toolRoot; the patch set carries no copy of the runtime. @status:spec/done

A command that uses the patch set prints `patches: /abs/path (source: flag|env|settings)`; a command that uses the tree also prints `fork tree: /abs/path (source: flag|env|settings)`. Under `--json` all three roots live only in the top-level `roots.tool|patches|fork` of schema 2; the command `data` may repeat the subject of the answer, but it does not replace `roots`. @status:impl/done
Global flags: `--patches-dir <path>`, `--fork-dir <path>`, `--json`, `--ci`, `--verbose`. Both path flags take part in an independent flag → env → settings precedence. @status:spec/done

Exit codes: `0` success; `1` a check did not pass (markers, inventory, the delta did not apply, a red test, a guard); `2` a startup/environment error (no git-lfs, an unreachable pin, no permissions, a broken config); `3` the cycle has to stop (a human is needed: a conflict, a design decision). An internal error (a bug) is 2 as well, with a request to attach the `--verbose` log. @status:spec/done
The main path is non-interactive; there are no stdin questions. Every error prints a `hint:` - what to do (PROP-012 §2). @status:spec/done

Running any command again after it completed successfully is a no-op or the same result (the exceptions are stated). An interruption (SIGINT/kill) leaves no partially applied state that the next command would not recognize: every command begins by validating the actual state, not a cache. @status:spec/done
2. codkit where

Print toolRoot and the independently resolved patchesDir/forkDir with their source and exists. Neither external directory has to exist or to be configured; `where` does not read `codkit.json` and has no side effects. `data`: `{patches: null|{path,source,exists}, fork: null|{path,source,exists}}`; the top-level `roots` holds the same roots plus tool. Codes: 0, except for broken settings or a disjoint-roots violation - 2. @status:spec/done
3. codkit check-tree

The identity/fitness check (PROP-008 §2) without changes. The `--require-clean` flag demands cleanliness (dirt → 1). The output is a table of `ok|fail` checks plus the first error with its hint. Codes: 0 fit; 1 unfit but repairable with codkit commands (the wrong pin, for instance - hint "run codkit load"); 2 fatally unfit (not a git repository, not upstream, no lfs). @status:spec/done
4. codkit clone [--from url]

Clone the tree into an empty/absent directory and check out the pin. **Local only**: under `--ci` it is an immediate exit 2 `CK-E-NET-FORBIDDEN`. Preconditions: the path is resolved; the directory is absent or empty; a source is given - `publishRemoteUrl` from the config or `--from <url>`. Steps: `git clone --no-checkout <url> <path>`; `git checkout --detach <pin.sha>`; when there are LFS paths - `git lfs install --local` and `git lfs pull` (the network is allowed - the command is a local one); a final `check-tree`. Idempotency: a non-empty directory with a fit tree → the message "already present", exit 0; non-empty with foreign content → 2. Cloning happens only through this command or through an explicit `load --clone-if-missing` (never as a side effect: a typo in a path must not start a download of gigabytes). @status:impl/done

**Shallow cloning is dropped** (the M0 implementation): the anchored origin check `##ID-CHECK-ORIGIN` requires the root commit of the history to be reachable, and a shallow tree does not have it by construction - "shallow is admissible as long as the pin is reachable" from an early edition did not survive implementation: such a tree would fail `CK-E-NOT-UPSTREAM` forever, on every command. If a cheaper clone is ever needed, that is a separate decision with a different origin-check scheme. @status:impl/done
5. codkit load […] and the two-way codkit sync […]

A tombstone (Phase 1 of the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign, 2026-09-06): the one-way `sync` command was renamed to `load`, and its contract moved to the `CMD-LOAD` anchor of this section. The anchor itself is neither renamed nor deleted - the address of a cited anchor never changes (NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR). The second life of the name: since Phase 8 of that campaign (2026-09-06, decision D15) `codkit sync` is a real two-way command, and the live contract is `CMD-SYNC-TWO-WAY` below. Between Phase 1 and Phase 8 the name was a stub that exited 2 ("renamed to codkit load"), so that scripts carrying the old meaning would break loudly; an alias is deliberately refused now as well. @status:spec/done

**The two-way command** (Phase 8 of the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign, decisions D15/D16/D19/D20; the algorithm is PROP-008 §5a). `codkit sync [--squash] [--commit] [--message m] [--discard] [--fresh] [--dry-run] [--abort] [--continue]`: one command that extracts the work of the tree (as `save` does, replay of commits and `--squash` included) and delivers the patchset shift (as `load` does), by rule D16 for each file: the tree only → extract; patchset only → apply the patchset version, and overwriting the target during the rebuild is explained; both sides → **a diff3 materialization** (Phase 8b, D19): the 3-way merge is laid down as markers inside the tree file under a live transaction, exit 1 `CK-E-BOTH-SIDES-EDITED` with the list of files and both roads - a human resolves the markers (as in the resolve phase of the cycle), then `codkit sync --continue` finishes the run and `codkit sync --abort` returns everything to how it was (PROP-008 `##SYNC-CONFLICT-DIFF3`, `##SYNC-ABORT`, `##SYNC-CONTINUE`); there is no automatic merge. An own conflict on both sides stays the "choose a side" recipe (own code has no marker blocks), and under `--discard` so does the uncommitted both-sides part - `--continue` is extraction, not discarding. The D17 lineage is checked as in `save`: not an ancestor of the patchset HEAD → `CK-E-PATCHSET-MOVED`; a mark without an artifact map → the same refusal with the hint "run codkit load once" (R13). Order: the tree lock → a live transaction → `CK-E-SYNC-IN-PROGRESS` → check-tree/ref-preflight → D8 → D17 → classification → both sides → a refusal **before the first write** (no transaction file, no moved ref, not a byte) → `--dry-run` (print the classification, exit 0, nothing written) → write the transaction → the save half → the rebuild = the load half → the consumed ref → the mark → lift the transaction. `--discard` means the same as it does for `load` (D11): tree commits are discarded on purpose (a consumed ref), while the guard goes on guarding edits; under `--ci` it is exit 2. Nothing moved on either side and there is no transaction → the answer of the load engine, usually "up to date", exit 0, without a transaction. `--abort`/`--continue` are the recovery of a stopped synchronization (Phase 8b, D21): no record - an honest exit 2; the extraction flags (`--squash`/`--commit`/`--message`/`--fresh`) apply to `--continue`, while `--discard`/`--dry-run`, and any flag at all with `--abort`, are exit 2. Codes: 0; 1 (`CK-E-BOTH-SIDES-EDITED` - materialized unresolved markers, "the merge never reached the file" and an own conflict; `CK-E-PATCHSET-MOVED`; `CK-E-SYNC-IN-PROGRESS` - a live record and the refusals of `--abort` over someone else's work; the inheritance from `save`: markers/Cause/a forbidden target/a deletion); 2 (the environment, `--ci`+`--discard`, a recovery with no record or with foreign flags). @status:impl/done

Bring the tree to the pin and apply the delta (the algorithm is PROP-008 §3). Preconditions: the config is valid; the tree passes `check-tree`; the generated branch is not shared with a sibling worktree (`CK-E-WORKTREE-REF-SHARED`, exit 2 - the preflight runs BEFORE the dirt check, ruling D7 of 2026-09-06); **there are no unextracted edits and no tree commits** (the guard of PROP-008 §4: edits are exit 1 `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` with the list of files and the hint "run codkit save, or codkit status; codkit load --discard drops tree commits deliberately"; tree commits are the same code, "N commit(s) in the fork tree since the last codkit apply are not in patchset yet"; HEAD off the branch while foreign commits exist is `CK-E-TREE-HEAD`, exit 1). `--fresh` is the "from scratch" mode: a reset to the pin plus a cleanup of untracked paths by the whitelist before the delta is applied (PROP-011 §4); a known materialization of overlay targets is replaced by the same run (PROP-005 §5 `##OVERLAY-KNOWN-MATERIALIZATION`, PROP-008 §4). `--dry-run` is a forecast: the full apply cycle in memory/index without changing working files or refs; it prints classified outcomes (the report format is the one `cycle` uses); `forecast` uses it. `--discard` (decision D11, Phase 6 of the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign) sacrifices the third half of the guard **by name**: tree commits above the last generated tip are discarded on purpose, by the very mechanism the guard used to keep from being used blindly - an ordinary rebuild of the branch (the commits stop being reachable from HEAD) plus the consumed ref `refs/codkit/consumed/…` (PROP-006 §1 `##CONSUMED-REFS`, which only `gc` cleans) and the message `discarded N commit(s): <first>..<last>; kept as <ref>`. The ref is written **before** the rebuild, under the lock of the shared repository, right after the precondition "the foreign set has not changed since the check, otherwise `CK-E-INTERNAL` before any ref or file moves": unlike `save`, the patch set has replayed nothing here, and the ref is the only keeper of the line (the parent session's ruling of 2026-09-06: a crash between the ref and the rebuild leaves the ref on commits that are still alive - "a discard begun and not finished", which loses nothing and names itself; `save` has the reverse order - there the patch set is the keeper already). The bounds of the flag: the guard goes on guarding file edits and own code (mixed dirt is an ordinary refusal), and the anomaly of a rewritten history and HEAD off the branch as well (`CK-E-TREE-HEAD`); without tree commits it is a no-op, exit 0 with an info line; under `--ci` it is exit 2 `CK-E-CONFIG`: a non-interactive run does not decide on its own to throw away someone else's work. Side effects (not under dry-run): the branch `codkit/applied/<pin.tag>` is recreated (when the fingerprint changed), the tree HEAD is on its tip, own code is copied, `product.overrides.json` is written, the effective `info/exclude` is restored, and the mark and the cache are updated. A repeat with no changes is a fast no-op (the comparison rule of PROP-006 §1) that prints `up to date`. Codes: 0; 1 (the guard; an artifact did not apply - on its own pin that means a broken artifact `CK-E-ARTIFACT-BROKEN`, and which one is printed); 2 (the environment). The former name: between Phase 1 and Phase 8 of the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign `codkit sync` was a usage error without an envelope (exit 2, "renamed to codkit load"), so that scripts carrying the old meaning would break loudly; since Phase 8 the name belongs to the two-way command - `##CMD-SYNC-TWO-WAY` above. @status:spec/done

**The extension of `--discard` (decision D-S3-5, confirmed by the owner on 2026-09-08, option 2):** only together with `--fresh` does the `--discard` flag drop, besides tree commits, the working-tree edits of **tracked upstream files without marker blocks** (today `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE`, a manual `git checkout` in the managed tree): the plan prints every such path as a `discard <path>` line before the first write, the actual discarding matches the plan one for one (R14), and the file returns to the pin plus the delta. Never discarded: files with marker blocks (an unextracted intervention may live there - `save` is for it; such a file stays a `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` refusal even with `--discard`), own code and own extensions (their side of the truth is `save`/`load` per PROP-008), and untracked files outside the cleanup lists. Without `--fresh` the `--discard` flag still touches tree commits only. The reason: a build of the tree rewrites a tracked file with a build artifact that is byte-for-byte indistinguishable from a human edit, and returning to dev mode must not require a git command typed by hand in a managed tree. Rejected: a separate flag (a second name for the same "sacrifice by name" gesture), and a list of the known side effects of a build (it cannot be kept current across pins). The norm of the release protocol: packaging preferably runs in a throwaway clone, as `publish` does, so that the dev tree receives no build artifacts. @status:spec/done
6. codkit status

Print: the pin; the tip of the branch; tree commits outside patchset - the line `tree commits not in patchset: N` plus up to 20 `<short> <subject>` lines (`data.treeCommits: {base, count, commits}`); with N>0 the `reload needed …` line is NOT printed - moving to patchset is exactly what would destroy those commits, and the question is addressed to `save`; the currency of the branch (up to date / reload needed) is printed when N=0; **the line `loaded from patchset commit: <sha|dirty|none|unknown>`** and, when the delta has shifted away from the mark, **`patchset moved since load: N artifact(s)`** with the list (the data of the manual `CK-E-PATCHSET-MOVED` recipe; `data.loadedFrom`, `data.patchsetMoved`; the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign, decision D10, Phase 7); own code - N changed files (the tree against `delta/own/`); own extensions - the line `own extensions: D declared, P path(s) differ between tree and patchset` with the list (PROP-005 `OWN-EXTENSION-UNIT`; `data.ownExtensions: {declared, differing}`), and their `extensions/<name>/` directories in the tree are own, not upstream dirt; **a stranded materialization** - an untracked `extensions/<name>/` directory of the tree that no declaration covers and that does not exist on the pin (the declaration was withdrawn, and a `load` without `--fresh` does not touch the directory - PROP-005 `OWN-EXTENSION-STRANDED`): the line `own extensions: … , S stranded materialization(s)` with the list of paths and the hint `codkit load --fresh removes it`; `data.ownExtensions.stranded: [path…]`; exit code 1 (there is something to remove); upstream files - M changed (dirt against HEAD, outside the own directory and outside the declared extensions), K marker blocks in them, the validity of the markers (pairing/id); uncommitted `delta/` changes in patchset while the tree is clean (a divergence in the direction of truth). Read-only; it works even while the lock is held. Codes: 0 clean/consistent; 1 there is something unextracted (edits, own code or tree commits) or the markers are invalid (an informational command - code 1 makes it usable in scripts). Time: seconds on a full tree. @status:spec/done
7. codkit save [path…] [--commit] [--message m] [--squash] [--allow-new-file path]

Extract the work (the algorithm is PROP-008 §4). Without arguments it takes every changed file; with paths it is targeted.
