`gen` is a namespace: a bare `codkit gen` and an unknown subcommand give the list of subcommands and exit 2; the subcommands are `feature` and `brand`; only patchesDir is needed (`configMode: 'none'`). Flags: `--title <text>` (a value), `--setting`, `--cold` (boolean), `--holder`, `--license`, `--year` (values, as for `license annotate`), `--header-style line|block`, `--header-file <path>` (values; PROP-015 `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`). @status:spec/done

`codkit gen feature <id> --title <text> [--setting] [--cold] [--holder …] [--license …] [--year …] [--header-style line|block] [--header-file <path>]` is the skeleton of a product feature (PROP-015 §5 `GEN-FEATURE`, `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`, `GEN-TEST-LIVES-WITH-THE-FEATURE`, `GEN-REFUSES-EXISTING`): three files under `delta/own/contrib/<name>/` (the test in the `test/browser/` of the feature), the import line for the composition root and the reminder about the unit. Codes: 0; 1 - `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS`; 2 - `CK-E-GEN-ID`, a missing `--title`, incompatible header flags, an unreadable `--header-file`, the environment. `--json`: `data: {id, files:[…], importLine, headerWritten:boolean, headerStyle: "line"|"block"|"file"|null}`. @status:spec/done

`codkit gen brand [--holder …] [--license …] [--year …] [--header-style line|block] [--header-file <path>]` is the scaffold of the brand table (the header flags are the same as for `gen feature`, PROP-015 `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`) `delta/own/common/brand.ts`, plus the printing of the hook text for `_format` with its reminders (PROP-015 `GEN-BRAND`). Codes: 0; 1 - `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS`; 2 - the environment. `--json`: `data: {file, hookText, reminders:[…]}`. @status:spec/done
22. Command roster

`where`, `check-tree`, `clone`, `load`, `status`, `save`, `sync`, `gc`, `marker new`, `reresolve`, `inventory`, `verify`, `overlay apply|check`, `build up|down|status|errors`, `cycle start|continue|status|restart`, `forecast`, `rebase-onto-pin`, `ci`, `publish`, `hooks install|check`, `imageset`, `license check|annotate|notices`, `standards load|check|license`, `runtime load|check`, `gen feature|brand`. Planned (PROP-016): `types`. @status:spec/done

`codkit types` - the contract of the verb lives in `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#CMD-TYPES` and is not restated here: it prints the registered types, their package and version and the capability matrix, needs no patch set and writes nothing. Two more facts of PROP-016 bind the roster to the types: every verb keeps its name, flags and exit codes and names the type where it matters (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-VERBS-UNIVERSAL`), and a verb whose capability the type does not declare refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` before any write (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-CAPABILITY-REFUSAL`). @status:spec/plan
codkit PROP-008: The engines — the resolver, identity, load, save, 3-way, renames, the cause

A "file at the pin" is always read from the git objects of the tree: `git show <pin.sha>:<path>` — without the network and without a checkout. Every git call goes through the `gitx` wrapper with an isolated environment (PROP-002 §2). @status:spec/done
1. The resolver of the three roots

toolRoot is computed from the URL of the installed entrypoint and has the source `install`. The external roots are resolved independently and return either `null` or `{path, source:"flag"|"env"|"settings", exists, warning}`. @status:spec/done

Spaces and Unicode in a path are allowed. An existing target must be a directory. Canonicalization of the existing prefix closes the bypass of the nested-root guard through a symlink even for a target that does not exist yet. On Windows a path longer than 200 characters gives a warning about long-path support. There is no sibling/default/config fallback. @status:spec/done
2. The check of the identity and the fitness of the tree
Input: path. Output: the list of check results; the first fatal one stops. @status:spec/done

`path` exists and `git -C path rev-parse --absolute-git-dir --show-toplevel` succeeds and returns a toplevel (a bare repository without a working tree is unfit) — otherwise 2 (`CK-E-NOT-A-REPO`; hint: `codkit clone` or check the path). Refined during the M0 implementation: this call also gives both paths the later checks need. @status:impl/done

Origin: `git -C path cat-file -e <upstreamAnchorCommit>` — the anchor commit is present in the objects (by reachability, not by the name of a remote: remote names are only a hint). Otherwise 2 (`CK-E-NOT-UPSTREAM`). @status:spec/done

The pin is reachable: `git cat-file -e <pin.sha>` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <anchor> <pin.sha>`. Otherwise 2 (`CK-E-PIN-UNREACHABLE`; the hint is the exact fetch command the human/CI has to run; codkit itself never fetches under `--ci`, and locally it does not fetch without an explicit command). @status:spec/done

git-lfs (generalized during the M0 implementation — with no hard-wired paths): if the tree holds LFS-tracked paths (`git lfs ls-files -n` is non-empty; when git-lfs itself is absent this is decided by grepping `filter=lfs` over `git show <pin>:.gitattributes`), then `git lfs version` must succeed AND a sample of up to the first 3 paths from `git lfs ls-files -n` must not begin with `version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1` (the marker of a pointer file); a violation → 2 (`CK-E-LFS`; pointer files must not be taken for the delta). A tree without LFS paths (fixtures) passes the check vacuously, with an info line. At the real pin LFS paths exist (~98 files of the copilot cache) — the contract of the environment is preserved. The sample reads the files of the **working tree**, not the git objects: for an LFS path the stored blob is the pointer itself, so `git show` always looks like a pointer. @status:spec/done

Permissions: `fs.access(path, W_OK)` and a trial write+delete of a file in `<path>/.git/codkit/` (except in read-only modes, where the command only reads). The error comes before the work begins, not in the middle of an apply; the code is `CK-E-TREE-READONLY` (PROP-012 §2). @status:spec/done
Cleanliness (only when the command requires it): `git status --porcelain` is empty, the excluded own directory taken into account. @status:spec/done
3. load: bringing the tree to the pin and building the generated branch
Notation: `B` = the name of the branch `codkit/applied/<pin.tag>`. @status:spec/done

`writeTreeHook()` — the installation of the reminder pre-commit hook of the tree (the norm PROP-012 §5 `##FORK-TREE-PRECOMMIT-HOOK`; campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decision D9): in an ordinary tree (per-worktree admin dir == common dir) it writes only into the repository's own administrative path — `hooks/pre-commit` under the absolute git directory of the tree (`--absolute-git-dir`) — with our script (shebang `sh`, portable), which NEVER rejects a commit: without `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1` it prints the reminder (on the branch `codkit/applied/*` — the work reaches patchset only through codkit save/sync; off the branch while the branch exists — `save` will refuse until the return `git switch codkit/applied/<tag>`, the concrete tag substituted into the text at installation), with the variable it stays silent; on a read-only mount a write error is not fatal (as with the mark, `CK-W-MARK-RO`). The effective path `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path hooks/pre-commit` is deliberately NOT used for the installation: it follows `core.hooksPath`, and that one may point outside the administrative directory of the repository (a per-user or site-wide set of hooks) — codkit has the authority neither to follow that config nor to write there. While a configured `core.hooksPath` stands, git runs the configured hook and not the administrative copy: the copy is installed all the same (a file of the repository itself, restored by every load and becoming a live reminder as soon as the config is removed), but `writeTreeHook()` returns false and issues an explicit fail-soft warning (`CK-W-MARK-RO`) that the reminder does not print while that config stands. The effective path is resolved in TWO scopes (REPAIR-006): in isolation (it sees the local config of the repository) and with the machine config (`machineConfig` — the single exception to the isolation of PROP-002, a read-only path resolution): a global/system `core.hooksPath` is caught too. A failure of the resolution (for example, a local `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` makes `--git-path hooks/*` fatal) is NOT counted as proof of a printing reminder: `writeTreeHook()` returns false with the warning "it cannot be proven which hook git runs" — an honest "does not print" instead of a silent "prints" (a false-positive active guard — a finding of REPAIR-006; the class is the same, the promise is now softer, the honesty is not). Ownership: the hook carries the marker `# codkit-hook v1` under the shebang (like the patch-set hooks, PROP-007 §19); a FOREIGN `hooks/pre-commit` file is neither overwritten nor chained — a warning and false, the bytes untouched (a finding of REPAIR-006); the exact bytes of a hook written by codkit before the marker was introduced are recognized as our own and updated. In a linked worktree the hook is NOT installed, neither into the shared common dir nor at the old appended path: `--git-path hooks/...` resolves into the shared common dir, and the reminder would speak in the name of the branch of one tree in every sibling worktree of the repository, including trees codkit does not manage; `writeTreeHook()` returns false and issues an explicit fail-soft warning that the reminder is unavailable in this tree (the protection is the refusal of `load`/`save` over foreign commits, not the hook). The single rule for the administrative paths of the tree: administrative files are never built by appending a suffix to `--absolute-git-dir` — in a linked worktree it points into the per-worktree directory, which git does not read for these files; `info/exclude` is always asked of git itself through `--git-path` (in an ordinary tree this gives the same `<tree>/.git/...`, in a linked worktree the common dir), and the hook is the single exception to "ask git": its effective `--git-path` follows `core.hooksPath`, so only the repository's own admin path is written, while `--git-path hooks/...` itself is used only to check whether git runs our copy. If the administrative path or the effective location does not resolve, that is a refusal / an unproven reminder, not a fallback to a constructed path. A worktree-scoped hook (`extensions.worktreeConfig` + a per-worktree `core.hooksPath`) is an open architectural item for the owner (PROP-012 §5) and is not authorized here. @status:impl/done

REPAIR-008: the distinction between the normal (`git-dir == common-dir`) and the linked layout itself uses the same platform-aware canonical path equality as the effective hook: Windows slash/case aliases do not create a false linked verdict; a distinct per-worktree path stays linked. Native Windows proof remains open. @status:impl/done

**A branch is an object shared by every worktree of the repository; the movement of the ref is guarded (REPAIR-006).** Git plumbing allows two worktrees on one branch (`symbolic-ref` checks nothing): moving `refs/heads/<generated>` from the second leaves the index/worktree of the first dirty against a HEAD nobody moved. Therefore every mutation/selection of the generated ref (`updateRef()` of step 9 of `load`; the `update-ref` claim AND the `symbolic-ref HEAD` of the cycle — PROP-009 materialize, resume included, where the ref already points at the tip) is performed only as "lock → preflight → mutate": the lock of the shared repository is taken (the hard-link lock of the PROP-006 `##LOCK-MECHANISM` protocol on the file `<common-dir>/codkit/refs.lock`, the directory contained), then a FRESH `git worktree list --porcelain` proves that no OTHER worktree stands on `refs/heads/<branch>` (self exempt; a record without a branch is detached), and only then `update-ref` + `symbolic-ref HEAD`. An inability to obtain the list is a failure of the safety proof (`CK-E-ARTIFACT-BROKEN`), never an empty list / fail-open. A taken branch is `CK-E-WORKTREE-REF-SHARED` (load: exit 2 `unfit`): both trees are named, every ref/index/worktree untouched. The coordination closes the "checked→swapped" race for codkit processes (two patch sets on two worktrees of one repository are serialized by the shared lock too); a foreign `git symbolic-ref` in that microsecond window remains possible — a git-side interlock does not exist, the window is narrowed to lock→mutate under the lock and documented. An extension of the same lock serializes the writes of the shared files of the repository (the worktree-local exclude writes the shared config and the shared `info/exclude` during the migration). @status:impl/done

REPAIR-007: a full load first builds the tip without changing the live tree, then takes the common-repository lock, runs a fresh worktree/ref preflight and holds the lock through the `--fresh` cleanup, update-ref, HEAD/index/worktree move. Not one untracked byte is deleted before a successful preflight. A refusal on a sibling ref preserves the removable sentinel, ref, index tree and HEAD tree exactly. @status:impl/done

The canonical order of the layers of the generated CI/publish history is `patch → own → overlay → resource`; an empty layer is skipped, the order of the rest does not change. An ordinary local `load` keeps the former semantics: `opts.commitOwn=false`, own does not reach the index or the commits of the branch but is copied by the `syncOwnCode()` step after HEAD is moved, and is excluded locally (the rule PROP-005 `##OWN-EXCLUDED-LOCALLY`: in a single repository — a block in the effective `info/exclude`, in a multi-worktree repository — a worktree-local file; the rule of the administrative paths is `##TREE-HOOK-STEP` above); the choice of the dev channel of the overlay does not change either. The alignment of the publish history therefore does not turn local own code into tracked files. @status:spec/done

**The copying of own code** (`syncOwnCode` / `mirrorOwnBack`): a walk over `delta/own/**` and `<tree>/src/vs/<ownDirName>/**`; for every file a comparison of the bytes (the fast filter is the size; on equal sizes — a full comparison of the content; mtime is NOT used as a criterion — false positives on checkout); a difference → a copy (source→destination for `load`, destination→source for `save`); absence in the source → deletion in the destination; empty directories are deleted. Symlinks inside own are forbidden (an error). @status:spec/done

**The mtime requirement**: regenerating the branch changes neither the content nor the mtime of files whose final state did not change (step 2 rewrites only `changed`) — otherwise the watch daemons stage a recompilation storm. The control experiment is P3-S10 (FEAT-001 §6). @status:spec/done
4. save/extract and the drift guard

An interruption between the writing of a patch and the rebuilding of the branch is safe: the next `load`/`save` sees the mismatch of the fingerprint and rebuilds the branch; the artifacts are already correct. @status:spec/done

**The lineage of the tree** (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decision D17): "what the tree was loaded from" = the value of the `Codkit-Patchset-Commit` trailer of the base commit (the upper generated tip of the line; ##TREE-IS-TRUTH — the branch, not the mark), or the field `mark.patchSetCommit` when base = the pin and there are no generated commits at all (an empty patchset at the first load, F19). The value is a 40-hex sha, `dirty` or `none`. `save` (and the future two-way `sync`): a sha → `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> HEAD` in patchset; not an ancestor → exit 1 `CK-E-PATCHSET-MOVED`: "the tree was loaded from patchset commit <sha>, which is not an ancestor of patchset HEAD <sha2>; the tree's work belongs to that state" + the recipe `##PATCHSET-MOVED-RULE`. `dirty`/`none` → a warning and continuation: a state that cannot be named cannot be checked either, but the work of the tree belongs to it all the same. An old mark without the field when base = the pin is a silent skip ("unnamed"): not a value of D17 but an honest "I do not know". Rejected: extracting silently into a foreign branch (the former behaviour after a `git switch` without a `save`). It is switched off only by the flag `skipPatchsetMovedCheck`, together with the byte check (D12/D18). @status:impl/done

**A patchset that moved under a loaded tree is a refusal before the first write** (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, Phase 7, decisions D16/D18; it closes hypothesis H1/S0.7: `CK-E-INTERNAL` AFTER the ref had been moved and the file overwritten). The mark of the tree carries the `artifacts` map — the sha256 of every `delta/` file outside `delta/own/**` (own is covered by `ownFiles`) at the moment of the load (PROP-006 §1 `##TREE-MARK`). Before any write — the mirroring of own and pass 2 of the replay included — `save` compares the **bytes** of the artifacts with the map, not the sha of a commit: any way of returning the same bytes passes. **The scope of the check is the patch layer `delta/patches/**`** (a refinement by the worker of Phase 7 after a red test of the M1 procedure): the overlay/resource/rule/removed layers are authored only in patchset, and their materialization into the tree by the rebuild is the regular flow (`##SAVE-EXTRACTS-TWO-LAYERS`: a hand-written resource artifact between two saves is a documented procedure, not a foreign edit), so refusing on them would return the M1 defect in the shape of a new refusal. A foreign move of a **patch artifact** is the dangerous case: the rebuild would apply it to a file the work of the tree belongs to (H1). The classification (the module `lib/syncMerge.ts`): `patchsetChanged` — the bytes differ from the map; `treeChanged` — the target is in the selection of `changesSince(base, worktree)`. For `save`: `patchsetOnly ∪ both` non-empty → exit 1 `CK-E-PATCHSET-MOVED`, nothing written; the text holds the sha of the load, the list of artifacts and the manual recipe D18: (1) return the patchset artifacts to the loaded state (`git stash`, `git switch <branch>` or `git checkout <sha> -- delta/`); (2) `codkit save`; (3) bring the move back (`git stash pop` / `git merge` / `git rebase`); (4) `codkit load`. The one-command form is the future two-way `codkit sync` (Phase 8); while it does not exist it does not enter the hint: a hint must be executable on the day it is printed. **A refinement of the implementation to the letter of D16/R13** (the worker of Phase 7): an artifact from "both" is not counted as moved when its bytes reproduce one of the states of the tree (the working file or the blob of one of the foreign commits) — that is codkit's own partial extraction (an addressed save, an interrupted replay) and not a foreign edit, and refusing it would lock the documented recovery paths (an addressed save → a full save; an interruption → a repeated save). Without the map (an old mark) `save` does not refuse but warns: a mismatch of the fingerprint by itself does not tell a foreign edit from our own extraction. `status` prints `loaded from patchset commit: <sha|dirty>` and, when it has moved, `patchset moved since load: N artifact(s)` — the data of the recipe (PROP-007 §6). The exception `skipPatchsetMovedCheck` is only the cycle (D12: its phases regenerate and commit the artifacts themselves) and the rebase-onto-pin/completed-rebase paths, which move the artifacts themselves; an internal flag, not a public one. The two-way `sync` (Phase 8) takes the same classification: the tree only → extract; patchset only → apply the patchset version, where overwriting the target during the rebuild is **explainable** (an extension of the `assertNothingMoved` set); both sides → the stop `CK-E-BOTH-SIDES-EDITED` (the message is generalized from own to the whole patch layer, F20). @status:impl/done

**The drift guard**: `dirty(tree)` = (`git status --porcelain` is non-empty outside the own directory) ∨ (an own divergence of the classes `both` — the bytes differ — or `tree-only` — the file exists only in the tree) ∨ (**the third half**, campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decision D7) the foreign commits of the tree are non-empty (`##TREE-COMMITS-ARE-WORK`): the commits of the first-parent line above the last generated tip, which the other two halves do not see — over a commit `git status` gives a clean tree. The list for the human holds the lines `commit <short> "<subject>" (not in patchset)`; the refusal is exit 1 `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE`: for edits "N path(s) … not in patchset yet", for commits "N commit(s) in the fork tree since the last codkit apply are not in patchset yet", with a hint ("codkit save" or "codkit status"). **The order of the refusals (owner ruling 2026-09-06, spike S0.12)**: the preflight of a shared generated ref (`##GENERATED-REF-WORKTREE-PREFLIGHT`) runs BEFORE any dirt check, unconditionally, in every guarding command: a commit of a neighbouring worktree on the shared branch moves the shared ref and makes the index of THIS tree "staged-dirty" — phantom dirt whose cause is the sharing of the ref, not local work; the refusal `CK-E-WORKTREE-REF-SHARED` (exit 2) names both trees and does not advise `save` — a hint "run codkit save" would here pull foreign work into this patch set as an edit of our own. The cause is diagnosed before the symptom; `CK-E-TREE-HEAD` obeys the same order (D8: an anomaly of the line, or HEAD off the branch with foreign — exit 1, with the same code from `##TREE-COMMITS-ARE-WORK`). A file that exists ONLY in the `delta/own/` of patchset (`patchset-only`) is NOT dirt: otherwise the first load of any tree would be impossible (a refinement of the M0 implementation). `--fresh` suppresses the fast path and does not count untracked paths as dirt (otherwise fresh would never clean anything), but it does NOT lift the refusal over commits: `--fresh` is about the untracked, while a commit is the same unextracted work as an edit. `--dry-run` does not run the guard; `skipDriftGuard` is the only bypass, only for `save` / the future two-way `sync` after the extraction. The refinement of REPAIR-005 (PROP-005 §5 `##OVERLAY-KNOWN-MATERIALIZATION`): before refusing, `load --fresh` classifies every tracked overlay target that differs from HEAD — bytes exactly equal to the strict composition of the configured overlays at the pin in the context of the run are a known materialization of codkit, which this run replaces (and says so in the output), not dirt; everything else stays dirt, `--fresh` is not a blanket reset. An ordinary `load` gets no such exception: the fast path could answer "up to date" and leave the packaging bytes. `ci` deliberately passes no classifier: ci materializes overlay targets only through the commits of the generated branch, ci's own runs do not create that state, and the single source of such bytes in a ci tree is an out-of-band `overlay apply`, that is a reused developer tree, which the guard must name out loud; the way out there too is a codkit command (`load --fresh` of that tree) or a single-use fresh tree, not a direct git restore. **The exception for a stranded materialization of an own extension (2026-09-08, PROP-005 `OWN-EXTENSION-STRANDED`):** for an ordinary `load` (without `--fresh`; not for `cycle start`, which refuses `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` over such a tree, and not for the two-way `sync`, where the extracting half fires before the guard with `CK-E-NEW-FILE-IN-UPSTREAM-ZONE`; `ci` and `publish` go by a fresh pass, where the untracked is taken away by the cleanup, and do not meet the guard on that path — measured 2026-09-08) a first-level untracked directory under `extensions/` that no record of the `extensions` section of the manifest declares and that the pin does not ship is not dirt: `load` writes not a byte into such a directory and does not delete it, so a refusal would guard nothing and would lock a daily command after a legitimate step in patchset (the removal of the declaration); the reminder about the directory is taken over by `status` (PROP-007 `CMD-STATUS`, the line about stranded materializations with the recipe `load --fresh`). The predicate gets a hook into the same pure classification as `status` (`isStrandedExtension` next to `isKnownMaterialization` and `isDiscardable`); the rule about a new file in the upstream zone does not change for anything else. @status:impl/done

**Commits in the fork tree are work** (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decisions D1/D2/D8). Work = the uncommitted ∨ the commits of the first-parent line unreachable from the last generated tip. The detector `foreignCommits(tree, pin, branch)` (`lib/treeCommits.ts`): `git rev-list --first-parent --format=…` for `<ref>` ∈ {HEAD, `refs/heads/<branch>`} (those that exist), the lower bound is always the pin; a commit is generated ⟺ the author is `codkit@patchset.invalid` AND the trailer `Codkit-Upstream-Pin` is non-empty (F13); `base` = the topmost generated one, and when there is none — `base = pin.sha` (an empty patchset, the branch is not created); `foreign` = the commits above `base`, from the old to the new. An anomaly: a non-generated commit below `base` — the history under the generated tip was rewritten → `CK-E-TREE-HEAD` (exit 1, "reset the branch to <sha> or restore it from refs/codkit/consumed/…"). The same code refuses when the branch exists, HEAD is off it and the line of HEAD carries foreign work ("HEAD is on <ref|detached> with N commit(s) not in patchset; switch to <branch> (git switch) or merge them there, then run codkit save"). When there is no branch, the chain of HEAD above the pin is work wherever HEAD may be (the first load after a clone); the generated tip itself is not work. Rejected: a base from the cache/mark (they are not authoritative, `##TREE-IS-TRUTH`); a rev-list without `--first-parent` (the states of side branches never existed on the line of the branch). The format of a record is NOT NUL-clean: before every record there is a `commit <sha>` line, and the trailer adds its own `
` (S0.2); the parser cuts by `/^commit [0-9a-f]{40}
/m`, then by `\0`, stripping the trailing `
`. Consumed commits stay reachable through `refs/codkit/consumed/*` (PROP-006 §1 `##CONSUMED-REFS`). @status:impl/done

The reverse direction, file by file and for every layer of the delta (a generalization from own code to the whole patch layer, campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decision D16): own is told apart by the `ownFiles` map of the mark (PROP-006 §1 `##TREE-MARK`), the remaining `delta/**` files outside `delta/own/**` by the `artifacts` map of the same mark (Phase 7). The tree file == the mark → patchset changed (apply patchset); the patchset file == the mark → the tree changed (the dirt of the guard, extracted by save); both sides != the mark — a conflict of the two sides: for own — exit 1 `CK-E-BOTH-SIDES-EDITED` with the name of the file; for non-own artifacts in `save` — the refusal `CK-E-PATCHSET-MOVED` with the recipe (`##PATCHSET-MOVED-RULE`: an extraction into a foreign moved artifact neither stays silent nor merges), in the two-way `sync` (Phase 8) — the same stop `CK-E-BOTH-SIDES-EDITED`, generalized from own to the patch layer (F20). The overlay/resource/rule/removed layers are authored only in patchset and are always "patchset only". For own over a clean tree `load` warns `CK-W-PATCHSET-SIDE-EDIT` and applies the patchset version (at the moment of a load the direction of truth is patchset). Rejected: auto-merging patches (3-way is the territory of the cycle; the diff3 materialization for a human is Phase 8b, not an auto-merge). @status:impl/done

**`save` extracts the final state of the tree relative to the last applied tip** (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decisions D3/D4/D6). The selection is `changesSince(tree, base, state)` (`lib/treeState.ts`): `git diff --name-status --no-renames <base>` (staged+unstaged+committed together — the final state) ∪ the `??` records of `git status --porcelain -z` (the only thing the diff does not see), minus the own prefix, plus the `forcedPaths` of internal calls; the bytes of a file come through `bytesOf(state, path)` (the working file, or `git cat-file blob` for a commit state — the foundation of the replay `##SAVE-REPLAYS-TREE-COMMITS`). The selection is NOT `git status`: over a commit it is empty, and committed work used to be invisible (F7). A rename under `--no-renames` = a deletion + a new file — the deletion refuses `CK-E-DELETES-UPSTREAM-FILE`, as an unstaged rename does today. "Nothing to save" takes the commits into account: a tree with empty commits and no file changes is not nothing but a consumption. The precondition before the rebuild (D6): the foreign set has not changed since the extraction began, otherwise `CK-E-INTERNAL` (exit 2) BEFORE `updateRef`/`moveWorkTree` — it closes the order of F3 (destruction before the check). Consumed commits stay reachable: `refs/codkit/consumed/<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<short7>` → the former HEAD of the tree, `update-ref` under the shared lock of the repository, the message `tree commits consumed: N (<first>..<last>); kept as …`. An addressed `save <paths>` with foreign commits: the branch is not touched (##SAVE-SCOPED-BRANCH-RULE), the commits stay in the tree — `info` "N tree commit(s) stay in the tree until a full save", no consumed ref is written. The patchset commits made from the consumed ones — see `##SAVE-REPLAYS-TREE-COMMITS`: by default one per state, `--squash` — one folded commit. Rejected: two lists, `diff base..HEAD` + `status` — it duplicates paths and loses the staged ones; a refusal without `--commit` — an extraction must not demand a flag. @status:impl/done

**`save` replays the commits of the tree into the history of patchset one by one** (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, Phase 4, decision D5; owner ruling RP-3: the mode with commits is the default, "rebase and merge"). The states `S_1…S_n` = the foreign first-parent commits from the old to the new, then `S_wt` = the working tree. **Two passes** (`lib/saveReplay.ts`). Pass 1 (`planStates`) writes nothing: `planFile` for every `S_i` over an in-memory `ArtifactStore` (an overlay over `delta/patches` and `.codkit/pending`; it records the consumption of the pending drafts — the later states see the artifacts and the drafts of the earlier ones as they will be after those are written). Any error → `blocked`, exit 1, **nothing written** (no artifact, no own byte, no commit), the text carrying the sha and the subject of the source state; the validation of `Cause:` uses the same code as `hooks commit-msg` (F12: the patchset hooks do not run on the commits of `save`, and pass 1 does their work). Pass 2 (`writeStates`): for `S_1…S_n` the writing of the artifacts (`commitArtifacts`) + a patchset commit; for `S_wt` own (`mirrorOwnBack`) + the artifacts, with a commit only under `--commit`. The patchset commit for `S_i`: the paths = the changed artifacts of the state; the message = the original one verbatim (`%B`) + an empty line + `Codkit-Tree-Commit: <sha40>` (the separator is unconditional: a subject of the form "work: …" is indistinguishable from a trailer line, and guessing would glue the trailer to the subject paragraph); `GIT_AUTHOR_*` = the author of the tree commit, committer = the one who runs it (`commitIdentity()`). A state whose staged diff is empty → the commit is skipped with a message (the skip is visible: an empty tree of commits is consumed work too, but the history for it is empty). **Idempotence**: `git log --fixed-strings --grep="Codkit-Tree-Commit: <sha>" -1` in patchset; a state that is found is skipped (an interruption after its commit — the repeated `save` does not duplicate it), and `--squash` after a partial replay finishes the rest in one commit. `--squash`: the intermediate states are validated all the same (a naive single-pass implementation lets through a violation hidden by a later commit — the P4 prediction was proven by a red run: with the state-by-state validation switched off, S17c-reverted gives a false exit 0), while only the final state is written and committed — the plan is written from the disk, not from the store (the store describes the state after writes that never happened). The test seam `replayCheckpoint` (`CODKIT_TEST_SAVE_REPLAY_CRASH_AT`, the test build only): a hard exit after the commit of a state — the crash point of idempotence. Rejected: a single-pass write (a half-extracted delta is worse than one a human edits and repeats); squash by default (RP-3); own per commit (F14: own is excluded locally, the commits of the tree do not carry it). @status:impl/done
5. The 3-way apply at a foreign pin and the classification of the outcomes

Used by `cycle`, `forecast` and `rebase-onto-pin` (at one's own pin there are no conflicts by construction — the self-consistency invariant). Input: an artifact A with the target F, the old pin `oldPin`, the target ref `newRef`. Output: an outcome from the classes below + the materials. @status:spec/done
The names of the outcome classes in the state of the cycle: `clean`, `shifted`, `merged`, `conflict`, `target-deleted`, `target-renamed` (from §6), `rule-broken`, `contract-failed`. @status:spec/done
The engine does not stop at the first conflict: it goes through every independent artifact and gives back the full classified list; exit 3 belongs to the final mandatory human stop. @status:spec/done

The materialization for the resolve: for a `conflict` the orchestrator writes the result of `merge-file --diff3` with the standard conflict markers into the working file of the tree — a human and an agent edit it in the IDE the ordinary way. @status:spec/done
5a. sync: merging the two sides

**Two passes, and both orders are deliberate** (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, Phase 8, decisions D15/D16/D19). The first pass is reading: the lineage (D17), the D16 classification (`classifyTargets`, `##PATCHSET-MOVED-RULE`), both sides of own and of the patch layer; a conflict is found **before the first write**, and every 3-way merge is computed before it too (Phase 8b, D19): a conflict of the patch layer is materialized with diff3 markers (`##SYNC-CONFLICT-DIFF3` below) with exit 1 and a live transaction; an own conflict is `CK-E-BOTH-SIDES-EDITED` without markers (own code has no marker blocks), F20, with the manual recipe "pick a side": to take the tree — `git checkout <sha> -- delta/own/<F>` in patchset, then `save`; to take patchset — roll back the edit of F in the tree, then `sync`. The second pass is the write under the transaction: the save half (`runSave` with `skipPatchsetMovedCheck` — a moved patchset is input data here, not a refusal — and `explainedRewrites` = the `patchsetOnly` targets: a rebuild that applies the patchset version to them is explainable, an extension of the set "nothing moved"), then the consumed ref and the mark with the new map; when the tree has no work, the write is a single load half (`runSync`). `--discard` (D11/D15) discards the commits of the tree deliberately (the same branch of the load engine: the consumed ref before the rebuild, the file halves of the guard armed); under `--ci` — exit 2. `--squash`/`--commit`/`--message` are the inheritance of the save half, `--fresh` of the load half. Auto-merging is rejected here too: the human resolves the diff3 markers themselves (the materialization is `##SYNC-CONFLICT-DIFF3`, the recovery is `##SYNC-ABORT`/`##SYNC-CONTINUE`, Phase 8b); under `--discard` the uncommitted both-part keeps the recipe "pick a side" — `--continue` is an extraction, not a discard (D11). @status:impl/done

**The transaction** (decision D20): the file `.codkit/sync-transaction.json` in the root of patchset (the ownership protocol is PROP-006 §1 `##SYNC-TRANSACTION-FILE`), written by `writeContainedFileExclusive` **before the first mutation** — a repeated start over a live record is impossible by construction (link-EEXIST → a refusal) — and removed after the last one. The record: `{codkitSyncTransaction, id, startedAt, patchset:{head, dirtyBefore}, tree:{head, branchTip, markSnapshot}, rewrite:[{repo, path, blob}], patchsetCommits:[], consumedRef: null, conflicts:[{path, materialized}]}` (the shape of conflicts is Phase 8b: `materialized` is the sha256 of the written markers, `null` means the merge did not reach the file); the snapshots are `git hash-object -w` of only the files the run is going to rewrite (the artifacts of the tree selection in patchset, the `patchsetOnly` targets in the tree, the diverging own files of both sides; an absent file is a null blob, "a snapshot of absence"). Every patchset commit that is created carries the trailer `Codkit-Sync-Transaction: <id>` (recognition by content survives an interruption of the list in the record) and is appended to `patchsetCommits` by an atomic rewrite. While the file exists, step 0 of `load`/`save`/`sync` (and of every call of the engines) is exit 1 `CK-E-SYNC-IN-PROGRESS`, and the hint names both recovery commands; `status` prints `sync in progress: <id>, conflicts: N`. A refusal without a single write removes the record itself (the snapshots matched, HEAD did not move — a proof by checking, not by guessing); a refusal after a write leaves it. The crash tests are the seam `CODKIT_TEST_SYNC_CRASH_AT` (the test build only), the atoms: transaction-written, conflict-materialized, state-committed, worktree-moved, mark-written (PROP-013 §5 `##SYNC-CRASH-TESTS`). The recovery `--abort`/`--continue` is Phase 8b (D21, `##SYNC-ABORT`/`##SYNC-CONTINUE`); an "undo" after a successful sync was rejected there as well. @status:impl/done

**The materialization of a both-sides conflict** (Phase 8b of the campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decisions D19/D21; `codkit sync`, e2e `syncConflict.test.ts`, S26). When the D16 classification puts a target into `both`, `sync` neither refuses nor merges by itself: it puts the 3-way into the tree file with the standard diff3 markers **inside the marker block** `codkit:begin/end`. The sides (D19): the base is the file as the last apply loaded it (`<base>:<F>`, the tip of the generated branch); ours is the working file (or `HEAD:<F>` when the working one cannot be read); theirs is the pin + the current artifact through `applyUnified`. The merge is `runMergeFile` (classifyEngine, the single diff3 implementation in codkit, spike S0.8; `replayPatch` is wrong here: theirs = the pin + the artifact, not the base + the patch). The order: every merge is computed **before** any write (an artifact that does not land on the pin refuses the run while not a byte has been written) → the transaction with the ours snapshots of the conflicting files (`rewrite`, blob) → every merge is written by a durable single-file write (a wx temp + a rename that preserves the mode, the precedent `atomicReplace`) and is marked in the record with the atom `conflict-materialized` carrying the sha256 of the written bytes → exit 1 `CK-E-BOTH-SIDES-EDITED` with the list of the files and both roads onward. The human resolves the markers as in the resolve phase of the cycle (keep both sides and the ids of the blocks; the procedure is 05-upgrade-cycle), then `codkit sync --continue`. Under `--discard` the recipe is not materialized for the uncommitted both-part: `--continue` is an extraction, not a discard (D11). Our own 3-way auto-merge is rejected here too. @status:impl/done

**`codkit sync --continue`** (decision D21; e2e S26): finish an interrupted run from the record. No record — an honest exit 2: there is nothing to restore. The completeness check over `conflicts[]`, file by file: the markers are still there (the same four lines the manual procedure greps for) → the refusal `CK-E-BOTH-SIDES-EDITED` with the names; `materialized = null` and the file equals the ours snapshot byte for byte → the refusal "the merge did not reach the file" (a crash between the writing of the record and the writing of the markers does not pass itself off as the human "take the tree"; a real "take the tree" after the materialization gives the same bytes, but the record already carries the sha — the difference is the proof). Then the same writing pass as in a fresh run (`runSave` with `skipPatchsetMovedCheck` + `explainedRewrites`, the same atoms and trailers) under the same record; new both-targets that appeared after the stop get the same answer — the markers, exit 1, the record extended; the snapshots of the artifacts the record lacked are added before the pass (an abort after a crash in the continuation covers them too). On success the record is removed, exit 0. The extraction flags (`--squash`/`--commit`/`--message`/`--fresh`) apply to the continuation; `--discard`/`--dry-run` do not. @status:impl/done

**`codkit sync --abort`** (decision D21; e2e S27): give everything back as the run found it. This is the load-bearing half of the phase: materializing the markers is easy; the promise that the operator can always come back is what makes the markers a safe offer. No record — exit 2. The audit **before the first mutation**: the patchset commits above the recorded HEAD are removed only if each carries the trailer `Codkit-Sync-Transaction: <id>` of this record and HEAD stayed on the recorded line; the tree commits above the recorded HEAD only if each is generated (the codkit author + the pin trailer, F13; a descendancy check is NOT required for the tree — the rebuild leaves the line as a matter of course, D6); HEAD of the tree on a foreign ref, or a history that cannot be enumerated — a refusal with an explanation and the names; a foreign commit on top is **never thrown away** — the refusal `CK-E-SYNC-IN-PROGRESS` names its sha and subject. The mutations come in an order that makes an interrupted abort restartable (every step is idempotent, the record is removed last): patchset — a `reset --mixed` to the recorded HEAD (the index is resynchronized, the removed commits do not survive as staged changes) and the artifacts from the snapshots byte for byte (the blob from the object database, a wx temp + a rename with the mode); the tree — the files from the snapshots (those that were absent are deleted), the branch to `tree.head` with a guard of the current tip (a branch the run created is deleted), HEAD to the same place (a detached one stays detached, `--no-deref`), with a moved HEAD a `reset --mixed` of the index, the mark from `markSnapshot` (when there was none, it is removed). `refs/codkit/consumed/*` stays (harmless, D22 cleans it). The patchset commits are removed with `--mixed`, not `--soft`: the D21 plan called both mechanisms one family; the index must come back together with HEAD, otherwise what was removed survives as staged. An "undo" after a successful sync does not exist — that is `git reset --hard <before>` in patchset + `codkit load` (the recipe D18). @status:impl/done
6. Following the renames between pins
A separate explicit step before the apply (not an auto-detection inside it — on large diffs git switches rename detection off silently). @status:spec/done

Pairs with `similarity < 100` are marked "needs a human eye" in the report (the carry-over is done, but it lands on the red list of the review). The check case of the polygon: the rename `src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/remoteAgentHostProtocolClient.ts → agentHostProtocolClient.ts` (R096, the window `1.134.0→1.135.0`). @status:spec/done
7. Finding the cause commit
`git log --format=%H --follow oldPin..newPin -- F` — the commits that touched the file. @status:spec/done

One commit → it is the cause. Several → narrow down by lines: for every hunk of the artifact take the range of the affected lines at `oldPin` and run `git log -L<start>,<end>:F oldPin..newPin --format=%H`; the cause commit is the earliest commit that crossed the range; when `-L` is not applicable (the file was deleted/renamed), the cause commit is declared to be the last commit of the first step, marked `approx`. @status:spec/done
For `target-deleted`/`target-renamed` — the commit that deleted/renamed it (`git log --diff-filter=D|R --follow`). @status:spec/done

Output: `{sha, approx: bool}`; it is written into the `cause` of the patch header (by the regeneration step), into the journal and into the `Cause:` trailer of the fix commit. The report of the cycle is grouped by cause commits (dozens of refusals → a handful of causes). @status:spec/done
codkit PROP-009: The upgrade-cycle orchestrator - state, journal, phases, cadence
1. Cadence and upstream tracking

**We track the release tags of upstream, at a weekly step** (fact: the tags `1.128`…`1.135` come about a week apart; the window `1.134→1.135` is 267 commits). The pin moves only on green CI; a stuck cycle blocks nobody - we stay on the old pin and release from it. @status:spec/done
Batching several tags is allowed as an exception (a toolchain cascade, for instance), but not as the norm: on large diffs automatic rename detection degrades. @status:spec/done

**A daily forecast** (independent of tags): a nightly dry run of applying the delta to a fresh upstream `main`; a report by owners - «intervention X, the upstream cause commit Y will break it soon». It changes nothing; it is implemented by the same apply engine in dry-run mode. @status:spec/done

**Our release is a separate rhythm**: we release when the product is ready, from the current green pin; the product version is its own, and the upstream pin is a machine field in the publication artifact. @status:spec/done
2. Cycle state - cycle/state.json

Committed on the cycle branch; the presence of the file in the patch-set work tree means «a cycle is running»; the state is written atomically (a temporary file + rename) after every change. @status:spec/done

Before `reset --hard`, `restart` atomically duplicates the recovery snapshot into the local `.codkit/cycle-control.json` (`codkitCycleControl: 1`, `status: running|done`). This file is not committed and lies outside the reset scope: if the tracked `cycle/state.json` disappeared after the reset, a repeated `restart` and `status` finish the operation from the exact bump/base SHAs. `done` is kept until the next verified start, so that a crash after the last mutation has an idempotent answer. @status:impl/done
3. The cycle journal

`cycle/log/<targetTag>.md` (human-readable, committed) and `cycle/log/<targetTag>.jsonl` (machine-readable, one atomically appended line per event: `{"codkitCycleJournal":1,"ts":…,"artifact":…,"outcome":…,"resolution":…,"cause":…,"by":"human|agent:<name>","verified":…}`). @status:spec/done

The completeness check: every artifact with a non-`clean` outcome has a record in the jsonl - otherwise `cycle continue` does not let the cycle into the `done` phase (exit 1, `CK-E-LOG-INCOMPLETE`). @status:spec/done
The journal of agent decisions is the same jsonl with the field `by: "agent:<name>"`; an agent writes there through an ordinary file (the contract for the agent protocol FEAT-004). @status:spec/done
4. The state machine - phases and transitions

Every phase is idempotent and resumable: `continue` re-reads `state.json`, validates the actual state of the tree and of the patch set and continues from `phase`; an interruption at any point loses no data. @status:spec/done

**init** (`cycle start <target>`): the checks (PROP-007 §14) → the branch `codkit/cycle/<targetTag>` off the current main → the canonical pin commit (an edit of `codkit.json`: pin.tag/sha/date; message `codkit cycle: bump pin to <tag>`) → state → phase=apply. @status:spec/done

**apply**: the rename step (PROP-008 §6) → carrying the artifacts over the renames in a separate canonical commit → the classification loop (PROP-008 §5) over every artifact against the new pin → filling in `state.artifacts` → the `clean|shifted|merged` artifacts are regenerated automatically (PROP-004 §5 against the new pin; the `pin` field of the headers is updated) and committed as one machine canonical «regeneration» commit (the «regenerable» category: it may be thrown away and created anew) → if `conflict|target-deleted|rule-broken` are empty, phase=deps-advisory, otherwise phase=resolve and a **stop** (exit 3): the red list is printed, grouped by cause commits, with the owners from the inventory. @status:spec/done

**resolve** (humans and agents work in the tree; the conflicts are materialized with the standard markers): after the edits, `cycle continue` runs `save` over the affected files; every resolution is a separate commit with the trailer `Cause: <sha>` (prepared by the hook of PROP-007 §19); a journal record is mandatory; once all are resolved → phase=deps-advisory. @status:spec/done

**deps-advisory**: the semantic readers the project type declares are run over the `oldPin..newPin` diff (the readers are the type's answer, not the engine's; VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-005#VSCODE-ADVISORY-READERS`) → a report on «what changed in the toolchain»; a non-empty report in interactive mode is a **stop point** (exit 3; a human runs `npm install` in the tree by the protocol - the daemons are stopped beforehand with `build down --all`); under `--ci` the report goes to the log and the cycle continues. @status:spec/done

**stabilize**: `build up` → `build errors` (the full output) → own tests → contract tests → (by profile) upstream tests → marking the `contract-failed` artifacts → red → phase=resolve (back); green → phase=done. @status:spec/done

**done** (`continue`): the journal completeness check → a snapshot of the inventory metrics into the cycle journal → a commit of the journal and of the state (the runtime state is deleted by the final commit) → the instruction to merge the cycle branch into main without a squash. The completion checklist includes checking the bootstrap forbidden services and the selected build-watch boundaries against the new pin. @status:spec/done
**Rollback**: `cycle restart` - a `git reset --hard` of the cycle branch to the parent of the pin commit plus deletion of the state (confirmed by `--yes`). @status:spec/done
The mandatory stop points: the toolchain advisory; manual conflicts; broken rules; patches to deleted files; a large design decision (stop, explain, offer the options). @status:spec/done
5. The canonical commit set of a cycle and the trailers

The canonical set (it is not squashed on merge - otherwise the cost metric is lost): «bump pin»; «renames» (the artifacts carried over the renames); «regeneration» (machine-made - it may be thrown away and created anew); «deps/toolchain»; individual fixes, each with its own cause; «removal of the artifacts of files that disappeared» - always a separate commit with an explanation. @status:spec/done

The trailers: every commit of a cycle carries `Codkit-Cycle: <targetTag>`; fixes carry `Cause: <upstream SHA>` in addition. The codkit hook puts them there, CI checks them (without machine validation a trailer does not take root - the lesson of the references). The canonical messages produced under the hook are uniform, so that they are easy to search for. @status:spec/done
6. Build order

The orchestrator is built **after** apply and extract are stable - a minimal version in the MVP (pin → apply → a report of the refusals → continue), the extension later. The tests of the orchestrator itself run on a fake fork tree (PROP-013 §2, §5): the git operations are real, the heavy parts are emulated. @status:spec/done
codkit PROP-010: Build integration - code delivery, watch daemons, tests
1. Own-code delivery and the graft point

Own code is delivered from patchesDir to forkDir by copying, not by a symlink/junction: a plain checkout, a globber, a watcher, a linter and packaging must all see the result the same way. On every pin, contract tests confirm that the build/test globs cover `src/vs/<ownDirName>/**`. @status:spec/done
Tombstone (PROP-016 split, 2026-09-09): moved to spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-004#BUILD-COMMIT-COMES-FROM-THE-TREE-HEAD; the address stays for citations. @status:spec/done
2. Watch-daemon wrapper

Codkit starts the selected npm scripts of forkDir as detached processes; stdout/stderr, the pid and the expected command identity are kept in `patchesDir/.codkit/build/`. The truth is a living process with a matching identity; the record is a hint and carries the treeId. Linux uses `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and the process group; macOS/Windows must use a natively verified process probe/termination path instead of assuming POSIX semantics. On POSIX the recorded pid is also the pgid: the exit of the npm leader does NOT mean the daemon is dead while at least one descendant remains in that group. `status` keeps counting such a group as living; `down` sends TERM to the whole group, waits for ALL of its members to disappear, then KILLs if needed and waits again. The record is removed only after the group is empty; a group that survives KILL yields `CK-E-INTERNAL` with the record preserved for another attempt at management. This closes the crash-resume flake of REPAIR-006, where an early npm exit left the shell/compiler without a kill handle and the next full run saw its own leaked watcher. @status:spec/done

The live daemon/process-group pass is confirmed on Linux. Native macOS and Windows `up/status/errors/down`, command identity and process-tree termination remain a mandatory open matrix. @status:spec/plan

REPAIR-007: POSIX termination uses the platform from the probe and signals exactly the negated recorded pgid; the test observes TERM and KILL and goes red when the signal seam is not called. On Windows a recorded root pid that has already disappeared cannot be safely recovered through `taskkill /t`: status is `unknown`, `down` and a repeated `up` fail closed, and the record is kept with an instruction to prove teardown natively; this is not passed off as `dead`/`not-running`. A native Job Object remains an open proof. @status:impl/done

A fresh POSIX pid record gets exactly a 2000 ms settling window, and only as a fail-closed `starting`: right after the spawn npm may not have published the expected argv identity/descendant yet. An absent/mismatched identity is NEVER `living`, is never signalled and never certifies an old log; a CI owner may poll until the identity is proven, while individual `up/down/status/errors` see `starting` and refuse a destructive/certifying action. After the threshold a mismatched argv is `unknown` with zero signals; an absent pid without a pgid is `dead`. On Windows an absent root is `unknown` immediately. @status:impl/done

REPAIR-008 state machine: a daemon record is absent, invalid, starting (`pid:0` exclusive reservation or a bounded unproven startup), living (argv or a surviving POSIX pgid proven), dead (a valid owner proven gone) or unknown. A reservation is published as already complete JSON by a single exclusive hard link, carries a UUID nonce and moves to the final pid only by CAS on the exact generation. A second `up` and concurrent `down/status/errors` neither remove nor seize a starting record; a displaced owner terminates its own spawned process. An empty/truncated/malformed/schema-invalid/unreadable record is `unknown` and is preserved by every command; `errors` does not read an old log for starting/unknown. @status:impl/done

All daemon records/logs/rotation and the dependency receipt in `.codkit/build` are read/created/replaced/renamed/removed only through the contained runtime-root API: `.codkit`, `build`, the leaf and the rotation target must be real non-symlink regular paths; the open descriptor and the parent identity are re-proven. Before any path or mutation a channel key must be a single portable basename: empty/dot/dot-dot, separators/traversal, absolute/drive/UNC/device/reserved/control/platform aliases are forbidden with a stable `CK-E-CONFIG`; derived files are direct children of the runtime dir only. Node without portable `openat`/`renameat` keeps the narrow parent-swap limit already documented in PROP-002. @status:impl/done

REPAIR-009: daemon record transitions are serialized by a short-lived contained per-channel operation lock in the administrative area of the patch set (`.codkit/locks/daemon-<key>.lock`). The key is the full SHA-256 of the ASCII-case-folded channel name, so two spellings of one channel cannot hold two locks over one runtime file. The complete nonce-carrying bytes are published by a single exclusive hard link; the reader distinguishes absent/valid/invalid, and a malformed/unreadable/symlinked/schema-invalid lock is a refusal and is NEVER removed automatically. Only a valid lock whose owner pid is proven absent is recovered; EPERM or a reused pid stays "possibly alive" and refuses. `upChannel` and `downChannel` take the lock before the first inspection of the record or the process and hold it across the whole mutation: for up, the probe, the retirement of a stale record, the reservation, the rotation, the spawn and the final publication or the exact cleanup; for down, the identity proof, TERM/wait/KILL/wait and the exact retirement. Two channel locks are never held at once; the outer order stays global/cycle → tree → daemon-channel. Replacement, removal and signals require an unforgeable live channel-bound capability or stay private inside the locked closure; before the final replace, removal, TERM and KILL the exact generation is re-read and re-checked. Immutable generation pointers are rejected: portable Node has no conditional pointer replace, and they add crash/GC states without closing the race. @status:impl/done

REPAIR-012 (a correction of REPAIR-011): **every artifact the lock protocol publishes carries a provable owner.** The public lock carries a pid and a nonce checked by the liveness machinery; so does the claim that recovers an orphaned generation, but in its bytes rather than in its name: a strict JSON record with its own schema (in the style of the lock record) names the pid and the nonce of the publisher and the exact dev/ino of the published generation, and is validated on publication. The claim name is single and fixed per publication (`<public>.orphan-<dev>-<ino>.owner`): the election is the exclusive publication of that name, where `EEXIST` is exactly a lost election, that is, an atomic primitive decided by the file system and not by reading a directory. REPAIR-013 (a correction of REPAIR-012, two independent audits): **an inode number is an identity only while the inode is pinned.** On a file system that reuses numbers (ext4 hands a freed number to the next file of the same directory almost always; tmpfs never), a successor that published a new generation under the public name could get the very number recorded in the claim, and the dev/ino comparison then passed against another file: two contenders unlinked one public name. REPAIR-014 (a correction of REPAIR-013, audit A1/B13-4): the pin is opened **at the start of the pass**, where the identity is taken, before the claim name and bytes are derived from it, and is held across the election, the proofs and the unlink until the `finally` of every exit. Opening it AFTER the election, as in REPAIR-013, pinned whatever stood under the name by then: a contender whose publication had already been unlinked compared the name with itself, a tautology on any file system, and measurement on ext4 showed that the reproduced failure was closed precisely by the re-read `nlink` (with the REPAIR-013 pin and `nlink` removed: 16/120 double acquisitions; with the REPAIR-014 pin and `nlink` removed: 0/120, so each of the two guards now closes the failure on its own and both are kept). The claim name is derived from the pinned `fstat` as well: two contenders on one inode get one name and collide in the election, while a contender on another inode does not enter that election - its binding refuses before the unlink. The identity for the re-proof is taken from the `fstat` of the descriptor and not from a path `lstat`; before the public name is unlinked exactly two proofs are re-checked - the public name is still that pinned inode (`lstat` against `fstat`; a divergence is `'lost'`, not a refusal), and the parent is still the directory whose identity was taken on entry; `nlink` is re-read within that same proof instead of being trusted from the stat at the start of the pass (a living successor under the name, or an owner that hard-linked the publication while the scan ran, is visible only in a fresh stat). `nlink === 0` on the pinned inode means the publication was unlinked while the pass held it: `'lost'`. The unlink itself tolerates `ENOENT` as `'lost'`. The rule `nlink != 1` carries a clean meaning: an extra hard link to the publication is a living owner. The same law of pinning is applied to the private-link removal (`removeContainedHardlinkGeneration`): the publication is pinned before that path's own election and both unlinks tolerate `ENOENT`. Whether the fixed claim name is occupied is decided by a fresh read of that path and not by a stale scan: a valid claim naming this publication is a competitor (the election answers atomically, a live publisher's claim is never removed and is never offered for removal by a hint); damage - a non-regular entry, or bytes that do not name the inode which encodes their own name - is a loud refusal naming the file. The winner's `finally` re-checks that the file at its claim path is still the one it publishes, by the same re-proof as the sweep. Recovery distinguishes three states and NEVER collapses them into one: a claim whose publisher may be alive is a lost election (retry); a claim whose publisher is proven absent is the debris of a recoverer killed midway, it is buried (with a re-proof that the file at that path is still the one whose record was read) and the pass is repeated; any other extra link is a living owner and a refusal. A reused pid is read as possibly alive and its claim is not touched: a refusal, never a theft. The limit of the law is named honestly: the number in the BYTES of another claim, and the name derived from it, outlive any descriptor - the claim of a killed recoverer is a freely dangling inode number; while the pid of its publisher is alive, a refusal stays the right direction. The alternatives of REPAIR-011/012 are rejected and named: an anonymous claim link (exactly the CK-A32 wedge - debris indistinguishable from a living competitor); a timeout or an age check (guessing where a proof is available); and the publisher in the claim NAME - a unique name per contender destroys the collision the election rested on, the `EEXIST` branch goes dead, and the election degenerates into read-then-act, where two contenders unlink one public lock name (the REPAIR-011 regression). The alternatives of REPAIR-013 are rejected and named: a return to an election by hard-linking the publication (brings back the anonymous CK-A32 wedge); a content hash or a generation counter (the bytes of the publication are not ours to constrain). Narrowing `nlink != 1` is NO LONGER listed as a rejected alternative: in REPAIR-013 it was the load-bearing guard of the reproduced failure, and the record that called it "not a proof" was a mistake of the parent, corrected in REPAIR-014. The residue of pinning is named honestly: on Windows `O_NOFOLLOW` is zero and an open handle interacts with deletion differently - the guarantee is a POSIX one, native Windows is unverified (CK-A04). The generation election lives in `containedGeneration.ts` and the claim grammar in `containedClaim.ts`, apart from `containedFile.ts`: this half needs an injectable liveness oracle that nobody else needs, and the containment layer still does not decide the policy of whose bytes these are. Test base: tests that compare dev/ino, count `nlink` or run the lock election must get their fixtures on a root where number reuse is MEASURED (create/unlink/create, not the predicate "not tmpfs": btrfs and APFS pass such a predicate and never reuse), chosen explicitly and failing loudly when there is no such root (test/support/diskRoot.ts) - for three rounds in a row the defect was invisible because every fixture lived on the single file system where the central assumption of the protocol comes for free. @status:impl/done

REPAIR-009: new daemon records are strict - the reservation and the final record must carry a nonce, unknown fields are forbidden, and `startedAt` must be a real canonical finite ISO timestamp (round-trip `toISOString`). Semantic invalidity is `unknown`; the exact bytes and the mtime of the record are preserved by every command. The exported collapsing `readRecord()` is gone: the only public reader is the discriminated `readRecordState()`, so a future production caller cannot merge absent and invalid. Log readers (`errors`) fail closed too: an invalid record is an environment failure, never `gone`, and an old finished pass is not certified. @status:impl/done

REPAIR-009: `status`, `down` and `errors` are bound to the currently resolved tree id/path. `status` stays lock-free, read-only and point-in-time, and reports recorded tree ownership and a mismatch honestly; on a mismatch `down` sends no signal at all and `errors` does not certify another tree's log. Mutating and certifying mismatches return an environment failure. `errors` holds no lock while it waits: a snapshot of the generation, the read/poll of the log, a second read, and certification only if the same final generation still owns the current tree; a rotation, a change of generation, starting/invalid/unknown or a loss of ownership is an environment failure, never a mixed or an old green. @status:impl/done

REPAIR-009: the whole channel set is validated before caching, before any path is created and before any mutation. Case-insensitively, `all` and `deps-hash` are reserved; ASCII-case-fold duplicates and collisions of the derived `.json`/`.log`/`.log.1` names are rejected with a diagnostic naming both original spellings; a name whose actual plus candidate/temp file name exceeds the portable component limit (255 bytes) is rejected before `.codkit` is created. @status:impl/done

REPAIR-009: every contained writer loops until all bytes are written or it fails - a short `writeSync` never publishes truncated bytes. Directory identity is re-proven by dev/ino and not by the returned path string, for exclusive publication, append, rename, remove and runtime mutations: a swap to a DIFFERENT ordinary directory must refuse without touching the replacement or the external sentinel files. An append/write over an existing runtime leaf with more than one hard link refuses, so that an internal log does not mutate an external hard-link peer. The honest portable limit is kept: without `openat`/`renameat` a narrow parent-swap window remains (PROP-002), and the hard-link/ctime limitation is recorded in the risks. @status:impl/done

REPAIR-009: `build status` stays report-only and exits 0 when the OBSERVATION succeeded, not when every daemon is healthy. `starting` and `unknown` stay visible states of the line/JSON; the command/reference and the JSON documentation must say so explicitly, so that exit 0 is not read as a health check. @status:impl/done

The environment contract of the daemons on Linux (M1 measurement on a live tree): a watch over 17 948 files requires `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` ≥ 524288; with the default 65536 the transpile daemon finishes the first pass (the boundaries are printed normally) but fails with `ENOSPC` while installing the watchers. Before the start `build up` reads `/proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_watches` and, at a value < 262144, warns with the remedy command (`sudo sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288` plus an entry in /etc/sysctl.d); this is the owner's machine setting and codkit does not change it. For a single CI pass the result of the pass before the watchers fail is usable. @status:impl/done

The pass-boundary detector is strict versioned data. The default lives in `toolRoot/config/build-watch.json`; the patch set selected by the user may supply a complete fork-specific profile only through an explicit contained `codkit.json.buildWatchFile`. An implicit file at the same path does not shadow the shipped default. Channels declare `passStart`, `passEnd`, `errorLine`, `errorCountLine`, `falseEndGuards`; unknown fields are forbidden, and a channel without `errorLine` and `errorCountLine` is invalid. The counting detector `errorCountLine` is validated on load: every pattern must contain a capturing group for the number (group 1 is the only one the counter reads), otherwise `CK-E-CONFIG` before any log is read; and during the read: a pattern that MATCHED a count line but yielded no numeric group 1 (no group, or a group that captured non-digits) is also `CK-E-CONFIG` and not "no summary" (REPAIR-006: a silent `stated:null` with zero parsed diagnostics produced a false green). A custom profile must have stored green/red log fixtures; the cycle re-checks the expressions on the new pin. @status:spec/done

In a finished pass a count-only channel (`errorCountLine` non-empty, `errorLine` empty) MUST have a matched summary line: a mismatch or a drift of wording is `CK-E-CONFIG`, not an effective zero. A fallback to the number of parsed diagnostics is allowed only when a real `errorLine` detector exists. @status:impl/done

codkit PROP-011: CI and the air-gapped circuit
1. The job contract (the same for any CI)
checkout of the patch set by the regular CI step; @status:spec/done
the fork tree is provided in any way: a bind mount of a persistent directory, a CI volume or cache, an image layer, a checkout as a second repository; @status:spec/done

the container is started with three independent paths: the installed toolRoot, the patch set through `--patches-dir`/`CODKIT_PATCHES_DIR`, the fork through `--fork-dir`/`CODKIT_FORK_DIR`; @status:spec/done
one command, `codkit ci`. The image contains the Codkit runtime and the Node/git/git-lfs environment, but contains no consumer patch set and no fork checkout. @status:spec/done

**The air-gapped circuit is the primary mode, not a degradation**: there is no external internet in the target environment; everything needed is brought in by the supply kit (§7); the customer's CI is any of them (Jenkins/GitHub/GitLab/their own). Every new codkit mechanism is designed for offline first. @status:spec/done
2. Network

The global `--ci` is a hard zero-network mode: codkit performs no network call at all. The `gitx` module takes `netAllowed`; with `netAllowed=false`, `fetch|clone|pull|lfs pull|push|ls-remote` are not started at all (exit 2 `CK-E-NET-FORBIDDEN` with a text saying which external action the CI has to perform). `publish` is not `--ci`: it refuses the combination with `--ci`, requires `--yes-i-am-publish-bot` and only then turns the network on. Before any materialization or change of refs the publish bot must pass the read-only gate `git ls-remote <publishRemoteUrl>`; a failure ends the command with code 2 and no mutations. Push stays with `publish` alone, on the supplier side. Automated tests: `ci` on the polygon with the network physically off; separately, publish against a local bare remote with the gate checked. @status:spec/done
3. Profiles

`verify` (the threshold of every PR; seconds to minutes): `check-tree` → the fresh pass → apply → `verify` (PROP-007 §11) → the race guards: the pin guard (the pin of the PR branch equals the pin of the target branch; in CI the `codkit.json` of the PR is compared against base) - a mismatch → 1 with the hint `codkit rebase-onto-pin`. @status:spec/done

`build`: `verify` + the dependencies (the upstream fast path by the hash of the manifests; on a lock change, a full install from the internal registry) + `build up` + `build errors` (one pass, full output) + own tests + contract tests; the upstream hygiene/eslint run BEFORE the materialization of the overlay targets upstream is strict about (the order: hygiene → overlay apply → our checks). The skeleton and the order are universal; the scripts each step runs are the project type's answer (VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-004#VSCODE-BUILD-STEPS`). @status:spec/done

The CI itself names the base for the pin guard: the flag `--pin-guard-base <ref>` (a ref in the patch-set repository; the `codkit.json` of the patch-set work tree and the one at the ref are compared). Without the flag the step is skipped with an info line - the run does not pretend that the guard passed. On a mismatch the hint points at the implemented `rebase-onto-pin` command. @status:impl/done

The M1 decision on «on a lock change, a full install from the internal registry»: **`ci` installs nothing itself** - installing the dependencies from the internal registry is a job step OUTSIDE the codkit container (or a pre-filled cache/mount). The behaviour of `ci --profile build`: the npm receipts `node_modules/.package-lock.json` and `build/node_modules/.package-lock.json` of the tree are absent (including the case of an empty bind-mount directory left behind) → exit 2 `CK-E-DEPS-MISSING` with the text «provide node_modules via cache/mount (air-gapped supply kit)»; a stale `.codkit/build/deps-hash.json` does not cancel this presence probe; the lock or `.nvmrc` changed against the record → the warning «refresh node_modules out of band», the run continues and the record is updated (the warning fires once per lock change, not forever); the record is one per tree, keyed by `treeId` (like the daemon records). @status:impl/done

The cache: the key is `pin.sha` plus the hash of the lock files; the only writer is the job of the main branch, the rest read. A toolchain change (the cycle advisory) changes the key, that is, a controlled full rebuild. The cold build (~an hour) is paid once per agent/cache. @status:spec/done
4. The «from scratch» pass and the cleanup whitelist

«From scratch» refers to the content of the tree: the tracked files are brought to the pin by a git checkout (only the changed files are rewritten - together with the mtime discipline this keeps incremental compilation warm), then the delta is applied. Untracked content is cleaned **by a whitelist** that deliberately keeps the build caches. @status:spec/done

`cleanupWhitelist` (the conventions of PROP-003 §3), the pattern semantics are gitignore-style; refined by the M0 implementation: `node_modules/` (at any level), `.build/`, `/out*/` (anchored: the top level only - an unanchored `out*/` would protect `outer/` and `output/` anywhere as well), `extensions/*/out/`, `extensions/*/dist/`, `.eslintcache`, `*.tsbuildinfo`; the `.git/codkit/` entry of the early edition is removed - git does not report the content of `.git` in the untracked list, and the mark is untouchable anyway. In addition, the own directory `src/vs/<ownDirName>/` and `.git/**` are always kept. The algorithm: `git clean -fdx` is NOT used; the untracked list is the union of `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` and `… --others --ignored --exclude-standard` (a lone `--others` does NOT show ignored files), by files (without `--directory` - otherwise a collapsed directory would delete the whitelisted content inside it); the entries covered by the whitelist are subtracted from it, and the rest is deleted. The discipline: what is not in the list is deleted. The pattern semantics, the algorithm and the discipline are the engine's; **which** paths a build leaves behind is the project type's answer (VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-002#VSCODE-CLEANUP-WHITELIST`), and the list above is that type's value carried here until the extraction of phase P2. @status:impl/done

Installing the tree dependencies after a restore relies on the upstream fast path «the dependencies are up to date» (the hash of the manifests, the lock and `.nvmrc`) - seconds when the lock files are unchanged. @status:spec/done
5. Permissions and safe.directory

A mounted tree usually belongs to another uid: before the first git call, `ci` checks for the «dubious ownership» sign (a trial `git status`; the characteristic error) and adds both paths to the configuration of the **container**: for this `ci` uses not `/dev/null` but the file `.codkit/gitconfig-ci` (pointed at through `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` inside the container) with the entries `safe.directory=<tree>` and `<patchset>` - without touching the machine. The right to write into the tree and into the cache directories is checked before the work starts. Agreeing the uid/gid is the contract of starting the container (the documentation of PROP-012 §4). @status:spec/done

The M1 implementation: `gitx` gained the option `gitConfigGlobal` (it replaces `/dev/null`; the system configuration stays off) and a run-wide setting - ONLY a `ci` run uses it, and only after the probe has fired; `.codkit/gitconfig-ci` is created or extended with the union of the safe.directory entries (the tree + the patch set). The write probes: the tree is checked (check-tree in write mode); the patch-set runtime is checked by actually creating the lock before any work with the tree, and `EACCES`/`EPERM`/`EROFS` are turned into exit 2 `CK-E-TREE-READONLY` with a hint about a separate writable `.codkit` mount. The dubious-ownership branch is confirmed by a live Docker matrix with owner 1000 and process UID 10001; the unit tests cover the writer/gitx and the classification of the lock I/O. @status:impl/done
6. The effective diff

For a PR the CI builds the diff of the **applied states**: the tip of the generated branch for base and for the PR (`git diff base-top pr-top` in the tree) - this is an ordinary code diff, which the reviewer reads instead of a diff of patch files; plus the inventory diff (`inventory --diff`). It is implemented inside `ci --profile verify` by the flag `--effective-diff <base-ref>`; the output is a CI file artifact. @status:spec/done

The M1 implementation: the base tip is built by `syncEngine.buildAppliedTip()` - the generated commits of the base state are written into the object database of the TREE without touching the working copy, the refs, the mark or the cache (for a disposable ci tree this is normal; for a live tree it would be a surprise - hence only in `ci`). The requirements: the base pin is reachable in the tree AND the base delta applies on its own pin; otherwise only the inventory diff is built, with a warning (the exit code does not change). The artifacts: `.codkit/out/effective-diff.patch` (the full diff; `--stat` is printed to the output) and `.codkit/out/inventory-diff.md`. The REPAIR-006 refinement (the obsolete M1 text is removed): the base tip is built by `buildGeneratedTip()` - the full generated history, INCLUDING the aggregate own commit of its own (`commitOwn`, PROP-005 LT-OWN; the same layer order as the PR tip), so own files enter the diff of the tips as ordinary code; the literal review of `delta/own/**` in a patch-set PR stays available, but is no longer the only window into own code. @status:impl/done

Keeping the table current is an item of the cycle advisory; the external network exists on the supplier side only: the mirror bot (fetch from upstream → push to the mirror) and the publish bot, each with its own service account. @status:spec/done

The logs: the cycle journal is PROP-009 §3 (md + jsonl, both committed); the daemon logs are `.codkit/build/*.log` (rotation: on `up` the old log is renamed to `.1`, one generation is kept); `--verbose` prints diagnostics to stderr (the git commands with their arguments, the timings of the steps). @status:spec/done
