5. Open decision points (the work continues on the default)

**The pre-commit hook in the fork tree is the NORM, rewritten by the owner decision RP-1 of campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE (the ruling verbatim: «вместо запрета сделать напоминание»; the original norm of 2026-08-31, «согласен с обеими утверждениями», installed a rejecting hook and is cancelled by this decision).** The hook NEVER rejects a commit: a commit in the tree is work (PROP-008 §4 `##TREE-COMMITS-ARE-WORK`), since phases 2–4 of the campaign it is not lost - the destructive commands refuse over it (`##DRIFT-GUARD-PREDICATE`) and `save` extracts it - so a refusal protected nothing. The hook prints a reminder to stderr: on a `codkit/applied/*` branch, «codkit: this commit is work in the fork tree; it reaches patchset only when you run codkit save or codkit sync»; off it, with the branch in existence (a detached HEAD included), «codkit: HEAD is not on codkit/applied/<tag>; codkit save will refuse until you switch back (git switch codkit/applied/<tag>)» with the concrete `<tag>` of this tree substituted at installation time (`save` will refuse there with `CK-E-TREE-HEAD`, decision D8). `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1` suppresses the reminder (only codkit's own git calls set it; load, however, builds the branch through commit-tree/update-ref, which the hook does not interfere with by construction). `load` installs the script only into the repository's own administrative path - `hooks/pre-commit` under the absolute git directory of the tree (an ordinary tree: `<tree>/.git/hooks/pre-commit`; the rule of the administrative paths is PROP-008 §3 `##TREE-HOOK-STEP`), never following `core.hooksPath` outside the administrative directory of the repository; the hook is restored by every `load` with the current branch name. Exception 1: in a linked worktree the hook is not installed and `load` issues a warning - the hooks are shared by the whole repository, and the reminder would speak in the name of the branch of one tree even in the sibling worktrees that codkit does not manage; the protection there is the refusal of `load`/`save` over foreign commits (the implementation is PROP-008 §3). Exception 2: when a configured `core.hooksPath` (of ANY scope - local/global/system; both are checked, REPAIR-006) leads the git hooks away from the hooks directory of the repository, the administrative copy is installed but git keeps executing the configured hook - `load` warns and `writeTreeHook()` returns false: the reminder is unavailable and unprovable while that configuration stands (honest diagnostics instead of a silent copy that does not work; a refusal to resolve the path - `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, for instance - is also unavailable-with-a-warning and never «active»; the location of the configured hook is not codkit's business). Exception 3: a FOREIGN `hooks/pre-commit` (without the ownership marker `# codkit-hook v1`) is neither overwritten nor chained to: a warning, false, and the bytes are preserved exactly - the same ownership discipline as for the patch-set hooks (REPAIR-006). AN OPEN ARCHITECTURAL POINT (with the owner for consideration): a worktree-scoped hook requires `extensions.worktreeConfig` and management of a per-worktree `core.hooksPath`; it is not authorized in this task. Upstream installs no hooks (the `hooks/` of the effective location is empty apart from LFS) - the place is free. The implementation is a step of `load` (PROP-008 §3), acceptance scenario S20. @status:impl/done

**The naming scheme of the published release refs.** The `codkit/release/…` namespace and the trailers are defined; the final versioning scheme of the product is not. The default: the branches `codkit/release/<short-sha patchset>+<pin.tag>`, the release tags `patchset-v<semver>+<pin.tag>` (both coordinates in the name). **It requires an owner decision** once a real release process of the product appears. @status:spec/plan

codkit PROP-014: The standards package and licence markup

Codkit ships a **standards package** — a vibe package of kind `flow` with norms for a patch-set repository — and can deliver it into a product repository with `codkit standards load`, so that an ordinary `vibe install` materializes it from there. Every file of the package carries machine-readable licence information, and it is checked algorithmically before any write into someone else's repository: a package that fails the check is copied nowhere, and no bypass flag exists. @status:spec/done

Terms. The **standards package** is the directory `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/v<version>/` in toolRoot. The **installed copy** is the same directory relative to patchesDir. The **managed manifest block** is the lines of the product `vibe.toml` between the markers `# codkit:begin standards` and `# codkit:end standards`. A **carrier** is where a file's licence information lives: a header comment in the file itself or an adjacent sidecar `<file name>.license`. The **licence policy** is `toolRoot/config/license-policy.json`. A **holder** is a string from the `holders` of the policy. @status:spec/done
1. The standards package

The only source of the package is `toolRoot/vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/v<version>/`; exactly one `v*` directory exists at that location, otherwise the Codkit installation is corrupted (`CK-E-INTERNAL`). The version is read from `[package] version` of the package `vibe.toml` with the regular expression `^version = "([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)"$` and must match the directory name without the `v`. @status:spec/done

**Shipped packages (development version 1.0.0).** Every package of the set carries 1.0.0 and is changed in place under that number (`DEV-VERSION-IS-1-0-0` in the conventions, `DECISION-STD-MUTABLE-EDITION` below). The tool ships a **set** of vibe packages under `toolRoot/vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/<name>/v<version>/`; every name has exactly one `v*` directory, otherwise `CK-E-INTERNAL`. The set: `standards` (mandatory, the edition of the norms) and `agent-skills` (the agent skills, §1a). `codkit standards load` delivers **every** shipped package in one run; `standards check` checks them all; the components block of the notice lists them all (`STD-NOTICE-COMPONENTS-BLOCK` already walks `org.vibevm.codkit/*`). Decision D-S3-1 of campaign CODKIT-STANDARDS-03: one delivery instead of a second command; a separate package instead of skills inside the standard, because the version of a norm must not change when a harness procedure is edited. @status:spec/plan

The package identity is `(group, name, version)` = `(org.vibevm.codkit, standards, <version>)`; the manifest `vibe.toml` carries `kind = "flow"`, `license = "UPL-1.0"` and a `[boot_snippet]` with `category = "flow"`. The content of an edition under a released version never changes; a change to a standard is a new version. @status:spec/done

The mandatory files of the package: `vibe.toml`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` (without an extension — licence detectors compare its text with the canonical one), `LICENSES/<ID>.txt` for every licence used in a carrier, `REUSE.toml`, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` (only when there are third-party files), the boot snippet named by `[boot_snippet] source`, and at least one document under `vibevm/vibespecs/flows/standards/`. The prose of the standards, the boot snippet and the package README are English (owner decision of 2026-09-06, `DECISION-STD-LANGUAGE`); the licence notice in every carrier, in `LICENSE` and in the README is given twice — in English and in Russian (`LIC-NOTICE-BILINGUAL`); the UPL text is English only. Codkit as a whole is released under UPL-1.0 (owner decision of 2026-09-06, verbatim: «Поменять лицензию Codkit на UPL»): the root `LICENSE.md` (the notice in English and in Russian, then the UPL text, then a paragraph about third-party dependencies), `package.json` `license = "UPL-1.0"`, the root entry of `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, the anchor in `common/PROP-000` (the tombstone `LICENSE-PROPRIETARY`, the new `LICENSE-UPL`) and the risk row `CK-R-LEGAL-001` change in one commit (the `licensing` flow: every licence statement together).
