4. The `runtime load|check` commands; delivered files in `verify`, `save`, `inventory`

`codkit runtime load [--dry-run] [--upgrade]` (patchesDir only, the tree is not read): (1) the source is the single version directory in toolRoot and the version literal (`RT-VERSION-LITERAL`; otherwise `CK-E-RUNTIME-PACKAGE`, exit 2); (2) the licence gate is `LIC-CHECK-ALGORITHM` over the version directory with the policy of Codkit → 0 problems, otherwise `CK-E-LICENSE-PACKAGE` with the list, exit 2 and not a single write; (3) the target `delta/own/codkit/` without the notice file: `absent` / `identical` / `drift` by a comparison of the trees; a `drift` without `--upgrade` is `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` with the paths, exit 1 and not a single write; (4) `--dry-run` prints the plan (the created/replaced/removed paths) and exits 0; (5) the directory is written into a temporary directory and renamed as a whole, and the notice file in the target is preserved; (6) the notice goes into both roots per PROP-014 §4a (`STD-LOAD-STEP-WRITE-NOTICE`, the block of components); (7) the report `{ command: 'runtime load', version, target, state: 'created' | 'upgraded' | 'unchanged', files: { written, removed }, notice }` and three hints: the graft `import '../codkit/browser/featureFlags.contribution.js';` in the composition root of the product, the `code-import-patterns` block per `LAYERS.md`, and the first feature through `codkit gen feature`. @status:spec/done

`--upgrade` replaces the directory as a whole without comparing it with the previous version (Codkit keeps no old versions and does not merge): it prints the list of the removed and the replaced paths; without the flag any drift is a refusal, so edits to what was delivered are lost only by an explicit decision. @status:spec/done

`codkit runtime check` is read-only: `identical` → 0; `absent` → 0 with the text `runtime not installed`; `drift` → `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` with the paths, exit 1; plus the state of the copies of the notice per PROP-014 §4a. `--json`: `data: {target:{state, version, paths}, noticeFiles}` - the same key as `standards check` has (PROP-007 §25 `CMD-RUNTIME-CHECK`). @status:spec/done

The files under `delta/own/codkit/**` are delivered by Codkit (PROP-005 `OWN-DELIVERED-BY-CODKIT`): they are not covered by units and do not count as code of the product; `verify` compares the installed copy with the shipped version (`CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` on a difference) and rejects an own unit with a root inside `codkit/` (`CK-E-OWN-UNDER-CODKIT`). @status:spec/done

`save` refuses with `CK-E-DELIVERED-EDIT` and a list when a file of the tree under `src/vs/<ownDirName>/codkit/**` differs from `delta/own/codkit/**` or is absent from the delta; nothing is mirrored. Hint: change it in Codkit and run `runtime load --upgrade`. @status:spec/done
The inventory shows the installed library as one synthetic entry `CK-codkit-runtime` (layer `own`, category `delivered`, a `reason` carrying the version), not as files. @status:spec/done

The release branch of `publish` carries the files of the library: each of them carries its own header, and the condition of UPL is satisfied; only the notice file is excluded (PROP-014 §4a `STD-NOTICE-RELEASE-EXCLUSION`). @status:spec/done

The generated files are code of the product: the header is written from `--holder`/`--license` (the year is `--year` or the current one) in one of two styles. `--header-style line` (the default) is four `//` lines: the copyright first, the SPDX last. `--header-style block` is a block comment of the upstream shape: the line `/*---…---`, ` *  Copyright (c) <year> <holder>. All rights reserved.`, ` *  Licensed under the <license> licence. The full licence text is the licence file of this repository.`, ` *  SPDX-License-Identifier: <license>`, the line ` *---…---*/` - so that the own code of a product looks like the upstream code next to it (`MI-SAME-SHAPE-AS-UPSTREAMS-PARALLEL-SYSTEM`). `--header-file <path>` (a path relative to patchesDir) writes the header verbatim from a file of the product - for shapes that the fields cannot express; the file must end with a line break; it does not combine with `--holder`/`--license`/`--year`/`--header-style` - exit 2, nothing written. `--header-style` without `--holder`/`--license` is exit 2 (there is nothing to shape). Without the header flags the files are written with no header and with the warning `no header written; pass --holder and --license, or --header-file`. The header of Codkit is never written into the files of a product. @status:spec/done

codkit PROP-016: Project types
1. Purpose and vocabulary

The engine of Codkit - patch sets, grafts, the own layer, the drift guard, `load`/`save`/`sync`, the generated branch, `cycle`, `rebase-onto-pin`, `publish`, licensing, standards delivery, the agent protocol - is universal. What is not universal is the knowledge of one family of upstreams: where own code lives, which file is the product manifest, how a service is overridden, how the tree is built and tested, which icons a distribution carries. Until now that knowledge sat inline in the engine and was VS Code's. A **project type** carries it instead, so that the same tool serves several VS Code forks, several Theia forks, and later products that are not IDEs. @status:spec/plan

A **project type** (short: type) is the tool's knowledge of one family of upstreams, shipped as one package and named by one identifier: `vscode`, `generic`, `theia`, later others. A patch set declares exactly one type. The engine asks the type; it never states a type's facts itself. @status:spec/done

A **capability** is a named optional ability a type declares (`brand-images`, `gen-brand`, `build-channels`, `runtime-library`, `own-extensions`, `service-override`, `entry-module`, `config-overlay`, `dev-channel`, `upgrade-advisory`). A verb that needs a capability refuses when the type does not declare it (`TYPE-CAPABILITY-REFUSAL`). @status:spec/done

A **type package** is the npm package that implements a type against the contract package `@codkit/type-api`: `@codkit/type-vscode`, `@codkit/type-generic`, `@codkit/type-theia`. The tool repository is an npm workspace holding the CLI package and the official type packages side by side; each is published on its own at the development version 1.0.0 (`DEV-VERSION-IS-1-0-0`). @status:spec/plan
2. The contract: ten questions a type answers

The contract is exactly the list of variation points measured in the engine (DESIGN-001 §1); a question is added to it only when a second type needs it, never in anticipation. Each area below is one object of small functions on the `ProjectType` interface of `@codkit/type-api`. The tenth area, generators, was added on 2026-09-09 exactly so: the second type needs a different skeleton (an inversify container module instead of a workbench contribution) and has no string-funnel graft at all. @status:spec/done

**Upstream identity.** The tag pattern a pin may use, how a pin resolves to `tag@sha@date` (universal form), the fingerprints `check-tree` requires of a healthy tree (manifest name, marker files), the anchor policy. @status:spec/done

**Tree layout.** The own root (`typeConfig.ownRoot`, a path from the tree root: `src/vs/<name>` for VS Code, a workspace package for Theia), whether own extensions exist and where they materialize, the cleanup whitelist of build outputs the fresh pass may remove, the forbidden patch targets, type-specific marker comment forms if any. @status:spec/done

**Layers.** `own`, `patch`, `resource-file` and `rewrite-rule` are universal and always present. `config-overlay` takes its targets and its optional dev channel from the type (VS Code: `product.json` with `product.overrides.json`). `own-extension` takes its materializer from the type (VS Code: `extensions/<name>`). `service-override` takes its verifier from the type (VS Code: `registerSingleton`; Theia: an inversify `rebind` in a container module). `entry-module` takes its locator from the type (VS Code: `workbench.common.main.ts`; Theia: the application's module list). A layer the type does not provide is absent for that patch set: `verify` refuses an artifact of that layer with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`. @status:spec/done

**Build and test.** The dependency install, the hygiene and lint scripts, the compile channels behind `build up|down|status|errors` and the foreign-watcher markers, the test runner with an own-root glob, the package build and the stamps it needs. `ci --profile build` is one universal skeleton (PROP-011) whose steps call these answers. @status:spec/done

**Upgrade advisory.** The semantic readers the cycle runs between two pins (VS Code: built-in extensions of `product.json`, Electron and TypeScript versions). The advisory's frame - what changed, what it means, what to do - is the engine's. @status:spec/done
**Brand images** (capability `brand-images`). The target table of the distribution's icons and image forms; the generator, the index and the verifier are the engine's. @status:spec/done
**Runtime library** (capability `runtime-library`). Which shipped runtime package the type delivers with `codkit runtime load` (today's library becomes `runtime-vscode`). @status:spec/done

**Standards and skills.** The standard `minimal-intervention` is universal; the seam catalogue and the list "how upstream would build it" that `ck-intervene` routes through come from the type's packages (`seams-vscode`). @status:spec/done

**Conventions.** The subsystems of intervention ids, the forbidden service ids, the defaults of `conventions.json` a product may extend through `conventionsExtensionFile`; the marker grammar and the id pattern's shape stay the engine's. @status:spec/done

**Generators.** The skeletons `gen feature` writes (the feature class, its flag declaration, its test) and the string-funnel graft `gen brand` prints are the type's: for VS Code a workbench contribution with DI and the `nls.ts` hook, for Theia an inversify container module with a preference-backed flag and no funnel graft (capability `gen-brand` absent). The engine owns the command, the header handling (`GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`), the refusal over existing files and the test location rule; the type supplies the templates and the reminders. @status:spec/plan

**What the engine never knows.** No module of the CLI package names a type's fact: no `product.json`, no `src/vs/`, no `extensions/`, no `registerSingleton`, no `npm run hygiene`, no icon table. The graft budget, the marker grammar, the drift guard's predicate, the sacrifice by name of `--discard`, the licence carriers, the generated branch, the cycle's transactions and the standards protocol belong to the engine and are forbidden to consult the type. A grep of the CLI package for the VS Code tokens of DESIGN-001 §1 is a gate of phase P2 and prints zero. @status:spec/plan
3. Types are packages

Workspace layout of the tool repository: `packages/codkit` (the CLI and the engine; the binary `codkit`), `packages/type-api` (the contract), `packages/type-vscode`, `packages/type-generic`, `packages/type-theia`. Each package has its own `package.json`, tests and licence carriers; the floor runs over the workspace. The split happens once, in phase P2, and every later type is born as a package. @status:spec/plan

The engine holds a **registry of the package names it will load**, keyed by type identifier (`vscode` → `@codkit/type-vscode`). A type is resolved by a dynamic import of that package from the CLI package's own dependencies; the official types are regular dependencies of the CLI package. No module is loaded from a patch set or from an arbitrary path: determinism, the air-gapped circuit and the clean room all want the set of loadable code fixed by the tool's own release. Adding a type is publishing its package and adding its name to the registry. @status:spec/done

A `type` the registry does not know, or whose package is not installed, is `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN`, exit 2, naming the identifier and the package the registry expected; no command proceeds without a type. @status:spec/done

The air-gapped supply kit (PROP-011) carries the CLI package and every official type package as tarballs; `npm pack` of the workspace produces them; the kit's manifest lists them with their versions and hashes. @status:spec/plan

`@codkit/type-api` is the only import a type package may take from the tool; the CLI package imports the type only through the interface. A change of the interface is a change of every official type in the same commit of the workspace (the workspace is one repository precisely so that this stays atomic). @status:spec/plan
4. Configuration

`codkit.json` schema 2 has `"type": "<identifier>"` and `"typeConfig": { ... }`. The engine validates the universal fields; the type validates `typeConfig` with its own schema and refuses with `CK-E-CONFIG` naming the field. One patch set, one type. @status:spec/done

Schema 2 is the only schema: a `codkit.json` without `type` (schema 1) is refused with `CK-E-CONFIG` that names the two fields to add (`type`, `typeConfig.ownRoot`) and nothing else; no command reads schema 1 and no code path infers a type. There is one consumer of the tool today and it is migrated in the campaign (phase P2: its `codkit.json` gets `"type": "vscode"` and `"typeConfig": {"ownRoot": "src/vs/patchset"}`, and its gates - `verify`, `status`, `ci --profile build`, the static proof, the dev and package UI proofs - run on the migrated configuration). Owner ruling of 2026-09-09. @status:spec/done

The own root is a **full path from the tree root** in `typeConfig.ownRoot`; the field is required, the type supplies its constraints (VS Code: under `src/vs/`; Theia: a workspace package directory) and refuses a root outside them with `CK-E-CONFIG`. The engine treats the own root as an opaque directory: mirrored by content, excluded from the drift guard, named in the inventory. @status:spec/done

Several forks are several patch sets, each bound to its own fork tree per command (`--patches-dir`, `--fork-dir`, the local config), exactly as today (`GOAL-ANY-FORK`). Two forks of one upstream are two patch sets of one type; forks of different upstreams are patch sets of different types. Sharing between forks travels through packages (standards, runtime, skills), never through the tool's configuration. A workspace file naming several patch sets is a later convenience and is not part of phases P1-P5. @status:spec/done
5. CLI

The verbs of the roster (PROP-007 `COMMAND-ROSTER`) are universal and keep their names, flags and exit codes. Their output names the type where it matters: `where` prints it, the JSON envelope carries `codkit.type`. @status:spec/done

A verb that needs a capability the type does not declare refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`, exit 2, naming the type and the capability, before any write; no verb silently does something else. The verbs that need one: `imageset *` (`brand-images`), `gen brand` (`gen-brand`), `build *` (`build-channels`), `runtime load|check` (`runtime-library`), and `verify` over an artifact of a layer the type does not provide. @status:spec/done

`codkit types` - print the registered types, their package and version, and the capability matrix; `--json`: `data: {types: [{id, package, version, installed, capabilities}]}`. Read-only, no patch set required. @status:spec/done

New codes: `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN` (type not registered or package not installed), `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` (verb or layer outside the type's capabilities). A type may add codes only under its own prefix (`CK-E-VSCODE-…`) for facts the engine cannot state; every code has an FAQ entry (PROP-012). @status:spec/done
6. The official types

`vscode` - today's behaviour, extracted without change: the specification module `modules/vscode` holds its answers (layout `src/vs/<own>` and `extensions/`, the `product.json` overlay with the `product.overrides.json` dev channel, built-in extensions, `registerSingleton`, `workbench.common.main`, `npm ci`/hygiene/eslint/watch channels/`test-node`, the package build and its stamps, the advisory readers, the brand image set, the runtime library, the seam catalogue, the conventions). The product's gates - `verify`, `status`, `ci --profile build`, its static proof and UI proofs - are the regression net of the extraction. @status:spec/plan

`generic` - a plain git upstream with no product model: no extensions, no service overrides, no entry module, no dev channel, no brand images, no runtime library; the install, lint, compile and test commands are declared in `typeConfig`; the own root is a configured directory. It carries `own`, `patch`, `resource-file`, `rewrite-rule` and `config-overlay` over declared JSON targets without a dev channel, so that `load|save|verify|cycle|publish|ci` run over any upstream before its own type exists. Its polygon is a **synthetic repository** in the fixtures (owner ruling). @status:spec/plan

`theia` - the second real type, designed from the facts of Theia master (`research/theia-facts-<version>`) and specified in `modules/theia`: the own root as a workspace package, the application manifest as the overlay target, inversify `rebind` as the service override, the application's module list as the entry module, yarn/lerna build and watch, its test runner, electron-builder packaging, its advisory readers. It is proved by a real product of the owner built on it, in that product's own repository, the way the VS Code product was built. @status:spec/plan
7. Testing

The engine's tests run against a **stub type** in the fixtures that answers the contract with the smallest possible layout; they never import an official type. Each type package has its own suites and its own polygon; FEAT-001 becomes two polygons - the VS Code-shaped one it is today and the synthetic generic one. @status:spec/plan

Acceptance scenarios (FEAT-002): a schema-1 patch set is refused with `CK-E-CONFIG` naming `type` and `typeConfig.ownRoot`; the migrated VS Code patch set behaves exactly as before; `codkit types` lists the official types; `imageset` over a `generic` patch set refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`; a `type` the registry does not know refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN`; the generic polygon passes `load`, `save`, `verify`, `cycle` and `ci --profile verify` end to end; the VS Code polygon passes every scenario it passed before the split. @status:spec/plan
8. Specifications: the split

`modules/codkit` specifies the engine and this contract; `modules/vscode` specifies the `vscode` type; `modules/theia` will specify the `theia` type; `common/*` states the vision without naming an upstream. A fact that is a type's answer moves to the type's module; a fact about the engine stays. @status:spec/plan

Anchors are immutable: a moved fact leaves a tombstone at its old address naming the new one (`NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR`), and every `##ANCHOR` citation in code is re-pointed in the same commit; `trace:check` and the spec map are the gates. The unit count of the two modules together equals the count before the split plus the tombstones and the new facts of this document. @status:spec/plan
The type modules of the tool are English like the rest of the tool's specifications (`SPEC-LANGUAGE-IS-ENGLISH`); a product's specifications keep the product's own rule. @status:spec/plan
9. Decisions

**Decision:** a type is a separate npm package from the first day, resolved through a registry of names. **Why:** the owner's ruling - the procedure of splitting is done once; a package boundary that exists only in a directory drifts back into the engine. **Considered and rejected:** in-tree directories under one package (cheaper now, a second split later); arbitrary plugin loading from a patch set (breaks determinism, the air-gapped kit and the clean room). **When to revisit:** a third party ships a type - then the registry becomes a declared list in the tool's configuration rather than a constant. @status:spec/done

**Decision:** no compatibility layer for the old configuration schema: schema 2 is required, schema 1 is refused with a migration hint. **Why:** the owner's ruling of 2026-09-09 - the tool has one consumer, and fixing it is cheaper than building a compatibility layer and maintaining it afterwards; the consumer is migrated inside the campaign with its gates as the proof. **Considered and rejected:** reading schema 1 as `vscode` (a second code path, a second set of tests, and a rule that would outlive its only reason). **When to revisit:** never for schema 1; a future schema change gets the same treatment while the consumers can be counted on one hand. @status:spec/done

**Decision:** the contract's areas are the measured variation points and nothing else. **Why:** an interface designed for one real type fits that type; the `generic` type and the Theia type are the two forces that keep it honest, and each new question is added when a type needs it. **Considered and rejected:** a general "hooks everywhere" plugin API (speculative surface, untestable). **When to revisit:** a third real type that needs a tenth question. @status:spec/plan
vscode PROP-001: The `vscode` project type - overview and module map

`vscode` is the project type (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-TERM`) that carries the tool's knowledge of the Visual Studio Code family of upstreams: where own code lives, which file is the product manifest, how a service is overridden, how the tree is built and tested, which images a distribution carries, which library the runtime capability delivers. The engine of `modules/codkit` asks the nine questions of the contract (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-CONTRACT-IS-CLOSED`); this module is the set of answers, and nothing here is a fact about the engine. @status:spec/done

The type is today's behaviour extracted without change (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-VSCODE`). Every fact of this module that carries an anchor moved here from `modules/codkit` in the specification split of PROP-016 phase P1 and moved **verbatim**, keeping its anchor, its wording and its status; the old address holds a tombstone and stays valid for citations (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-SPEC-TOMBSTONES`). A fact with no tombstone behind it is new with this module and says so by its status. @status:spec/plan
1. Module map

Module contents: PROP-001 the type and this map; PROP-002 tree layout - the own root, own extensions, the cleanup whitelist, the forbidden patch targets; PROP-003 layers - the `product.json` overlay with its `product.overrides.json` dev channel, the built-in extensions, the `registerSingleton` service override, the entry modules; PROP-004 build and test - the dependency install, hygiene and eslint, the watch channels and their pass boundaries, the test runners and the package build with its stamps; PROP-005 the readers of the upgrade advisory; PROP-006 the brand image set - the target table and the artwork families; PROP-007 the runtime library delivered by the `runtime-library` capability; PROP-008 the generators - the feature skeleton, the brand table and the `nls.ts` hook; PROP-009 the conventions defaults - the subsystems of intervention ids and the forbidden service ids. The contract these answer is `modules/codkit/PROP-016`; the neighbouring measurement of the upstream is `research/vscode-facts-1.135`. @status:spec/done
2. Declared capabilities

The type declares every optional capability of `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-TERM-CAPABILITY`: `brand-images`, `gen-brand`, `build-channels`, `runtime-library`, `own-extensions`, `service-override`, `entry-module`, `config-overlay`, `dev-channel`, `upgrade-advisory`. No verb of the roster refuses over a `vscode` patch set for want of a capability, which is what makes the extraction invisible to the existing product. @status:spec/done
3. Upstream identity

The type's answer to the identity question (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-IDENTITY`): the pin tag is an upstream release tag of the form `<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (`1.135.0`); a healthy tree carries `product.json` and `package.json` at its root and `src/vs/` below it; the origin is proved by the reachability of the anchor commit of the microsoft/vscode history, and the anchor policy is the engine's `ANCHOR-COMMIT-RULE` computed once per patch set. The resolution of a pin into `tag@sha@date` is universal and stays the engine's. @status:spec/done
vscode PROP-002: Tree layout - the own root, own extensions, cleanup, forbidden targets
1. Where own code lives
The directory is placed under `src/vs/<ownDirName>/`; on every new pin the cycle checks that the actual tsconfig, layering, test and nls globs of the selected fork cover that path. @status:spec/done

The type's constraint on `typeConfig.ownRoot` is that the own root lies under `src/vs/` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-OWN-ROOT`); a root outside it is `CK-E-CONFIG` naming the constraint. The field is required and has no default - schema 2 is the only schema (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-SCHEMA-2-REQUIRED`). The engine treats the root as an opaque directory - mirrored by content, excluded from the drift guard, named in the inventory - and only this type knows why it has to sit under `src/vs/`: the tsconfig, layering, test and nls globs of the distribution are anchored there. @status:spec/done
2. Own extensions

The `own-extension` kind of unit: the directory `delta/own-extensions/<name>/**` is mirrored into `<tree>/extensions/<name>/**` (the rsync semantics of `OWN-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH`: `load` into the tree, `save` back, `ci` into the own commit of the generated branch). The declaration is the section `extensions: [{ id, name, owner, reason, pin, contractTests }]` of the `patchset.delta.json` manifest (schema `codkitOwnManifest: 2`, an absent section is admissible); `name` has the form `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` and is unique; the directory must contain the `package.json` of the extension; a directory under `delta/own-extensions/` that is declared by no entry is a violation as well (otherwise it silently fails to materialize, the analogue of `OWN-UNCOVERED`); a violation is `CK-E-OWN-EXTENSION-MANIFEST`; an extension named after an existing upstream directory `extensions/<name>` on the pin is the same refusal with the text `name collides with an upstream extension`. Drift between the tree and the delta is `CK-E-OWN-EXTENSION-DRIFT` in `verify`. In the inventory it is an entry with layer `own` and category `own-extension`. An empty section is serialized as absent (the canonical bytes of the manifest do not change). The managed block of `info/exclude` (`OWN-EXCLUDED-LOCALLY`) does not cover extensions: `git status` shows `extensions/<name>/` as untracked, and the dirt guards filter it by prefix; extending the block to extensions is a separate rule (deferred). @status:spec/done

Removing the declaration does not remove the materialization: `load` mirrors only the declared extensions, while the directory `<tree>/extensions/<name>/` of a removed extension stays in the tree untracked - it is removed by `load --fresh` (the cleanup of untracked paths, PROP-011 §4), and no other command deletes it (an untracked directory under `extensions/` may equally be a person's local experiment); a plain `load` over such a tree passes and does not touch the directory - the drift guard does not count a stranded materialization as dirt (PROP-008 `DRIFT-GUARD-PREDICATE`, the exception of 2026-09-08: `load` neither writes into that directory nor deletes it, so a refusal would guard nothing), and for the other commands nothing changes: `cycle start` refuses with `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE`, `sync` with `CK-E-NEW-FILE-IN-UPSTREAM-ZONE`, and `ci` and `publish` remove the untracked paths with a fresh pass. So that this is not silent, `status` names such directories stranded materializations (PROP-007 `CMD-STATUS`): an untracked directory under `extensions/` that is covered by no declaration and does not exist on the pin. Observed by the product campaign of 2026-09-08. @status:spec/done

Why the layer: a language pack for the strings of own code (`contributes.localizations`), themes and a product icon theme, a walkthrough, `configurationDefaults` - all of this is the Extension API, the most sanctioned seam after `product.json`; without the layer such files would go one by one as add-file patches (`NEW-FILES-LIVE-IN-OWN`). An upstream build fact: a declarative extension is picked up by the glob `extensions/*/package.json` without build edits; an extension with TypeScript requires two entries in the build lists (`build/gulpfile.extensions.ts`, `build/npm/dirs.ts`) - those are two artifacts of the constant graft set (`CONSTANT-GRAFT-SET`), not part of the layer. @status:spec/done
3. The lint target of the own directory

An upstream fact: a file without a target in `local/code-import-patterns` gets the warning "Missing definition…", and warnings mean failure; a new directory requires a target in `eslint.config.js` (one block) or an entry in `.eslint-ignore`. The rule: **one patch `CK-build-003`** adds a marked target block for `src/vs/patchset/**` to `eslint.config.js` (next to the entry-module blocks, `eslint.config.js:1975+`). @status:spec/done
4. The cleanup whitelist and the forbidden patch targets

The build outputs the fresh pass may remove without asking, that is the value of `cleanupWhitelist` for this type: `node_modules/` at any level, `.build/`, the anchored `/out*/`, `extensions/*/out/`, `extensions/*/dist/`, `.eslintcache`, `*.tsbuildinfo`. The pattern semantics, the algorithm that computes the untracked set and the discipline "what is not in the list is deleted" are the engine's (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-011#CLEANUP-WHITELIST-CONTENT`); which paths a build of this distribution actually leaves behind is the type's answer, and a second type names its own. @status:spec/done

The forbidden patch targets of this type, that is the value of `forbiddenPatchTargets`: `.config/1espt/**` (a file with mixed line endings that no deterministic patch can carry) together with the overlay targets of PROP-003. The field itself, its additive extension through `conventionsExtensionFile` and the refusal `CK-E-FORBIDDEN-TARGET` are the engine's (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-003#CONV-FORBIDDEN-TARGETS`). @status:spec/done
vscode PROP-003: Layers - the product.json overlay, built-in extensions, service overrides, entry modules
1. config-overlay: the targets and the dev channel

The overlay targets of this type and their channels: `product.json` is the product manifest and the only target with a **dev channel** - the sidecar `product.overrides.json` the bootstrap reads under `VSCODE_DEV`; the `package.json` of the tree is a target without a dev channel and admits the addition of `scripts` keys only. The two-channel machinery, the composition of several overlays of one target, `expectUpstream` and `CK-E-OVERLAY-DRIFT` are the engine's (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#OVERLAY-TWO-CHANNELS`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#OVERLAY-NON-PRODUCT-TARGETS`); which file is the manifest, and whether a dev channel exists at all, is the type's answer. @status:spec/done

Facts: the dev channel `product.overrides.json` works only under `VSCODE_DEV` (`src/bootstrap-meta.ts:21-27`); at packaging time upstream stamps `commit`, `date`, `checksums`, `version` (`gulpfile.vscode.ts:335-361`), so overlay operations do not touch the stamped keys (`overlay check`: an operation on the keys `commit|date|checksums|version` is a warning; the list is aligned with the stamping, M1). Hygiene forbids the key `extensionsGallery` in the root `product.json` (`build/hygiene.ts:92-101`) and does NOT consider `product.overrides.json`, so the dev channel is legal; in CI the build profile runs the upstream hygiene BEFORE the overlay is materialized (the order is fixed in PROP-011 §6). @status:spec/done
2. Built-in extensions

The distribution declares its built-in extensions in the `builtInExtensions` array of `product.json` (each entry naming the extension, its version and the `vsix` source) and picks up the extensions of the tree by the glob `extensions/*/package.json`. Both are the type's knowledge: the overlay may add or remove an entry of that array, the advisory reads its diff between two pins (PROP-005), the air-gapped supply kit fills `.build/builtInExtensions` from it, and an own extension of the patch set materializes next to them (PROP-002 `##OWN-EXTENSION-UNIT`). @status:spec/plan
3. service-override: registerSingleton

The service-override mechanism: an own module calls `registerSingleton` for the same decorator and a compatible InstantiationType after the original registration. The behavior "the last admissible registration wins" must be confirmed by a contract test on the selected pin; bootstrap services from the installed forbidden list must not be overridden. **Coverage (an upstream fact, checked 2026-09-07):** the `registerSingleton` registry is read only by the renderer (`workbench.ts`, a loop without a `has` guard - the last registration wins) and by the extension host; Electron main, the shared process, the server and the CLI assemble services by an explicit `ServiceCollection.set` and do not read the registry, and `IProductService` is set explicitly in every process and cannot be overridden. For those processes the layer that replaces behavior is entry-module: a graft into the service assembly function (`createServices`/`initServices`) with an explicit `set` from an own function. @status:spec/done

The prohibition: ids from `forbiddenServiceIds` (bootstrap services are installed by an explicit `set` before the Workbench is created - an override silently breaks loading). The check is a linter in `verify`: a grep over own code looks for `registerSingleton(<Id>` calls with a forbidden id. @status:spec/done
The minimal integration sample selects a non-bootstrap service from the actual pin and proves the override with an own contract test; the service name is not part of Codkit. @status:spec/done
Late-registration behavior must be confirmed both in development loading and in the packaged bundle; dev-only evidence does not close packaging acceptance. @status:spec/plan
4. entry-module: the locator

The entry modules of this type: the renderer entry is `src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts` with its desktop and web continuations, and the service assembly functions of the processes that do not read the `registerSingleton` registry (`createServices`/`initServices` of the Electron main process, of the shared process, of the server and of the CLI) are the entries a graft targets there. The upstream precedent of a forked import list is `src/vs/sessions/sessions.common.main.ts`. The layer itself - the two forms of the layer, the marker discipline, the `# layer: entry-module` carrier and the rewrite-rule candidacy - is the engine's (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#EM-PURPOSE`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#EM-TWO-FORMS`); the concrete entry is confirmed against the actual chain of the selected fork at every pin. @status:spec/done
vscode PROP-004: Build and test - install, hygiene, watch channels, runners, packaging stamps
1. The commands of the type

The commands the universal `ci --profile build` skeleton calls for this type (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-011#PROFILE-BUILD`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-CI-IMPL`): the dependency install is `npm ci` of the tree and of `build/` (in CI it is supplied out of band and only its receipts are probed); the hygiene script is `npm run hygiene` and the lint script is `npm run eslint`, and both run **before** the overlay targets are materialized, because upstream hygiene is strict about the manifest it checks; the product and contract tests are `npm run test-node -- --runGlob vs/<ownRoot leaf>/**/test/{common,node}/**/*.test.js`; the package build is the upstream `gulp vscode-*` task. The order of the steps, the profiles and the exit codes are the engine's; the names of the scripts are this type's answer. @status:spec/done

**Build commit.** The product package build (`gulp vscode-*`) stamps `product.json.commit` from `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION`, and without it by reading `.git/HEAD` as a directory (`build/lib/git.ts` at pin 1.135.0); a managed tree is a linked worktree, its `.git` is a file, so the package is left without `commit`, and without `commit` the NLS loader does not read language packs. The rule: the packaging step of the release protocol (page 08) exports `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION=<tree HEAD>` (the value is printed by `codkit where --json`/`status`) and `VSCODE_QUALITY`; Codkit neither builds the package nor changes code. @status:spec/plan
2. Watch channels

Traps the wrapper implements: `npm run compile` and a restart of the transpile daemon wipe `out/`, so `build up` does not restart a living channel; before `npm install` in the tree the daemons must be stopped, so `build down --all` is invoked by the deps-advisory protocol; the upstream `watchd` scripts and our channels are mutually exclusive, so `up` refuses to start when a foreign watch process over the same tree is detected (probing by the command-line substrings `build/next/index.ts transpile --watch` and `gulp watch-`). @status:spec/done
3. Pass boundaries and error lines

`falseEndGuards`: the lines `Finished compilation <id> with … errors` with a non-empty `<id>` come from the code-generation channels (`api-proposal-names`, `extension-point-names`), which print their markers on every change; a naive match yields false pass ends. M1 refinement: with strict `passEnd` expressions the guards are defence in depth and become load-bearing only when `passEnd` is weakened; the count lines are separated into their own data field `errorCountLine` (for typecheck/copilot the count line is not a diagnostic; extensions has NO count field, and the authority there is the parsed diagnostics, REPAIR-003/006). @status:impl/done
4. Test runners

**The split by runners.** `--runGlob` bypasses the regular layer exclusion of the upstream node runner, and a suite that brings up the workbench pulls in style sheets that node does not load; therefore `ci --profile build` runs the node runner over the glob `vs/<own>/**/test/{common,node}/**/*.test.js`, while the `test/browser` suites of the product, of the library and of the features are a mandatory protocol step outside `ci`: the upstream electron runner (`scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/<own>/**/test/browser/**/*.test.js'`, under `xvfb-run` on a machine without a display), because a CI container without a display cannot make it mandatory for the profile. @status:spec/plan
vscode PROP-005: The readers of the upgrade advisory
1. What the advisory reads between two pins

The semantic readers the cycle runs over the `oldPin..newPin` diff for this type: the files `.nvmrc`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `build/npm/dirs.ts`; the `builtInExtensions` entries of `product.json`; the Electron version and the TypeScript version, read by grep over `build/lib/electron.ts` and `package.json`. Each reader answers "what changed in the toolchain of this distribution"; a reader that finds nothing contributes no line. @status:spec/plan

The frame around these readings - the `deps-advisory` phase, the stop for a human in interactive mode with exit 3, the log line under `--ci`, and the protocol step "stop the daemons with `build down --all` before `npm install` in the tree" - belongs to the engine (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-009#PHASE-DEPS-ADVISORY`). Only the list of readers is the type's, and a type that declares no `upgrade-advisory` capability makes the phase an empty report rather than a refusal. @status:spec/plan
vscode PROP-006: The brand image set - the target table and the artwork families
1. The target table

The targets are discovered, not hard-coded. The set of paths is built-in knowledge of the distribution (fixed paths and globs). The application icon: `resources/win32/code.ico`, `resources/darwin/code.icns`, `resources/linux/code.png`, `resources/win32/code_*.png`, `resources/linux/rpm/*.xpm`, `resources/server/favicon.ico`, `resources/server/code-*.png`. The installer graphics: `resources/win32/inno-big-*.bmp`, `resources/win32/inno-small-*.bmp`. The file-type icons: `resources/win32/*.ico` and `resources/darwin/*.icns` - minus `code.ico` and `code.icns`, and the subtraction is declared by an explicit `exclude` list rather than by the order of the patterns: a glob that silently took someone else's target would give two map entries for one path. The empty-editor watermarks: `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/media/letterpress-*.svg` and `src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/media/letterpress-*.svg`. A missing fixed path is printed; a glob without matches yields no target; one file captured by two patterns is `CK-E-ARTIFACT-BROKEN` and not a silent duplicate (that is a defect of the pattern table, and it has to be loud). The structure of every existing file is read from its bytes: the list of ICO frames and their sizes in directory order, the types and sizes of the ICNS elements, the sizes of BMP/XPM/PNG, the nominal size of an SVG from `width`/`height` or `viewBox` - a change upstream to the set of frames, types or sizes is picked up automatically instead of being missed. ICNS: the PNG-capable elements `ic07 ic08 ic09 ic10 ic11 ic12 ic13 ic14` are regenerated; the legacy elements (the compressed miniatures `ic04`/`ic05`, the `info` chunk) carry no PNG and are not reproduced - they are listed in the report and in `data.targets[].legacyTypes`. On the 1.135.0 upstream tree this is **84 targets and 370 required sizes**, and neither number is written down in the code. @status:impl/done

**Decision:** the role of every target - "where a human sees this image" - is codkit's knowledge: it lives in the path table `packages/codkit/src/lib/imagesetTargets.ts` and is worded without the name of any downstream product.

**Why:** The role is what whoever draws needs, and it is a property of the layout of the distribution rather than of a particular product: `resources/win32/code.ico` is the icon of the executable, of the taskbar button, of the shortcut and of the file associations; `resources/win32/inno-small-*.bmp` is the header of every page of the installation wizard; `resources/linux/rpm/*.xpm` is the icon of the package in the menu of RPM distributions. codkit is a universal tool, so the name of a product in its texts would be a leak; this is checked by a test that looks for the forbidden substrings in the rendered index.

**Considered and rejected:**
- keeping the roles in the product repository - every product would rewrite the same knowledge about upstream;
- not writing the role at all - the index stops being a document worth handing to an agent.

**When to revisit:** when upstream adds a target whose role is not derivable from its path - then the table needs a source and not a guess. @status:impl/done
2. Families and artworks

A target names two different things, and they must not be confused. The **family** is the guard group and the masters directory: one contract test covers the whole family at once. The **artwork** is which drawing inside the family the target wants. There are five families: `icon` (one drawing over nine targets - ico, icns, png, xpm, two Start tiles, a favicon and two web-manifest icons), `installer-big` and `installer-small` (one drawing over seven targets each), `filetype` (28 drawings over 55 targets: the Windows and macOS sets overlap, and one type exists on macOS only) and `letterpress` (6 drawings over 6 targets). The master key is the family for a family with one drawing and `<family>/<artwork>` for a family with several. The identifier of the guard test is derived from the FAMILY and not from the artwork (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-GUARD-PER-FAMILY`): `guard.brand.filetype` covers all 55 file-type files instead of requiring 55 suites. @status:impl/done

**Decision:** the command covers the whole brand surface of the distribution - the application icon, the installer graphics, the file-type icons, the web client's icons and the empty-editor watermarks - and not the application icon alone.

**Why:** The owner's direction of 2026-09-06. A rebranding that left 55 file-type icons as upstream's is not a rebranding but a half-finished thing: the user sees somebody else's mark in the file explorer on every file of the project. The difference in cost is small, because the whole expensive part - the discovery of the structure, the codecs, the pipeline - is written already and does not depend on the number of targets: growing from 20 targets to 84 added a pattern table and the split between family and artwork, but not one new codec.

**Considered and rejected:**
- limiting it to the application icon - it leaves the most visible part of somebody else's artwork inside the product and postpones exactly the work of splitting family from artwork that will have to be done anyway;
- moving the file-type icons into a separate command - the same pipeline, the same containers, the same masters; the second command would be a copy of the first with a different list of paths.

**When to revisit:** if upstream starts loading brand artwork from a format that is neither a raster container nor an SVG - observed through a target for which neither a codec nor the vector path exists. @status:impl/done
vscode PROP-007: The runtime library - features, flags, brand engine
1. Purpose and the shape of the library

The Codkit runtime is a TypeScript library in the spirit and the style of VS Code, shared by every fork Codkit maintains: a feature-flags service built on ports and adapters with observables, a host that creates a feature when its flag turns on and disposes it when the flag turns off, a message branding engine, a simulator of the remote flag source and an inspector. It exists so that the delta of a product is built as a parallel system (services through DI, contributions through registries) rather than as a set of patches, and so that every new feature of a product is isolated in its own directory and switched on by a flag (owner rulings of 2026-09-07). @status:spec/done

This library is what the `runtime-library` capability of the `vscode` type delivers; a second type delivers its own (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-RUNTIME`). Everything about **how** it is delivered - the managed copy, the single version directory in toolRoot, the version literal, `runtime load --upgrade`, `runtime check`, `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT`, the refusal of `save` over a delivered edit and the synthetic inventory entry - is universal and stays with the engine (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-015#RT-IS-A-MANAGED-COPY`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-015#RT-LOAD-STEPS`). Everything about **what** it contains is here. @status:spec/plan

The library consists only of `.ts` and `.md` files: no JSON, no TOML, no images, no `.license` companions - so that it requires from a product neither a build resource allow-list nor hygiene exceptions for foreign extensions; the data lives in TypeScript modules. There are no characters outside ASCII in the code and in the strings (the upstream minifier rejects non-ASCII in its output); Cyrillic is admissible only in the comments of the header. @status:spec/done
2. Architecture

The core of the library (`common/`) depends only on its own ports: the flag source (`IFlagSource`), the provider of the remote snapshot (`IRemoteFlagsProvider`), the context-key publisher, the host restart port and the factory of feature instances. The adapters to the upstream APIs lie in one directory, `browser/adapters/`, and implement the ports over the current APIs; a change of an upstream API changes one adapter, and neither the core nor the features of a product are touched. For processes without a DI registry and without context keys there are null adapters. @status:spec/done

The surface of contact with upstream is narrow and enforced: `common/**` imports only `vs/base/common/**`, `vs/platform/*/common/**` and its own; `browser/**` imports additionally `vs/workbench/common/contributions.js`, `vs/workbench/services/host/browser/host.js`, `vs/workbench/services/lifecycle/common/lifecycle.js`, `vs/platform/*/common/**`; nothing is imported from `vs/workbench/contrib/**`. The same list is the content of `LAYERS.md` and of the `code-import-patterns` block a product installs for the target `src/vs/<ownDirName>/codkit/~`; `shippedRuntime.test.ts` checks the imports of the library with regular expressions over the specifiers. @status:spec/done

The state of a flag is an observable (`observableValue`/`derived` from `vs/base/common/observable.js`), not only an event: `enablement(id)` and `liveState(id)` return `IObservable<FeatureState>`, the host subscribes through `autorun`, and the context key is updated from that same observable; the event `onDidChangeEnablement` remains an adapter for code without observables. This is the current reactive rule of upstream (the instruction `.github/instructions/observables.instructions.md`, hundreds of files with `autorun`/`derived`). @status:spec/done

The flag sources form layers with the fixed precedence `FLAG_LAYER_PRECEDENCE`: `build` (the build value from `product.json` through the `descriptor.product` function) → `policy` (the `inspect().policyValue` of the setting) → `remote-force` (the forcing key of the remote snapshot) → `user` (the first defined of `applicationValue`, `userValue`, `userLocalValue`, `userRemoteValue`) → `remote-default` (the default key of the remote snapshot) → `default` (`descriptor.default`). The build value is cancelled by no other layer: security features stay a property of the build that way. @status:spec/done

`resolveFeature(descriptor, readings)` returns `{ enabled, decidedBy }`: the first defined reading in the order of precedence; the `default` layer is always defined. The function is pure and is covered by a table of tests over every layer. @status:spec/done

Every event of a source (a setting change, a new remote snapshot) recomputes the affected features and applies the result in one `transaction()`: observers see no intermediate states; `onDidChangeEnablement` fires once with the list of the ids that actually changed; context keys are published only for the ones that changed. @status:spec/done

A feature with `hotToggle: false` (a "cold" one) reads `enablement(id)` frozen at its first computation in this session; `liveState(id)` changes meanwhile, `restartPending` holds the ids of every cold feature whose live state differs from the frozen one, and the restart port shows a "Restart" notification once per such change, in the upstream idiom (`INotificationService.prompt` + `IHostService.restart()`). @status:spec/done

The remote source is the same kind of port as any other: `IRemoteFlagsProvider` yields the current snapshot `RemoteFlagsSnapshot { version: 1, force, defaults, issuedAt? }` and the event of its change; `parseRemoteFlagsSnapshot` parses the text strictly (version 1, boolean values, string keys) and on any error returns `undefined`, never throwing. The library contains no network code; a future server implements the port over a shared-process channel. @status:spec/done

The simulator of the remote source is `StorageRemoteFlagsProvider`: the snapshot is kept in `IStorageService` (`StorageScope.APPLICATION`, `StorageTarget.MACHINE`, the key `codkit.features.remoteSnapshot`), is changed by the `simulate(patch)` and `clear()` methods of the `IRemoteFlagsSimulator` port (a `null` value in the patch removes the key) and notifies through `onDidChangeValue`. The internal switching interface and the future server thus walk one and the same path: snapshot → transaction → observables → features and `when`. @status:spec/done

The inspector is `InspectFeatureFlagsAction` (id `codkit.features.inspect`, title `Feature Flags: Inspect`, `f1: true`): a Quick Pick with one line per feature (the state icon, the title, the id, the layer that decided the state, the values by layer, the status of the instance, `restart pending`); selecting a feature opens the actions - enable/disable/reset the user setting (`updateValue(…, ConfigurationTarget.USER)`), simulate a remote `force`/`default` on/off/clear, clear the simulated snapshot. Every string goes through `localize`. @status:spec/done

A feature of a product is an ordinary VS Code class: `extends Disposable`, dependencies through the constructor by DI, and everything the feature adds (commands, menus, views, listeners) registered in `this._register(...)`. **Enabling a feature = creating the instance through `IInstantiationService.createInstance(ctor)`, disabling it = `dispose()`.** There is no base class with a mandatory `activate`: it would call a method of the subclass from the constructor of the base class, before the parameter properties of the subclass are assigned. @status:spec/done

`FeatureHost` (common) holds an `autorun` over `enablement(descriptor.id)`: on → it creates the instance with the factory, off → it calls `dispose()` on the instance; `dispose()` of the host destroys the instance; `state: IObservable<'inactive' | 'active' | 'failed'>`. `FeaturesHostContribution` (browser) is the only workbench contribution of the library (`registerWorkbenchContribution2('codkit.features.host', …, WorkbenchPhase.BlockRestore)`): for every declaration it waits for that declaration's phase through `ILifecycleService.when(phase)` (as the upstream registry of contributions does) and creates a `FeatureHost` with the factory `ctor => instantiationService.createInstance(ctor)`. @status:spec/done

An exception from the constructor of a feature does not bring the workbench down: the host catches it, moves the feature to `failed`, writes an `ILogService.error` and creates no instance; the inspector shows the status. The errors of the library itself are not thrown at runtime (a snapshot with an error is ignored, a missing value is `undefined`); the only exceptions are programming errors at registration (`RT-REGISTER-FEATURE`) and an unknown id in `enablement`/`liveState`/`explain`. @status:spec/done

`registerFeature(descriptor, ctor, phase = WorkbenchPhase.AfterRestored)` (browser) is called while the contribution module of a product is evaluated: `validateFeatureDescriptor` (a violation is a `throw`: an error of the author, caught by a test of the product before any UI); `featureDeclarations.declare({ descriptor, ctor, phase })` (a duplicate id is a `throw`); if there is a `descriptor.setting` and the build does not force the value (`descriptor.product?.(product)` is undefined, where `product` is the static import of `vs/platform/product/common/product.js`, the upstream idiom), then `registerConfiguration` with the node `{ id: setting.id, properties: { [setting.id]: { type: 'boolean', default: descriptor.default, description: setting.description, scope: setting.scope ?? ConfigurationScope.APPLICATION, tags: setting.tags, policy: setting.policy } } }`. A feature forced by the build registers no setting at all. @status:spec/done

`IFeatureDescriptor { id, title, default, hotToggle, setting?, product?, remote? }`; `id` has the form `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*(\.[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*)+$` (two parts or more - the prefix of the product is mandatory by the form); `setting: { id, description, scope?, tags?, policy? }`, where `description` is already localized by the product; `product` is a function of `IProductConfiguration` (the type is extended by the product through augmentation), not a string key: type-safe and without `any`; `remote.key` is the key in the remote snapshot, defaulting to `id`. @status:spec/done

For every declaration the context key `<id>.enabled` (boolean) is published through `IContextKeyService.createKey`; it follows `enablement(id)`, so that the `when` expressions of the menus, the commands and the views of a product react to the flag without any code. @status:spec/done

`createBrandTransform(rules)` returns the pure function `message => message`: the rules `{ find, replace, except? }` are applied in order, `find` is a literal (no RegExp), and a rule is skipped when the message contains any string from `except`; the fast path is that no `find` occurs in the message; the results are cached in an `LRUCache` (2048). `affectedEntries(transform, entries)` returns the keys of the messages the transform changes - for the guard snapshot of a product. The module is pure (`common`, only `vs/base/common/map.js`): a product puts the hook into `_format` (`nls.ts`), which is evaluated in every process, including bootstrap; the hook itself is a patch of the product of type `hook`, and the library does not touch `nls.ts`. @status:spec/done

The library creates no global names and does not read `globalThis` (the upstream rule "Do not introduce new types or values to the global namespace"); the only module singletons are `featureDeclarations` and the service decorator, as in the upstream registries. @status:spec/done
3. The typecheck harness and the tests

The library is compiled against the upstream sources on the pin by the TypeScript of the fork itself: a mirror directory where `src/vs/*` are symbolic links into the fork tree, `src/typings` and `src/vscode-dts` are links, `node_modules` is a link, and the `tsconfig` inherits the `src/tsconfig.base.json` of the fork and includes only the own directory with the library; `tsc --noEmit` → 0. The harness is a procedure of the central session and of the second pass of a product; it is not part of the Codkit `npm run floor` (there are no upstream sources in the repository). The result is recorded in the report of the campaign and in `CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERIFIED_UPSTREAM`. @status:spec/done

The library carries tests in the upstream style (`suite`/`test`, `ensureNoDisposablesAreLeakedInTestSuite`, `assert.deepStrictEqual` snapshots) for its own behavior and **for its assumptions about upstream**: the last registration in a `ServiceCollection` wins; `included: false` removes a property from the configuration registry; `affectsConfiguration` fires on the setting key of a feature. A red contract test on a new pin names the assumption that broke. @status:spec/done

The tests of the library are compiled by the harness but are **executed only in the fork tree** after `runtime load` and `load` (the upstream `test/unit/node` and electron runners find `test/**/*.test.js` under the own directory themselves; `codkit ci --profile build` runs the node runner over the glob `vs/<own>/**/test/**/*.test.js`, which covers `codkit/test/` as well). They are not run in the Codkit vitest: upstream stubs would be a second, false upstream. The limitation is recorded in the campaign as deferred to the second pass of a product. @status:spec/done
4. Decisions

**Decision:** the core on its own ports, the adapters to upstream in one directory, a narrow surface of imports enforced by the linter; no detection of the shape of an upstream API at runtime.

**Why:** over the 814 commits since the pin the registries of DI, of contributions and of configuration did not change, but the history knows a replacement of an API (`registerWorkbenchContribution` → `registerWorkbenchContribution2`); an adapter turns such a replacement into an edit of one file; a breakage must be loud at compilation, not silent at runtime.

**Considered and rejected:** `if ('x' in service)` and duck typing - a silent degradation; `any` - forbidden by the rules of upstream; copies of upstream classes "for robustness" - a second upstream.

**When to revisit:** when upstream rewrites DI or the model of configuration - a new set of adapters with the API towards the features unchanged. @status:spec/done

**Decision:** a feature is an instance of `Disposable` that the host creates through DI when the flag turns on and disposes when it turns off; one host contribution for all the features, with the phases through `ILifecycleService.when`.

**Why:** this is the life cycle of upstream itself; a base class with `activate()` called from an `autorun` in its own constructor would call a method of the subclass before the parameter properties of that subclass are assigned (they are assigned after `super()`), that is, it would fail on the first feature with injection.

**Considered and rejected:** `abstract class FeatureContribution` with `activate(store)` - a trap of construction order; `queueMicrotask` - it hides the order; `registerWorkbenchContribution2` per feature with a dynamic subclass - parameter decorators are not allowed on a class expression, and the registry accepts only a constructor.

**When to revisit:** if upstream gives the registry of contributions a factory with arguments. @status:spec/done

**Decision:** the state of a flag is an observable; the event remains an adapter.

**Why:** the rule of upstream (the instruction `observables.instructions.md`, `autorun`/`derived` in hundreds of files); `transaction()` gives a snapshot without intermediate states; upstream does not recommend events for control flow.

**Considered and rejected:** `Emitter`/`Event` alone - no transactions and no derivation.

**When to revisit:** when the reactive primitive of upstream changes. @status:spec/done

**Decision:** the remote source gives two layers - the forcing one (a kill switch) above the user and the default one below it; the build outranks them all.

**Why:** a server has two different intents - to switch a broken feature off for everyone, and to set the default of a rollout; upstream has the layer "the default of a setting arrives from the server" (`experiment` in the schema of a setting → `IWorkbenchAssignmentService.getTreatment` → `registerDefaultConfigurations(source: 'experiments')`), which confirms the shape of the default layer; upstream has no forcing layer, other than policy.

**Considered and rejected:** a single remote layer without a mode - it either breaks the choice of the user or cannot switch a feature off.

**When to revisit:** when a real server appears - to decide whether the default layer goes through an own implementation of the upstream assignment service. @status:spec/done

**Decision:** the simulator of the remote source keeps the snapshot in `IStorageService` and is edited by the inspector.

**Why:** it works in desktop and in web, requires no watcher and no file path, and walks the same port as the future server.

**Considered and rejected:** a file under user data with a correlated watcher - absent in web, extra code.

**When to revisit:** if the snapshot has to be replaced from outside the process (then a shared-process channel, as for the server). @status:spec/done

**Decision:** forcing by the build is checked at the evaluation of the module through the static import of the product; the setting is either registered or not.

**Why:** registering the schema of a setting is an action of the module-evaluation moment (the upstream idiom); DI is not available at that moment; at that same moment the upstream `src/main.ts` and `server.main.ts` read the static `product` as well.

**Considered and rejected:** `included: false` - an empty entry in the registry; `configure({ prefix })` before the imports - imports are hoisted and the order is not guaranteed.

**When to revisit:** if upstream stops exporting the static `product`. @status:spec/done

**Decision:** the tests of the library are compiled by the harness and executed in the fork tree.

**Why:** there are no upstream sources in the Codkit repository; stubs would be a second, false upstream.

**Considered and rejected:** vitest with mocks of `vs/*`; building a mini upstream in a fixture.

**When to revisit:** if Codkit gets a polygon with a fork tree in CI. @status:spec/done

**Decision:** the library has no resources and no data outside TypeScript and Markdown.

**Why:** the hygiene of the fork: unknown extensions fall under the checks of indentation and of the header; resources require entries in two allow-lists of the build; `.license` companions are yet another unknown extension; data in TS is the upstream idiom (`codiconsLibrary.ts`).

**Considered and rejected:** `compat.json`/`RUNTIME.toml` for the version - they are not needed, the version is read from the literal.

**When to revisit:** if the library needs a binary resource. @status:spec/done
vscode PROP-008: Generators - the feature skeleton, the brand table, the nls.ts hook

What `codkit gen feature` and `codkit gen brand` write is a template of this type: a class in the shape of a Visual Studio Code contribution with dependency injection through the constructor, a test in the layout the upstream runners find, a brand table hooked into `_format` of `nls.ts`, and the `code-import-patterns` targets the hygiene of the distribution demands. The commands themselves, their flags, the `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS`/`CK-E-GEN-ID` refusals and the rule that the header of a generated file is the product's (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-015#GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-015#GEN-REFUSES-EXISTING`) are the engine's; only the content of the templates comes from here. @status:spec/plan
1. The feature skeleton

`codkit gen feature <id> --title <text> [--setting] [--cold] [--holder <h>] [--license <spdx>] [--year <y>] [--header-style line|block] [--header-file <path>]`: the id has the form of `RT-DESCRIPTOR` (otherwise `CK-E-GEN-ID`, exit 2); the directory of the feature is the last segment of the id; it writes `delta/own/contrib/<name>/common/<name>.ts` (the id constants and, with `--setting`, the id of the setting), `delta/own/contrib/<name>/browser/<name>.contribution.ts` (a class `extends Disposable` with a DI constructor and a `registerFeature({...}, <Class>)` call; with `--cold`, `hotToggle: false`; the description of the setting through `localize`), `delta/own/contrib/<name>/test/browser/<name>.test.ts` (a skeleton with `ensureNoDisposablesAreLeakedInTestSuite`; the test lies in the directory of the feature - `GEN-TEST-LIVES-WITH-THE-FEATURE`); at the end it prints the import line for the composition root of the product and a reminder to declare the unit in `patchset.delta.json`. @status:spec/done

The test of the skeleton lies inside the directory of the feature (`delta/own/contrib/<name>/test/browser/`) and not in a common `delta/own/test/`: a unit of the own manifest owns its own tests, and the declaration of the single unit `delta/own/contrib/<name>` covers both the code and the test; the runners of the fork find it by the glob `vs/<ownDirName>/**/test/browser/**` (PROP-010 `TESTS-LAYER-SPLIT`). The reminder at the end of the command names only that unit. @status:spec/done
2. The brand table and the nls hook

`codkit gen brand [--holder …] [--license …] [--year …] [--header-style line|block] [--header-file <path>]` (the header is as in `gen feature`, `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`) writes `delta/own/common/brand.ts` - a starter table of rules with one example and a comment about the exceptions, exporting `brandMessage = createBrandTransform(RULES)` - and prints the text of the hook for `_format` in `nls.ts` with two reminders: the hook is a patch of the product of type `hook`; the target `src/vs/{monaco.d.ts,nls.ts}` in `code-import-patterns` must permit `vs/<ownDirName>/common/~`. @status:spec/done
vscode PROP-009: Conventions defaults - subsystems, forbidden services
1. Subsystems and the id pattern

The defaults this type contributes to `conventions.json`: the subsystems admitted in an intervention id are `workbench`, `editor`, `platform`, `extensions`, `build`, `product`, `base`, `server`, `test` - the top-level areas of the distribution's own source tree - and the effective `idPattern` is the engine's shape `^CK-(<subsystems joined by |>)-[0-9]{3}$` over that list. The field names, the shape of the pattern, the intervention types, the categories, the layer order and the marker forms are the engine's (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-003#CONV-SUBSYSTEMS`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-003#CONV-ID-PATTERN`); a product extends the list additively through `conventionsExtensionFile` and may not shrink it. @status:spec/done
2. Forbidden service ids

The base `forbiddenServiceIds` protects the bootstrap services that cannot be safely replaced by a late registration. The list is maintained in the installed policy and, at an upgrade, is checked against the actual bootstrap registrations of both the desktop and the web entry of the current pin. @status:spec/done
